C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on transferring GAN directions to diffusion models without finetuning and achieving competitive GAN/diffusion editing. v2 claims a universal, source-agnostic visual-direction framework that overcomes textual description limits and provides superior identity preservation across styles. Reusable zero-shot directions already existed in v1; the substantive expansion concerns source generality, applicability, and comparative positioning.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations contrasting globally pooled CLIP features with spatial denoising predictions, interprets cross-domain transfer as evidence against overfitting, and identifies limitations of global directions and subtle supervision changes. It reverses the timestep interpretation despite retaining the displayed examples. Its new ethics discussion also asserts that observed biases originate entirely in pretrained components.

D1.justification: v2 omits v1's Stable Diffusion v1.5 identifier, learning rate 5e-3, batch size 8, and approximately 30-minute direction-training time, while retaining AdamW, 1000 iterations, L40 hardware, and approximately five-second editing. It adds the NTI+Prompt2Prompt implementation choice, a 60-pair user-study disclosure and example question, and a changed project address. These are documentation changes, not established changes to omitted settings.

E1.justification: v2 adds artistic transformations such as Ukiyoe and Pixar through StyleGAN-NADA supervision, and evaluates attribute transfer to illustrations and paintings (Fig. 3 and appendix Figs. 15–16). These extend the represented domains and editing tasks beyond v1's photographic/generated face and animal examples. FFHQ and AFHQ coverage is retained; real-image editing already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated InstructPix2Pix, Prompt2Prompt, Weights2Weights, IP-Adapter, Attribute-Control, PnP-Diffusion, MasaCtrl, Asyrp, and DiffAE comparisons, and includes W+ Adapter quantitatively. It removes v1's Cycle Diffusion, Diffusion Pullback/NoiseCLR, and StyleCLIP/LatentCLR/SeFa/GANSpace comparisons. SEGA, Concept Sliders, LEDITS++, and qualitative W+ Adapter comparisons were already present, including in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: Default training sample count changes from 100 to 1000. v2 explicitly defaults to full-timestep editing, whereas v1 recommends 0.4T. Evaluation expands beyond LPIPS and CLIP rescoring to DINO, DreamSim, and CLIP/SigLIP similarity metrics, with a new 100-generated-sample comparison and a 200-pair Asian/Smile comparison. The reported user-study participant count changes from 50 to 40; these disclosures do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 retains the qualitative timestep, sample-size, and loss ablations while adding quantitative sample-size/loss results in Table 1. It introduces a DDIM-versus-DDPM inversion ablation in Fig. 6(b), expands composition demonstrations, and adds explicit subtle-edit failure cases in Appendix C/Fig. 11. These add substantial diagnostic evidence beyond the earlier qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly states that all experiments use random seed 0; v2 omits that information. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The omission establishes a reporting change, not an actual change of seeds or run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds quantitative results in Tables 1–3 and new source-transfer, stylized-image, inversion, and failure examples. v1's attribute-specific LPIPS comparison is replaced by a differently scoped comparison reporting ViDiT LPIPS 0.030, so a same-setting gain cannot be inferred. User-study results add InstructPix2Pix 2.06 and Prompt2Prompt 2.74 while removing Cycle Diffusion 2.65. The retained methods' study means and the entire rescoring matrix are unchanged.

M1.justification: The supervision interface is generalized: v1 Algorithm 1 constructs pairs from StyleGAN latent codes and a style-space direction, whereas v2 accepts image-edit pairs from any editing source, demonstrated with StyleGAN-NADA and Prompt2Prompt. The learned conditional embedding, semantic and latent losses, additive guidance, multidirectional composition, and DDPM inversion remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, and the abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around 'Learn Once, Edit Anywhere.' StyleGAN preliminaries are removed, the training algorithm moves from the appendix into the method section, limitations and ethics become separate sections, and the appendix is reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, redraws the overview and framework figures, reorganizes horizontal ablation panels vertically, and adds several quantitative tables and qualitative displays. Earlier GAN/diffusion-direction comparison figures disappear. Several appendix displays are retained and relocated, including v1 Figs. S.11–S.13 becoming v2 Figs. 7–9, rather than constituting new results.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reoriented from GAN latent-space discovery toward visual versus textual conditioning and source-independent transfer. v2 adds substantive discussions of newer conditioning and editing approaches, including IP-Adapter, Weights2Weights, Attribute-Control, InstructPix2Pix, and DiffAE, while removing the dedicated GAN exploration survey and numerous associated citations. The novelty positioning changes beyond bibliographic updates.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the edited-image noising expression from x_i plus noise in v1 to x'_i plus noise in v2, bringing the pseudocode into agreement with the intended paired-image objective. The principal loss and guidance equations remain equivalent, and neither version supplies theorems or proofs. The expanded mechanism discussion is explanatory rather than new theory.

improvement.justification: New supervision sources, multi-metric comparisons, inversion analysis, and explicit failures strengthen the evaluation. However, v2 removes important reproducibility details and reverses the timestep conclusion for retained examples. Its claim of consistently improving LPIPS/DINO with sample size also contradicts Table 1: from N=10 to 100, LPIPS worsens from 0.098 to 0.136 and DINO falls from 0.869 to 0.842. These material reporting problems coexist with substantive benefits, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from GANTASTIC to ViDiT, with matching authors, core objectives, editing equations, and retained results. All pages, including both appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

after.justification: v2 reports original quantitative comparisons and ablations, editing examples from multiple supervision sources, a 40-participant user study, and appendix experiments including failure cases.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing experiments, qualitative ablations, LPIPS comparisons, CLIP rescoring, and a 50-participant user study, with additional experimental results in its appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's random-initialization disclosure does not establish repeated runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 replace the proposed-model BLEU-4 results: Event-CSL 48.70 to 49.80, EvSign 29.41 to 20.20, PHOENIX-2014T-Event 17.53 to 16.48, and CSL-Daily-Event 8.27 to 7.09. GASLT is reclassified from gloss-based to gloss-free, consistent with its cited title.

These support a substantially revised methodological framing rather than merely updated bibliography formatting.

T1.justification: V2 Section 4.2 adds mathematical definitions of noisy motion, conditioned velocity prediction and the residual-field loss in Equations 3–5. These formal additions are localized to the new decoder. Existing R-precision, BAS and F1 definitions are retained in the relocated metrics appendix; neither version develops theorems or proofs.

Appendix A greatly improves implementation documentation, and Appendix F clarifies applicability limits. These gains outweigh the removed repository link and MCM T2M comparison. Unspecified benchmark splits and remaining overstatements, such as the S2G FGD claim despite MCM's better value in Table 9, still limit confidence in some conclusions.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic tests of whether selective attacks remain effective against adversarially trained defenses, reported in main Tables 6–9 and supplementary Tables 3–4. It also expands qualitative case studies across all targeted tasks on both datasets. The radar charts mainly redisplay tabulated results.

Missing numerical loss-ablation rows, ambiguity about the test cap, and the indirect GPHM comparison weaken reporting completeness, but the targeted validation and more explicit failure analysis provide a substantial net improvement.

The abstract and conclusion now emphasize local optical cues and reconstruction with patches as small as the PSF support.

C2.justification: Lens-design interpretation changes from approximately saturating benefits of increased mixing to an optimum followed by degradation from excessive blur. v2 adds interpretations concerning minimum patch size and wider uncertainty under domain shift. Conversely, v1's explicit limitations concerning long-range inconsistency and dependence on spatial texture disappear; runtime limitations remain and receive fuller analysis.

D1.justification: The detailed model-configuration table and core optical simulation specifications remain. v2 newly documents float16 inference and stopping gradients through scale fitting, and revises hardware/time information. It drops explicit flip-augmentation instructions and the direct project-page link, although repository availability is still asserted. Its PSF support is ambiguously described as 32 pixels in the main text and approximately 64 pixels in the supplement.

It adds Harvard evaluation and repurposes CAVE from CASSI training data to held-out filterless reconstruction and real-versus-fake object examples. ARAD1K and ICVL remain, while the high-resolution evaluation now emphasizes cross-dataset generalization without finetuning.

The noise study changes its noise-level sampling, SNR definition, and reported accuracy metric from PSNR to SAM.

It removes the RGB-projection FID analysis and uncertainty-based CASSI pixel-rejection experiment, and revises the noise-robustness comparisons. Patch overlap, rescaling, and saliency analyses largely persist; the shifted-probe saliency analysis was already present in v1's appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions retain uncertainty estimation from ten reconstructions with different noise seeds. However, v1's explicit five-resample count for the noise experiment and its same-seed, deterministic sampling control for saliency are no longer specifically documented. This changes statistical reporting detail without establishing an increase in independent training runs.

The strongest external filterless comparator changes from DGSMP at 30.04 to newly added SST at 31.77. These are revised comparisons under changed reported settings. v2 also replaces finetuned ICVL results with unfinetuned results, adds Harvard/CAVE outcomes, and removes CASSI results.

However, v1 Appendix A.5 uses noise-weighted, TV-regularized guidance for noisy measurements; v2 Supplement Section 6 explicitly uses the standard reconstruction pipeline without that regularizer. This changes the noise-handling extension rather than the central method.

Saliency displays are consolidated, noise plots use different axes and panels, and extensive supplementary reconstruction galleries and CASSI displays are removed.

It distinguishes its large-kernel setting from prior small-kernel, overlapping-patch approaches. It also expands the relationship to Jeon and colleagues' rotating optics and cites the newly evaluated reconstruction baselines.

It also replaces v1's mean-to-noise-standard-deviation SNR definition with a power-based decibel definition.

These provide useful validation beyond v1's finetuned high-resolution demonstration. The net improvement is limited by the removal of explicit texture and long-range failure qualifications, reduced access information, and ambiguity about PSF support underlying the emphasized patch-size claim.

Conversely, v2 explicitly specifies 10 reconstructions with different noise seeds, whereas v3 describes repeated sampling using an unspecified N. An increase in sampling runs is not established.

V2 replaces that novelty claim with scalable enforcement of existing path-specific counterfactual fairness through conditional independence and a connection to standard equalized odds, broadening the claimed scope to high-dimensional modalities.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of baseline over-correction and under-correction, acknowledges omitted exogenous influences, and explains that its sufficient independence constraint can suppress information that PSCF would permit. These materially qualify the causal mechanism and applicability, alongside new interpretations of synthetic and demographic experiments.

It also adds component FLOP costs, synthetic-generation parameters and statements about shared training and tuning controls. V2 adds focused coverage through a synthetic SCM, age-based fairness evaluation across the three datasets, and joint gender-by-age evaluation on MIMIC-CXR (Table 3; Appendices D.2 and D.4).

E4.justification: V2 removes v1's detailed Clue-versus-Dialog diversity analysis and six additional qualitative cases in Figures 6–7, substantially reducing supplementary analysis. E5.justification: Both versions report three experts assessing 50 dialogue samples, with identical Fleiss' Kappa values and rating counts. V2 explains and cites Kappa more fully but adds no uncertainty-estimation procedure, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Principal geolocation, interaction, ablation, and human-rating values remain unchanged; the full OSV-5M table only reduces numerical precision. Supplementary evidence changes substantially through added Im2GPS3k comparator results and removal of GeoCLIP, Im2GPS results, and qualitative outputs. Dataset statistics also change: v1 Figure 3(c) assigns 51k clues to Architecture, whereas v2 Figure 4(b) assigns approximately 51k to Road.

M1.justification: The architecture and projector-pretraining/QLoRA-finetuning procedure remain unchanged. V2 Section IV-C extends the described dialogue-generation pipeline with CoT Introspection: errors exceeding 25 km trigger ground-truth-guided revision of answers. V1's pipeline ended with prediction. CoT Deduction largely restates the existing self-questioning procedure.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, methodology, and dataset explanation; places the model before the dataset; and promotes several appendix evaluations into dedicated main-text subsections. It also changes LVLM terminology to MLLM, revises the author list, and adds biographies.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a journal layout, adds an architecture diagram, radar chart, distribution map, and boxed prompts, and redraws dataset charts. Tables are extensively restyled and relocated, with added evaluation-mode columns. Several appendix figures and the original dataset-example diagram disappear.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens positioning through text/social-network geolocation literature, a dedicated MLLM subsection covering specialized models such as LLaVA-Med and GeoChat, and new prompting, embodied-agent, and numerical-reasoning references. The existing visual-geolocation discussion largely remains.

T1.justification: The visual projection and language-model equations are equivalent reformulations, and the Geoscore definition is unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs. The added correction procedure is methodological, not a new theoretical result.

improvement.justification: V2 improves explanation of data construction and broadens research context, but removes Im2GPS evidence, the Im2GPS3k GeoCLIP comparison, detailed supplementary analyses, and reproducibility information. The principal results remain unchanged, and the added CoT Introspection procedure receives no separate evaluation. These substantive gains and losses leave the net effect on paper quality uncertain.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaGA and MG-Geo. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and included appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

after.justification: V2 retains original geolocation, interaction, ablation, and human-rating results in its main text and appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original geolocation evaluations, interaction experiments, training-stage ablations, human dialogue ratings, and qualitative results.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain MG-Geo, GaGA, and interactive geolocation. v3 broadens the headline performance claim from GWS15k to multiple benchmarks and adds formal investigation of the Similarity Trap to its stated contributions. These extend the existing contribution claims without replacing the paper's central research objective.

C2.justification: v3 substantially develops the interpretation of cue specificity and interaction failures, including the claim that the Similarity Trap is the primary bottleneck. It acknowledges MG-Geo's long-tailed distribution, possible post-hoc rationalization during Introspection, and limits on comparisons using reproduced GWS15k splits. Conversely, v2's explanation of fine-scale coordinate failures through numerical token prediction and its discussion of additional future modalities are removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a dataset access link and describes releases of splits, prompts, generation-path tags, reconstruction scripts, and per-country distributions. It newly specifies eight RTX4090 GPUs, a two-layer projector, and transfer-training details. Most original training hyperparameters remain available in Tables 10–11. Some earlier details disappear, including GPT-4V decoding settings and the GeoReasoner adaptation recipe. These are changes in documented access and reproducibility information; actual online availability was not checked.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on YFCC4k and uses MP16-Pro as an external retrieval corpus. This expands coverage within the existing global image-geolocation task. The OSV-5M and Google Landmarks training sources, GWS15k-style benchmark, OSV-5M-test, Im2GPS3k, and 547-image interactive setting are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership changes substantially. v3 Table 2 replaces the main Qwen-VL row with Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL, adds GLOBE, and adds coordinate comparisons with GeoReasoner and GRE. Table 6 adds ISNs and RFM S2 on OSV-5M-test. Table 9 adds several Im2GPS3k comparators while dropping PlaNet, CPlaNet, and ISNs there. The GPT-4V human dialogue comparison disappears. Hybrid and PIGEOTTO match the earlier OSV-5M-Baseline and PIGEON rows rather than constituting new comparators.

E3.justification: v2's three-expert, 50-sample dialogue assessment disappears. v3 introduces component ablations using Geoscore, clue hit rates, and LLM/MLLM judging, plus a size-matched Introspection-removal protocol and a Qwen3 transfer-training recipe. These are distinct experimental designs. The GWS15k sampling algorithm and original 547-image Direct/+Q/+QA evaluation are substantially retained, with the latter renamed as interaction tiers.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of ambiguous versus high-specificity cues, five dataset-component combinations, Introspection removal at a fixed training-sample budget, and transfer to Qwen3 (Tables 4, 5, 7, and 8). It also adds geographic error analysis and further qualitative cases. The earlier training-stage ablation survives as Table 13; renaming the existing interaction modes does not itself constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: The Fleiss' kappa agreement statistics accompanying v2's expert dialogue ratings (Table V) are removed with that study. v3 supplies no corresponding reliability statistic for its automated judges. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: The principal GaGA GWS15k scores, including 63.06% country accuracy, 6.28% city accuracy, and 3113.0 Geoscore, and the base Im2GPS3k row are retained. v3 adds substantial baseline, YFCC4k, retrieval, ablation, and transfer results; for example, the new retrieval variant reports 37.1% Acc@25km on Im2GPS3k. Human ratings, LLaVA-Llama3's +QA results, and several region-level and OSV distance-threshold entries disappear. Clue-frequency findings also change, with the largest category changing from road in v2 Figure 4 to architecture in v3 Figure 8.

M1.justification: v3 Appendix F introduces GaGA (MP16-Pro), adding retrieval-augmented generation with an external knowledge base. Appendix H also revises the Introspection prompt to require explicit visual-evidence checks and removal of unsupported clues. The base CLIP/Llama3 architecture and two-stage projector/QLoRA training remain substantially unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that existing datasets or experiments were regenerated using the revised prompt.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. The dataset section moves before the model section, while prompts, benchmark construction, and retained analyses move into organized appendices. The standalone discussion and biographies disappear, and the title, author presentation, and section conventions change.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column journal layout to a single-column conference layout. v3 merges the main administrative and coordinate comparisons into Table 2, removes the radar chart, redesigns architecture and curation diagrams, and adds distribution maps and diagnostic displays. Some existing material is relocated, including the benchmark map and training-stage table. New Figure 9 also contains inconsistent ground-truth labels and reported errors.

R1.justification: v3 replaces much of the generic MLLM discussion with a generation-based geolocation survey distinguishing retrieval augmentation from intrinsic reasoning. It adds substantive positioning against Img2Loc, GeoRanker, GLOBE, and GRE, plus a dataset comparison emphasizing expert-guided reasoning and dialogue. Several social/text-geolocation and unrelated domain references disappear. The later G3 citation is a different work from v2's guidebook-grounding G^3.

T1.justification: v3 Section 5.3 introduces the mathematical definition s(c)=1-H(G|c)/H(G) and a salience-weighted condition characterizing a Similarity Trap together with a localization-error threshold. This is a limited formal addition without a theorem or proof. The newly displayed standard training losses largely explicate the retained training procedure.

improvement.justification: The component ablations, size-matched Introspection control, and Qwen3 transfer test strengthen evidence for MG-Geo beyond v2's training-stage comparison. Explicit distribution and benchmark-comparability qualifications also improve transparency. These benefits are partly offset by removing the human dialogue assessment, underspecifying the new automated judges, and introducing inconsistent qualitative evidence: Figure 9 pairs a Denmark ground truth with a Melbourne prediction and a 0.2406 km error. The net improvement is therefore limited.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaGA and MG-Geo, with matching core methods and overlapping experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds dataset-component ablations, Introspection and backbone-transfer experiments, and additional benchmark results.

before.justification: v2 reports original geolocation evaluations, interactive prompting experiments, training-stage ablations, and expert assessments of generated dialogues.

C2.justification: The interpretations of clustering, architecture transfer, timestep choice, resizing and t-SNE results remain unchanged. Discussions of runtime overhead and weak ViT performance with limited samples are also retained.

D1.justification: The reported diffusion settings, cluster-selection rules, preprocessing, PyTorch implementation and NVIDIA RTX-3090 hardware are unchanged. The supplement retains the same implementation and efficiency details, and no code or data access information is added.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same dataset-distillation tasks on CIFAR-10/100, TinyImageNet, ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-100, ImageNette and ImageWoof. No additional dataset, domain or test scenario appears in the supplement.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SRe2L, Minimax, D4M and RDED. Table 2 retains DSA, IDM, TESLA, DATM, D4M, SRe2L and RDED in their corresponding architecture groups. Supplementary comparator membership is also unchanged; the new citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and the supplement retain the same IPC settings, teacher/student architectures, image preprocessing, patch sizes, soft-label evaluation and ablation configurations. Settings moved by pagination are not additions or revisions.

E4.justification: The clustering-feature and image-count ablations are unchanged, as are the supplementary timestep, cluster-count, resizing, cross-architecture and t-SNE analyses. Their questions, configurations and supporting evidence are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five randomly initialized evaluation networks in Section 4.1 and retain the same average and plus/minus reporting. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The matched numerical results and qualitative visualizations are unchanged throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains OursS accuracies of 59.4 ± 0.2 for ResNet-18 and 65.4 ± 0.7 for ResNet-101 on ImageNet-1K at IPC=50. Supplementary results are likewise identical.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 3.2–3.5 retain the same diffusion-based patch selection, DIFT clustering and ranking, IPC-dependent reconstruction, and soft-label calibration. The rewritten preliminaries do not change the proposed procedure.

P1.justification: Sections 2.2 and 3.1 receive localized rewrites, including removal of the brief VAE and latent-diffusion efficiency explanation. The overall section order, method narrative, experimental discussion and supplementary prose are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from the upper-right column to below Figure 3 in the left column on page 5. Subsequent text reflows, and references begin on page 8 rather than page 9. Figure content, captions and table structures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Siglidis et al., Diffusion models as data mining tools, to Section 2.2 and the references. It removes Kingma and Welling's Auto-encoding variational Bayes reference alongside the deleted VAE background passage. The positioning against dataset-distillation methods otherwise remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 2–3 change norm typesetting and explicitly include the subscript 2, retaining the squared-error formulation. The remaining equations and mathematical reasoning are unchanged; no theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

improvement.justification: v2 mainly rewrites background prose, clarifies loss notation, exchanges background citations and adjusts layout. These limited edits preserve the method, experimental evidence, supplementary analyses and reproducibility information. They do not establish a meaningful net improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-driven patch-selection work. Their complete main text and supplementary material, including equations, nine tables and fifteen figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–2 and supplementary efficiency and sensitivity studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification results for distilled datasets, cross-architecture evaluations, ablations and efficiency measurements in the main text and supplement.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: diffusion-guided selection instead of generation, clustering for representative and diverse samples, reusable one-step distillation, and strong large-scale and cross-architecture performance. Retitling and revised wording do not establish a distinct new core claim.

C2.justification: The new hard-label discussion attributes baseline weaknesses to insufficient diversity and image-label misalignment. v2's detailed explanations for patch composition and soft-label calibration, plus some t-SNE interpretations, are shortened or removed. The central diversity–representativeness explanation and small-sample ViT limitation remain.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies interpolation from latent to image resolution and channel averaging before patch scoring. It removes the explicit FKD identification and KL training-objective description while retaining teacher-provided soft labels. Hardware and basic preprocessing remain documented, but the conflicting 0.16/1.60 timestep statements make implementation guidance less consistent.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification using CIFAR-10/100, TinyImageNet, ImageNette, ImageWoof, ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-1K. The added hard-label experiment and 10/20-class timing cases change supervision and subset configurations within retained ImageNet coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 1 adds IGD, D3HR and MGD3. Table 2 replaces D4M with RDED in the ConvNet comparison and RDED with D4M in the ResNet-18 comparison. The new hard-label comparison includes Random, while v2's cross-method ResNet-101 comparison is removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include one-hot-label evaluation at IPC 1/10/50/100 and individual/cumulative timing for 10/20-class ImageNet subsets at IPC 100/200. These replace the earlier per-image timing and GPU-memory comparison at IPC 50. v4 also changes the reported DIFT timestep from 1.60 to 0.16 in Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.1, although Section 4.5 retains 1.60; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a substantive test of dataset quality without teacher soft labels, and Figure 5 tests computational reuse across configurations. Conversely, v2 Table 1's systematic concatenated-versus-single-patch comparison disappears. The t-SNE, timestep, cluster-count and resizing analyses largely persist; their relocation is not an addition.

E5.justification: Both versions specify evaluation using five randomly initialized networks and report averages with ± values in accuracy tables. No new run-count, seed, uncertainty-definition, confidence-interval or significance-testing practice is documented.

E6.justification: Numerous benchmark and ablation entries change. For ImageNet-1K at IPC 50, Table 1 reports 59.4±0.2 for v2 OursS versus 61.0±0.3 for v4 Ours. The ResNet-18-teacher/ViT-B result changes from 69.2 to 63.7. New hard-label results include 10.5±0.3 at IPC 10, below RDED's 11.4±0.4. Timing results are replaced and several sensitivity curves change. These are reporting differences, not established same-procedure performance gains.

M1.justification: The patch-selection, DIFT clustering, ranking and patch-assembly pipeline remains. However, v4 Algorithm 1 and Equations 4–6 replace loss differences L_t with noise-map differences N_t, while the abstract and ablation discussion still describe loss differences. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the procedure or reflects inconsistent notation. Pooling itself was already described in v2.

P1.justification: Beyond the rewritten title and abstract, v4 substantially reorganizes existing material: diffusion preliminaries move into related work, experimental settings move to Appendix A.1, and qualitative and timestep analyses move into the main text. Method subsections are consolidated, and the supplement is reorganized into sections A–C.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and Table 1 is reorganized by model family, removing separate patch-variant and ResNet-101 blocks. v4 adds a timing plot and hard-label table, removes the resource table and two patch illustrations, and relocates/resizes several analyses. The large appendix image grids are retained rather than newly generated evidence.

R1.justification: The discussion is substantially refocused toward model-finetuned and prototype-finetuned diffusion families, adding IGD, MGD3 and D3HR references. The earlier overview of kernel, gradient, feature and trajectory matching is removed, together with several corresponding references. The overarching positioning of selection against diffusion-based generation remains.

T1.justification: v4 revises the formal scoring expressions in Equations 4–6 and explicitly defines the spatial map and patch sum in Equations 6–7. Equivalence to v2's loss-based expressions is unresolved because N_t is separately defined as forward corruption in Equation 1. No theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: Newer baselines, hard-label evaluation and cumulative timing strengthen empirical validation. However, v4 removes direct patch-composition and ResNet-101 baseline comparisons and explicit FKD details, while introducing unresolved scoring and timestep inconsistencies. Reported default results also diverge without explanation: ImageNet-1K IPC-100 accuracy is 63.0 in Table 1 versus 63.4 in Table 5, whereas v2 reports 61.8 in both. These gains and losses in evidence and traceability prevent a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-driven dataset-distillation study. All pages, including equations, tables, plots and image-only appendices, support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

after.justification: v4 reports original classification and ablation results, including additional hard-label evaluations and cumulative synthesis-time measurements.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification results, cross-architecture evaluations, resource measurements and ablations in the main text and supplementary material.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about diffusion-guided selection, reduced distribution mismatch, one-step distillation across configurations, and competitive or superior performance. The added code-access statement does not change the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds an explanation attributing RDED class mixing to classifier errors, extends qualitative criticisms to IGD and MGD3, and discusses concentration becoming harmful at larger IPC. Section 4.6 adds explanations involving early-step fine-grained detail and excessive noise at later steps. These interpretive additions accompany retained experimental evidence.

D1.justification: v5 adds a source-code repository pointer in the abstract, identifies EDC as the source of evaluation hyperparameters, and clarifies the DIFT timestep as 160. Most other implementation information is moved from Appendix A.1 into Section 4.1 rather than newly disclosed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10/100, TinyImageNet, ImageNet-1K and its retained subsets, with the same classification and timing scenarios. No additional dataset, domain, or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: v5 removes DATM from the low-resolution ConvNet comparison in Table 2, although it remains in the qualitative capability summary. The high-resolution comparator set in Table 1 and the hard-label comparators in Table 7 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v5 consistently reports the DIFT timestep as 160, replacing 0.16 in v4's Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.1 and 1.60 in its ablation discussion. This corrects a stated experimental setting; the retained ablation curves do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The clustering, diffusion-timestep, sample-count, cluster-count, resizing, hard-label, and cross-architecture analyses are retained. The t-SNE plots and appendix visualizations also remain unchanged. Figures 6 and 7 exchange numbering and placement without changing their analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five randomly initialized evaluation networks and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practice in numerical tables. No new run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 loses six DATM results, including its CIFAR-10 accuracies of 66.8±0.2 and 76.1±0.3 at IPC 10 and 50. Retained numerical results, including the proposed method's scores and appendix results, remain unchanged. Table 4 additionally lists qualitative capability entries for IGD and MGD3.

M1.justification: The two-stage procedure remains differential-noise patch selection followed by DIFT-based clustering and ranking. No component, objective, or selection procedure is introduced or removed. The corrected DIFT timestep is a reported setting correction, not evidence of a redesigned method.

P1.justification: Experimental settings move from Appendix A.1 to Section 4.1, a baseline-description paragraph is added, and two ablation discussions are reordered. Local prose, author information, keywords, and acknowledgments change, but most scientific narrative remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables throughout the main text and appendices. Table 4 is transposed and expanded, Table 2 loses a column, and Figures 6–7 exchange numbering. Table 2 also newly bolds RDED's CIFAR-10 entries despite higher retained TESLA scores.

R1.justification: v5 adds five references covering video distillation, DD-Ranking, EDC, class-aware conditional mutual information, and rectified decoupled dataset distillation. It also expands baseline descriptions and the capability comparison, while retaining the central positioning against diffusion-based generation.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and their mathematical reasoning are retained. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs, and v5 introduces no new formal assumptions or definitions.

improvement.justification: The code pointer, hyperparameter reference, and timestep correction improve documentation. However, Table 2 removes DATM, the strongest CIFAR-10 comparator in v4, and newly bolds RDED's 50.2/68.4 despite TESLA's higher 66.4/72.6. With the core experiments otherwise retained, the reduced comparison completeness and misleading emphasis outweigh the limited documentation gains.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-driven dataset distillation work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

after.justification: v5 retains original classification results, runtime measurements, cross-architecture evaluations, and main-text and appendix ablations.

before.justification: v4 reports original classification results, teacher–student evaluations, runtime measurements, and ablations, including additional experiments in Appendices A and B.

Its abstract expands PMEB from 15 tasks/14 datasets to 16/15, although Section 3.1 and Table 1's caption retain the old counts.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive arguments that reduced modality gaps demonstrate better alignment, sample-size stability validates the smaller benchmark, and question-only comparisons validate multimodal requirements. It also attributes CONCH's advantages to larger training data and emphasizes data efficiency. These broaden the interpretation substantially, while the earlier prompt-effect interpretation disappears.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies PyTorch, LLaVA-NeXT-8B, an accumulated batch size of 144 and learning rate of 4e-4. It also clarifies composed-retrieval input handling for E5-V and CLIP-based comparators. These extend previously documented implementation details without establishing changes to the underlying training settings.

E1.justification: v2 adds Databiox classification with 922 images in Tables 1 and 3, increasing classification coverage from 12 to 13 tasks. The other evaluation datasets, three task families and training corpora are retained; changes to existing sample counts concern protocol rather than new coverage.

E2.justification: CONCH becomes an evaluated classification comparator in v2 Table 3; v1 discussed it but omitted it from that comparison. PLIP, PathCLIP, QuiltNet and E5-V remain, and the retrieval comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 replaces CONCH-ranked selection of 500 high-scoring, 500 low-scoring and 500 random images with 1,000 category-preserving random samples for large datasets, except Osteo. v2 adds classification accuracy, modality-gap evaluation and comparisons using 1,000, 3,000, 5,000 and all samples. Table 1 also revises Wsss4luad's reported source size from 4,693 to 10,091.

E4.justification: v2 adds t-SNE and quantitative modality-gap analysis in Section 5.4/Figure 4, and benchmark sample-size sensitivity in Section 5.5/Figure 5. v1's prompt and prompt-tuning ablation in Section 5.4.1/Table 4 is absent from the supplied v2. The embedding-fusion ablation remains in Table 5.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports 100 classification trials drawing from 21 templates and displays distributions, medians and quartiles in Figure 4. v2 replaces these with point scores in Table 3 without reporting trial counts, variability or aggregation. This substantially changes statistical reporting, but does not establish that fewer trials were actually performed.

E6.justification: v2 replaces classification distributions with a wF1/accuracy table, adds Databiox and CONCH results, and reports new sample-size and alignment findings. For example, Arch-PubMed modality gaps are 0.9284 for PathCLIP and 0.2587 for MLLM4PUE-P. Prompt-ablation results disappear. Classification changes cannot be interpreted as same-setting gains; retrieval, composed-retrieval and fusion-ablation numerical tables are unchanged after matching renumbering.

M1.justification: The summarization prompts, last-token embeddings, contrastive objective, QLoRA adaptation and zero-shot procedures remain substantively unchanged. v2's explicit LoRA discussion and 8B backbone designation expand documentation rather than establish a changed method.

P1.justification: The title, author list, abstract, introduction and conclusion receive edits. Related-work topics are reversed, and numbered experimental subsections become named paragraphs. These are localized narrative and organizational revisions within the same overall structure; much of the method exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the classification boxplots with a substantial two-metric table, removes the prompt-ablation table, and adds modality-gap and sample-size figures. The radar chart gains Databiox and revised styling, comparison tables gain training-dataset color groups, and existing method displays are relocated. These substantially change how the evidence is presented.

R1.justification: v2 strengthens its differentiation from E5-V by contrasting LoRA adaptation on existing image-text pairs with claimed pathology-instruction pretraining requirements. It adds Liang et al.'s modality-gap work and removes two background references on hierarchical vision transformers and mutation heterogeneity. The central positioning against separate-encoder pathology models remains.

T1.justification: The embedding construction and contrastive-loss equation remain unchanged, with no added assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations. The new modality-gap analysis applies a cited empirical metric without developing new mathematical theory.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence through CONCH comparisons, sample-size checks, modality-gap analysis and additional implementation details. However, it removes the direct prompt-strategy ablation and 100-trial template-variability reporting, leaves classification aggregation unspecified, and introduces inconsistent benchmark counts. These gains and losses affect important aspects of evidential strength, so the supplied PDFs do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.

A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same MLLM4PUE/PMEB study, with reliably matchable methods, equations, experiments and displays. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF includes an appendix or the separately referenced supplementary materials.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds classification comparisons, modality-gap measurements and sample-size analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, classification and composed-retrieval experiments, plus prompt and embedding-fusion ablations.

The abstract, introduction and conclusion now emphasize interleaved modalities, task/domain mismatch and retrieval as a clinical computational consult.

C2.justification: v2 emphasizes data efficiency, modality alignment and the adequacy of sampled evaluation. v3 introduces stronger explanations based on morphology-first learning and claims that every adaptation component is essential. It attributes CONCH's Pubmedset advantage to likely training/test overlap without reporting an overlap audit, and identifies genomics integration as future work.

D1.justification: v3 documents stage-specific corpus sizes, trained modules, batch sizes of 576/384, learning rates of 4e-5/1e-4, two-epoch schedules and eight H100 GPUs instead of six. Earlier QLoRA, checkpointing, DeepSpeed and temperature disclosures are no longer stated. The new filtering threshold remains unspecified, and referenced benchmark-construction prompts are unavailable.

DigestPath's two classification tasks and Wsss4luad disappear. Training adds MedNLI/MedMCQA text pairs and PathGen-1.6M. Bookset/Pubmedset retain the cited sources of Arch-book/Arch-PubMed; those name changes alone are not new coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained E5-V, PLIP, PathCLIP and QuiltNet, v3 evaluates PubmedCLIP, BiomedCLIP, Pathgen-CLIP variants, Patho-CLIP variants, MUSK, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LamRA and GME. CONCH expands from classification-only comparison in v2 to retrieval comparisons. Conversely, QuiltNet is no longer included in the fusion ablation.

E3.justification: Evaluation sizes change substantially: LCcolon increases from 1,000 to 10,000 samples, and Bookset from 1,306 to 2,688. Retrieval reporting changes from R@5/10/50 to R@1/5/10; classification changes from wF1 and accuracy to an undefined 'weighted accuracy.' Training budgets and input processing change, GPT-5 replaces the earlier ChatGPT cleaning description, and explicit training-data-matched comparisons are no longer provided.

E4.justification: v3 adds filtering, curriculum, stain-processing and resolution ablations, plus qualitative retrieval cases. Fusion analysis covers additional query types but removes question-only controls. The modality-gap study changes from t-SNE on Arch datasets against PathCLIP to UMAP on Educontent against several baselines. v2's sample-size robustness analysis is absent from the supplied v3.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. v3's bootstrap procedure filters training data; it does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. v2 Table 4 reports MLLM4PUE-Q R@5 of 47.5%/67.5% on Quilt-VQA/RED; v3 Table 2 reports HOMIE at 67.1%/87.7%. These involve changed models, training and answer processing, not controlled same-setting gains. Newly reported results include 78.5% multi-image-to-text and 30.7% video-to-text R@1.

M1.justification: HOMIE substantially revises MLLM4PUE: LLaVA-NeXT-8B with fixed-resolution inputs becomes Qwen2.5-VL-7B with native-resolution processing. v3 adds text-only retrieval adaptation, subsequent pathology tuning, a morphology-to-diagnosis curriculum, bootstrap filtering and stain normalization/augmentation. These change the procedure beyond renaming or expanded explanation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around HOMIE/PCR. Results move into the experiments section, composed retrieval becomes the leading evaluation, and the separate zero-shot-transfer explanation is replaced by architecture, adaptation and training-objective sections. This exceeds terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: v3 adds a clinical-retrieval workflow to Figure 1, redraws the architecture overview, introduces qualitative examples and replaces the modality-gap plots. Results tables are reordered and substantially restructured; the sample-size chart disappears and component-ablation displays are added. Figure 4 also introduces a caption/legend disagreement over image/text colors.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to MUSK, Pathgen/Patho-CLIP, VLM2Vec, LamRA and GME, positioning HOMIE against both pathology encoders and general multimodal retrievers. The introduction replaces much of the broad diagnostic-task motivation with literature on retrieval, interpretability, hallucination and clinician decision support.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 1 explicitly sums image-to-text and text-to-image contrastive terms. v3 Section 3.4 instead displays a batch-averaged query-to-candidate objective without a reverse term. Section 3.1 also formalizes the broader PCR input/candidate definition, including videos and interleaved inputs. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical support for composed retrieval through distinct multi-image/video tests, more competitive baselines and component controls (Tables 2–6), addressing v2's narrow composed-query validation. The gain is tempered by losing training-data-matched comparisons, incomplete reproducibility details and overstated interpretations: the stain ablation changes composed R@1 only from 53.2 to 53.1, and CONCH overlap is unverified. Nevertheless, the stronger testing of capabilities and design choices constitutes a substantial overall improvement.

A1.justification: These are identifiable versions of the same pathology-embedding work despite extensive revision and renaming. All supplied pages, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Neither PDF contains appendices; both reference separate supplementary material that is unavailable here.

after.justification: v3 Tables 2–6 and Figures 3–4 report original composed retrieval, simple retrieval, classification, qualitative and component-ablation results.

before.justification: v2 Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–5 report original retrieval, classification, embedding-alignment and ablation results.

Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: v4 elevates adaptation of any generative MLLM and a lightweight 2B model outperforming specialized 7B models into central claims. It explicitly organizes the contribution around architectural, task and domain mismatches. v3 emphasizes the public-data, two-stage omni-modal system without equivalent backbone-generality or parameter-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of domain-prior synergy, model scaling and learned prompt robustness. Appendix B introduces limitations concerning real clinical queries, modality coverage and deployment resources. The Pubmedset-overlap explanation and classification-transfer interpretation disappear. Its claimed consistent scaling is qualified by Table 4, where some scores decrease from 2B to 8B.

D1.justification: v4 supplies the filtering threshold 0.1, LoRA ranks and scaling factors, scheduler and warmup, BF16, FlashAttention-2 and DeepSpeed settings. Appendices add inference prompts, dataset-selection details, exact curation prompts and deployment memory/latency information. A project-page link is added; the PDFs alone do not verify its resources.

E1.justification: v4 adds the full NLI corpus to training and removes Pubmedset retrieval and all nine tile-classification datasets from reported evaluation. The composed tasks and remaining simple-retrieval datasets retain their coverage and sample counts. Appendix C describes classification inference but does not restore classification evaluations.

E2.justification: v4 Tables 2–3 add Qwen3-VL-2B, Qwen3-VL-8B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Lingshu-7B and PathoR1-7B. Table 2 also evaluates reciprocal rank fusion for all eleven dual-encoder baselines alongside retained vector addition. E5-V, LamRA and GME remain the same comparators despite added size suffixes.

E3.justification: The reported stage-one learning rate changes from 4e-5 to 2e-4. Main evaluations shift from Qwen2.5-VL-7B to Qwen3-VL-2B/8B, with additional backbone configurations and inference-prompt controls. GPT-5 curation is redescribed as strict extraction/formatting, although Appendix E retains generation language; benchmark regeneration is not established.

E4.justification: v4 adds six-backbone generality tests and No Prompt/No One Word robustness ablations. Component ablations now report task-specific retrieval results on Qwen3-VL-8B rather than composed/simple/classification averages. v3's separate simple-add versus prompt-guided fusion ablation disappears. The qualitative examples and modality-gap analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The bootstrap procedure concerns data filtering, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main HOMIE results are replaced: multi-image Bookset R@1 is 78.5 in v3, versus 75.2 and 79.8 for v4's Qwen3 2B and 8B variants. These are different configurations, not demonstrated same-setting gains. v4 adds extensive comparator, backbone and ablation results and removes Pubmedset, classification and fusion-ablation results. Shared baseline rows and modality-gap values remain unchanged.

M1.justification: The reported visual backbone changes from the Qwen2.5-associated ViT with window attention in v3 Section 3.2 to SigLIP-2 in v4 Section 3.3. The central two-stage adaptation, InfoNCE objective, filtering, curriculum, stain processing and EOL embedding extraction remain. Expanded video and prompt descriptions largely document existing capabilities.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental discussion and conclusion are substantially rewritten around model generality and three mismatches. v4 adds an existing-model analysis subsection and five supplementary sections, merges qualitative and embedding-visualization discussion, and changes the title terminology from omni-modal to multi-modal.

P2.justification: v4 switches to a single-column layout, replaces the opening radar presentation with a mismatch-analysis figure, and moves a revised clinical-workflow graphic to the appendix. The qualitative and UMAP figures are merged. Comparison and ablation tables are substantially restructured, a backbone table is added, and curation prompts become figures.

R1.justification: The related-work section largely retains its pathology dual-encoder versus general embedding framing. v4 adds references supporting Qwen3, SigLIP-2, positional encoding, EOL, NLI training and medical MLLMs, while removing classification-dataset and some contextual references. Positioning now more explicitly addresses specialized generative medical models.

T1.justification: The PCR similarity-ranking formulation and InfoNCE mathematics remain substantively unchanged. Neither version introduces theorems or proofs. v4's causal-attention and EOL discussion adds conceptual explanation rather than new formal results.

improvement.justification: The added RRF and pathology-MLLM controls, backbone tests, prompt ablations and reproducibility details strengthen support for the central PCR framework beyond v3. The net gain is limited by removal of Pubmedset, where CONCH led, and classification evidence. Reporting also needs correction: v4 gives the 2B Quilt-VQA R@1 as 34.4 in Table 2 but 33.4 in Table 4, and its uniform-scaling interpretation overstates the results.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HOMIE/PCR work and are readable, including figures, tables and equations. The supplied v3 ends after its references; v4 includes supplementary Appendices A–E. The format and title changes do not prevent reliable comparison.

after.justification: v4 reports original retrieval comparisons, evaluations across six adapted backbones, component and prompt ablations, and qualitative embedding analyses.

before.justification: v3 reports original composed-retrieval, simple-retrieval and tile-classification results, component and fusion ablations, and embedding-space analyses.

C1.justification: The core bilevel formulation, computational-complexity, convergence and benchmark-performance claims persist. V2 extends the introduction's contributions with claims about reduced gradient conflict, superiority to weight-swept LS and the importance of dynamic training trajectories.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the mechanism discussion: losses need not become equal, changing training trajectories matters despite nearly uniform final weights, LS can favor easier tasks, and comparable loss scales may explain insensitivity to task ordering. V1's discussion of poor QM9 performance with τ=1 disappears alongside that result.

D1.justification: V2 newly identifies one NVIDIA A6000 GPU, describes the router's shared-feature input and tabulates selected step sizes, penalty constants and τ choices for each dataset. V1's explicit coarse-to-fine grid-search recipe is omitted. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic two-task example, CelebA's 40 attributes, QM9's 11 properties, Cityscapes' two tasks and NYU-v2's three tasks. Added diagnostics and controls retain these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator rosters are unchanged; MoCo already appears in v1 Tables 1 and 4. V2 adds LS to the QM9 loss-trajectory comparison (v1 Figure 3 versus v2 Figure 6) and to new loss/gradient diagnostics. Weight sweeping further evaluates the existing LS method.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluation design with LS-weight and penalty sweeps, normalization-by-LDC component controls, shuffled-loss testing and gradient comparisons on eight sampled CelebA tasks after epoch 15. Core splits and training budgets remain. The reported Δm sign convention is corrected. V2 Table 6 lists NYU-v2's step size as 8e-5, whereas both setup passages state 1e-4; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: V1's detailed normalization-alternative grid is replaced by normalization/LDC component ablations on QM9 and NYU-v2. V2 additionally investigates penalty sensitivity, loss ordering, loss distributions, gradient conflicts, weight trajectories and trade-offs against weight-swept LS. The existing small-gradient diagnostic is retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages. V2 newly supplies standard deviations for the proposed method's aggregate results across all four benchmarks and for several additional controls (Tables 6–11), without reporting an increased run count. Most baseline and task-specific results remain mean-only.

E6.justification: Retained best Δm scores remain unchanged: Cityscapes -0.57, CelebA -1.31, QM9 49.5 and NYU-v2 -4.40. V2 adds substantial diagnostic and controlled-experiment results, including CelebA loss means of 0.1888 versus LS's 0.2872 and task-reordering results of -1.28 versus -1.31. Alternative-τ rows and the old normalization grid are removed, including QM9's τ=1 result of 113.6.

M1.justification: The bilevel objectives, penalty formulation and updates in Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. V1's 'identical normalization' becomes 'no normalization' in v2 Appendix A.1; this and the method renaming do not establish a procedural change.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the title and method, v2 rewrites the introduction around loss discrepancy, reorganizes Section 5 into results and analysis, moves experimental setup into Appendix A.1 and substantially restructures Appendix A. Terminology changes throughout, and the impact statement is removed.

P2.justification: V2 adds loss-distribution plots, gradient heatmaps, trade-off scatter plots, weight trajectories and several analysis tables. Earlier loss/gradient figures move to the appendix, with an LS panel added to the loss plot. Main benchmark tables are consolidated, detailed QM9 results move to the appendix, and algorithms receive new boxed layouts.

R1.justification: V2 adds engagement with Kurin et al. and Xin et al. concerning strong scalarization baselines, plus citations to Bayesian gradient aggregation, gap balancing and the evaluation metric. It removes the generalized-smoothness discussion and citation to Qi Zhang et al. The broader MTL/bilevel positioning remains.

T1.justification: The main convergence framework and proofs remain, including the O(epsilon^-2) rate in Appendix C despite its removal from theorem statements. Local edits correct the Δm sign definition, explicitly use the lower-level gradient in the PL assumption and change T=Omega(epsilon^-2) to T=O(epsilon^-2). V2 also introduces an inconsistent Phi=gradient(f)+lambda gradient(g) expression where v1 used Phi=f+lambda g.

improvement.justification: Weight-swept LS controls, component/order/sensitivity tests, standard deviations and selected hyperparameters strengthen the empirical support and reproducibility of the retained findings. The gain is tempered by removed alternative-τ and normalization comparisons and new inconsistencies: NYU-v2's learning rate and normalization labels disagree across Appendix A.1 and Tables 5–6, while Appendix C inconsistently redefines Phi. Overall, the added evidence provides a limited net quality improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from BiLB4MTL to LDC-MTL. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support reliable matching and comparison.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds loss/gradient diagnostics, sensitivity tests, component ablations and task-order experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on a synthetic example and four MTL benchmarks, including accuracy, runtime and normalization-ablation results.
