Freqformer's UHDM PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS change from 22.22/0.8018/0.2434 to 22.24/0.8021/0.2424; FHDMi scores remain unchanged. Haar PSNR changes from 13.32 to 23.01, and Table 6 scores and timings are replaced without establishing identical conditions. Section 3.2's high-frequency resizing PSNR changes from approximately 30 to 25 dB. Section 4.1 adds 0.58 versus 0.25 s/image for Freqformer versus ESDNet-L and revises Freqformer's computation from 2.49 to 2.46 TFLOPs.

M1.justification: The decomposition kernel, dual branches, SA-CA, hierarchical fusion, learnable FCT and two-stage losses remain unchanged. The explicit description of resized low-frequency inference resolves an inconsistent overview in v1; v1 Section 3.2 already specified small inputs during both training and inference.

P1.justification: The section sequence and much of the method exposition remain, with localized rewrites, clearer inference wording and reordered ablation discussion. The title changes 'Efficient' to 'Effective,' asymmetric training terminology becomes more prominent, author/affiliation information changes, and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different template with narrower text, running headers and substantially reorganized displays. New Figures 3 and 7 illustrate transform differences and ablation outputs. Tables 1, 2 and 6 expand; the old branch-comparison table disappears. Ablation tables move from text-wrapped placements to full-width blocks, and qualitative comparisons replace a UHDM example and introduce RRID panels.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 broadens from wavelet-based to frequency-based methods, adding DCT positioning against MBCNN and FHDe2Net and revising the critique of FHDe2Net. STD-Net and generative-restoration references are added. The existing research lineage and principal novelty positioning remain.

T1.justification: The mathematical method and losses are retained. The added equality expressing the high-frequency residual as the original image minus its low-frequency component restates the existing recurrence. No substantive new formal assumptions, theorems or proofs appear.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central design: the expanded Haar/DCT study and new SCP/DAT controls test choices that v1 supported only narrowly. Distinct additional datasets and comparator families strengthen the generality assessment, while measured latency makes the efficiency discussion more candid. These gains outweigh the removed branch comparison, omitted learning rate and less definite code-release statement. Unexplained changes to existing ablation scores and timings remain a reproducibility limitation.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Freqformer and are readable through their final references. Text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

after.justification: Sections 4–4.2 report original results on four datasets, additional comparator evaluations and expanded transform and architecture ablations.

before.justification: Sections 4–4.2 report original FHDMi/UHDM restoration results and experiments testing training strategies, frequency decomposition and architectural components.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central method, dataset and contour-evaluation contributions remain. V2 additionally presents release of the dataset and annotation pipeline as reusable research tools in its contribution list; v1 described their construction without this release claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of sequential-generation latency and expands tokenizer and spatial-attention interpretations, including a stronger claim that the retained heatmap demonstrates reconstructed 2D topology. Its new assertion of superiority across all semantic benchmarks is broader than Table 1 supports: the best listed LlamaSeg PC-59 score is 63.8 versus Unified-IO-XL's 64.0.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code/dataset access link and clarifies downstream controls for Table 6. Conversely, it omits v1's 20-pixel mask dilation, explicit contour RGB values and single-instance generation/verification rules. These are documentation changes, not demonstrated changes to implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same SA-OVRS, semantic and referring training data and the same semantic, open-vocabulary and referring evaluation benchmarks. The new label visualization and efficiency comparison do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds an efficiency comparison against LAVT and Unified-IO2-Large in Table 7. Although both methods already appeared elsewhere, this comparison is new; comparator membership in Tables 1–3 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation using latency, FPS and peak memory. Existing training budgets, model configurations and IoU/mAHD evaluation protocols are retained. Hardware, batch size and test inputs for the new timing comparison are not specified.

E4.justification: V2 adds inference-efficiency analysis and a descriptive visualization of SA-OVRS label abundance in Figure 4. The tokenizer, decoding and training-data ablations and the spatial-attention example already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new efficiency results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical scores. New Table 7 reports LlamaSeg-B at 3949.92 ms, 0.250 FPS and 3.69 GB, versus latencies of 35.89 ms for LAVT and 57906.23 ms for Unified-IO2-Large. These are additional efficiency results, not across-version segmentation gains.

M1.justification: The VQGAN mask tokenizer, LLaMA autoregressive generator, mask-token cross-entropy objective, SigLIP2 inputs and Janus-Pro adaptation remain unchanged. The annotation pipeline is condensed without establishing a procedural change.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the abstract, introduction, related work, dataset construction, result discussion and conclusion are rewritten. Contributions are consolidated, experimental settings gain separate subheadings, sections are renamed, and author notes and acknowledgments change.

P2.justification: V2 changes the page design, redraws Figures 1–3, reorganizes qualitative and reconstruction panels, and adds extensive table highlighting and resolution-gain annotations. It adds the label word cloud and efficiency table. Some new highlighting is misleading: Table 2 marks 47.4 on RefCOCO+ testA while leaving the higher 51.6 unmarked.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including HiMTok, ArGenSeg, Seg-VAR and run-length segmentation tokenization, while removing works including All in Tokens and Polyformer. Positioning against specialist segmentation pipelines and Unified-IO remains substantially the same; newly cited methods are not added to the accuracy comparisons.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same nearest-code quantization, mask reconstruction/binarization and average Hausdorff distance definitions. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

improvement.justification: The efficiency comparison and resource link add useful practical information, but the timing protocol remains underspecified. V2 also removes concrete annotation instructions and strengthens interpretations beyond the unchanged evidence, including the all-benchmarks claim contradicted by Table 1. These benefits and harms leave the net quality direction uncertain despite the extensive presentation revision.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LlamaSeg, and their readable text, equations, figures and tables support reliable matching. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds latency, throughput and memory measurements in Table 7.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation evaluations, mask-reconstruction experiments, decoding comparisons and training-data ablations in Tables 1–6.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims a unified staged-to-wild benchmark and identifies differences between frozen representations. v2 makes controlled synthetic data a central contribution and claims synthetic training can match or surpass staged training on wild transfer. The abstract and conclusion also expand the benchmark claim to three domains, 16 classes and privacy-amenable data generation.

C2.justification: v1 explains transfer through I3D's simpler motion representations and transformer overfitting. v2 emphasizes demographic/environmental diversity, synthetic appearance versus staged motion, and differences in recovery coverage. Its limitations newly discuss generator-induced biases and incomplete synthetic realism, extending the retained concerns about wild coverage and deployment privacy.

D1.justification: v2 documents generation prompts and attributes, annotation tooling and review, source permissions, feature extraction, four H100 GPUs and extraction time. Some precise v1 classifier and loss details disappear. Access wording changes from direct dataset/code links to a project page and an Appendix A.5 release-on-acceptance statement; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

E1.justification: The eight staged datasets and OOPS-derived wild corpus are retained under revised names. v2 adds 12,000 synthetic videos with demographic and environmental variation, expands the taxonomy from 10 to 16 classes, reports full-taxonomy wild evaluation beyond v1's binary wild labels, and evaluates cross-age and cross-BMI scenarios.

E2.justification: v1's classification comparison among I3D, VideoMAE-Pre and VideoMAE-K400 is replaced by VideoMAE-K400 training-source comparisons. SigLIP2 enters the feature comparisons, ASQuery replaces MS-TCN++ for supervised segmentation, and Appendix Table 8 adds evaluated TW-FINCH and KMeans baselines.

E3.justification: The staged CS/CV partitions are retained in Appendix A.2. Reported classification settings change from 150 epochs, batch size 256 and learning rate 5e-4 to 50 epochs, batch size 32 and 1e-5. v2 adds single-source, synthetic and combined-source controls and demographic protocols; embedding smoothing changes from 18-feature averages to five-frame means.

E4.justification: v2 adds training-source ablations, cross-age/BMI robustness tests in Figure 7, and temporal trajectory and recovery-completeness analyses in Appendix A.5.1 and Figure 8. Existing domain-shift analyses incorporate synthetic data and SigLIP2. Conversely, v1's qualitative segmentation prediction example becomes an annotation-only illustration in v2 Figure 3.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3.5 newly documents deterministic, hash-based seeding for synthetic attribute selection. This is limited seed information, not evidence of repeated experimental runs. Neither supplied PDF reports confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run variability for the benchmark scores.

E6.justification: v1 reports wild Fall F1 of 0.76/0.82 for I3D and 0.34/0.26 for VideoMAE-K400 under CS/CV training. v2 replaces these comparisons with scores of 52.3% for CMDFall training, 61.2%/60.5% for OF-Staged, 64.2% for synthetic and 65.6% for combined training. These are different experimental conditions, not same-setting improvements. New segmentation, demographic and temporal-analysis results further expand the evidence.

M1.justification: v2 introduces controlled Wan 2.2 synthetic-video generation and reports end-to-end VideoMAE-K400 classification, replacing v1's frozen-backbone approach. Supervised segmentation changes from MS-TCN++ to ASQuery. However, v2's end-to-end description is not clearly reconciled with Appendix A.5's classifier operating on extracted features.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around three domains. Experiments are reorganized around training sources, and dataset splits, search details and limitations move into a substantial appendix. This changes the narrative and document organization beyond simply inserting new results.

P2.justification: v2 changes the single-column layout to two columns, introduces a three-domain overview, redraws distribution and embedding plots, and reorganizes result tables with colored rankings. It adds demographic and trajectory figures and appendix tables. Figures 9–20 enlarge the existing embedding analysis rather than constituting separate experiments.

R1.justification: The review of existing fall datasets remains largely intact. v2 adds references supporting Wan, SigLIP2, ASQuery, VIA and demographic attribute design, while removing the class-balanced-loss and MS-TCN references. These are targeted additions supporting the expanded benchmark rather than a comprehensive restructuring of the prior-work landscape.

T1.justification: v1 Section 4.2 explicitly defines capped dataset weights as w_i = min(max_j |D_j| / |D_i|, 20); v2 omits this mathematical specification. Neither version develops theorems or proofs, so the change is limited to removal of a formal training rule.

improvement.justification: Shared 16-class wild timelines, direct training-source controls and demographic/recovery analyses substantially strengthen the benchmark's ability to investigate generalization beyond v1's backbone-focused evaluation. Generation and annotation documentation makes the expanded benchmark more auditable. These gains outweigh reduced classifier-backbone coverage, although implementation and access descriptions remain unclear. v2 also overstates universal SigLIP2 superiority: Table 6 gives staged-to-wild F1@50 of 20.26 for SigLIP2 versus 26.37 for I3D. The improvement rests on stronger benchmark design and evidence, not cross-version performance gains.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniFall, and their supplied pages, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 references supplementary backbone settings, a VideoMAE-Pre table and numerical distance tables that are not included in its PDF. v2 includes Appendix A. This limits comparison of those supplementary details, while the principal revisions are directly assessable.

after.justification: v2 reports original training-source comparisons, demographic generalization tests, supervised and unsupervised segmentation results, and temporal-completeness analyses in the main text and appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original domain-shift analyses, backbone classification experiments in Tables 2–3, and MS-TCN++ segmentation results in Table 4.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes synthetic-versus-staged transfer and feature-dependent domain complementarity. v3 retains the benchmark contributions but makes the fine-tuned-versus-zero-shot fall/fallen distinction central in its abstract, introduction, and conclusion. It newly argues that fallen recognition requires task-specific training and identifies it as the principal clinical bottleneck, while dropping the earlier feature-dependent qualification of segmentation transfer.

C2.justification: v3 attributes synthetic training's fallen-state benefits to extended post-fall ground contact and interprets MLLM confusion through temporal reasoning, missed clinical alerts, and deployment cost. The earlier I3D-specific transfer explanation is removed. Limitations become more specific: OF-ItW overrepresents spectacular accidents relative to elderly-care falls, and synthetic generation has ethnicity-taxonomy and binary-gender constraints.

D1.justification: v3 adds precise class definitions, temporal-boundary conventions, and detailed MLLM prompts, preprocessing, decoding, and response parsing. It adds a direct dataset pointer and supplementary-browser instructions. Conversely, it removes v2's classifier optimizer and training-budget description, multi-view annotation-transfer procedure, deterministic generation-attribute assignment, and extraction-time estimate. The appendix still promises release upon acceptance, so the new access pointer does not establish availability.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same eight staged datasets, 818 in-the-wild videos, and 12,000 synthetic videos, with the same classification and timeline-segmentation tasks. New model comparisons and in-the-wild training use existing coverage. The pooled Fall/Fallen score changes evaluation reporting rather than introducing new data or input scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 introduces Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 zero-shot comparisons, including 2B, 4B, and 8B variants, plus Keye-VL-1.5-8B in Appendix A.7. Conversely, ASQuery with I3D features disappears from the segmentation comparison, leaving SigLIP2 results. TW-FINCH and KMeans are retained in the appendix, not removed.

E3.justification: v3 adds individual-dataset training comparisons, a combined staged/synthetic/wild training configuration, and pooled Fall-or-Fallen evaluation. New MLLM experiments introduce 16-frame, 448-pixel-square inputs and model-size and prompt-selection protocols, including selection informed by OF-ItW ablations. Existing CS/CV and demographic split definitions remain substantially unchanged; these additions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds model-scale tests, detailed prompt-format/component/location ablations, and fallen-versus-lying confusion analysis (Figure 7 and Tables 7–10). It removes v2's temporal-trajectory and episode-completeness analysis, eight-class radar analysis, and I3D-versus-SigLIP2 segmentation comparison. Cross-age and cross-BMI tests are retained and moved to the appendix.

E5.justification: Appendix A.7 newly specifies inference seed 0 and fixed-seed temporal sampling for MLLM evaluation. Neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. This is added seed disclosure, not evidence of increased replication.

E6.justification: v3 Table 4 adds OF-ItW Fall/Fallen F1 scores of 67.8/29.2 for Qwen3-VL-8B and 68.0/31.0 for InternVL3.5-8B. The newly wild-trained VMAE configuration reports 76.0/53.6 under different training conditions. Extensive prompt, scale, and per-dataset results are added, while I3D segmentation, temporal-chain, and some CV-to-wild/synthetic entries disappear. Retained VMAE classification and SigLIP2 segmentation scores largely match v2.

M1.justification: No substantive change to the proposed benchmark-construction method is established. Wan2.2 generation and the 16-class annotation scheme remain; expression conditioning and separate fallen-state examples already appear in v2's appendix. Added MLLMs are comparison baselines, while expanded annotation rules and removed classifier descriptions change documentation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset rationale, experimental discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. v3 adds a main-text synthetic-data risks section and an appendix roadmap, reorganizes annotation and experimental documentation, and moves cross-view and demographic discussions into the appendix. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond added experiments alone.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column format with a single-column layout and rebuilds classification tables around test datasets, adding model rows, pooled detection columns, and OOD shading. It adds expression-conditioning and confusion figures plus definition and ablation tables, while removing radar, trajectory, and PRISMA-checklist displays. The demographic plot and twelve full-size embedding plots remain, with relocation and presentation edits.

R1.justification: The paper substantially expands its positioning from dataset unification and synthetic transfer to evaluating pretrained generalist MLLMs against smaller specialized models. Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5, Keye-VL, and vLLM/PagedAttention references support this new framing; an additional multi-camera fall-detection work is also cited. Much of the original dataset literature review remains.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. v3's class definitions clarify the existing annotation taxonomy; its pooled detection reporting is an evaluation addition rather than a mathematical extension.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful baselines, diagnostic ablations, an in-domain reference, and clearer annotation definitions. However, its new claim that fallen recognition requires task-specific training is not consistently supported: a zero-shot Qwen prompt variant reaches 45.4 Fallen F1 in Table 10, exceeding synthetic-trained VMAE's 42.3 in Table 4, with tradeoffs on other metrics. v3 also removes training details and v2's I3D results that qualified synthetic-data superiority. The expanded evidence improves usefulness, but unresolved central interpretations and lost documentation prevent a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniFall benchmark. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, added, and removed content to be matched reliably.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds zero-shot MLLM comparisons, prompt ablations, and an experiment incorporating in-the-wild training data.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, supervised and unsupervised segmentation, domain-distance, and demographic-transfer results in Section 4 and Appendix A.5.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The instance-first thesis remains, but v2 broadens the central contribution to attribute binding and both text-to-image and layout-to-image control. Its abstract, introduction and conclusion foreground three-benchmark validation, superiority over count-supervised approaches and IntraCompBench as a named contribution. v1 principally emphasized improved class/instance generation and the reported 52%/83% accuracies.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of CountGen's mask proposals, failures of exclusive box masking, image-quality tradeoffs and seed stability. It also identifies ambiguous parsed counts and missing 3D understanding as applicability limits. The runtime limitation remains, while v1's argument that normalization prevents transferring several baselines and its proposed SDXL-Turbo extension are removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents GPT-OSS-20B prompt parsing through instructions, examples and approximate cost, specifies normalized coordinates and bilinear attention upsampling, and identifies the reused layout annotations. This substantially expands implementation information beyond v1's assumed class/count inputs. However, v1's blanket single-A100-80GB experimental hardware statement is no longer provided. Both versions still promise code upon publication.

E1.justification: v2 adds HRS-Bench evaluations, color/texture/complex-composition tasks from T2I-CompBench, and layout-conditioned generation with overlapping boxes. These extend v1's counting-focused coverage substantially. IntraCompBench retains the earlier COCO-derived benchmark's classes and prompt construction; its new name does not establish new coverage. T2I-CompBench Numeracy also already appeared in v1 as T2I-CompBench++ Numeracy.

E2.justification: v2 adds Self-Cross to SD1.5 and SD3.5-M comparisons and evaluates A&E, SynGen, InitNO and TEBOpt against ISAC on SD3.5-M, where v1 lacked those comparisons. CountGen is newly evaluated on SDXL, while GLIGEN and CAR&SAR support the new layout comparison. Bounded Attention receives qualitative comparisons. Counting Guidance and the TokenCompose/IterComp comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include reuse of released HRS-Bench box layouts, best-of-10 selection on Flux.1-dev and Qwen-Image, and FID/CMMD measurements against native SDXL outputs. Original COCO sampling and detector-ensemble procedures remain. However, v2 Section 4.1 describes exact-count/all-class success while Appendix A.2 retains fractional detection accuracy, leaving any actual change to that scoring procedure unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds a semantic-overlap heatmap, CountGen-combination analysis, distributional image-quality evaluation, attention-layer ablation and a transparent-object failure case (Figure 2, Tables 10/13/14 and Figure 15). Earlier schedule, MPO and clustering ablations remain. Conversely, v1's separate propagation/normalization diagnostics and SDXL-Turbo dynamics analysis are removed, rather than merely relocated.

E5.justification: v1 reports multiple images and qualitative seed examples but provides no uncertainty estimates for its Numeracy table. v2 Appendix C.4 and Table 16 newly report 30 seeds and means with standard deviations for SD1.5/SDXL Numeracy results. This reporting improvement is confined to that evaluation; v1's unspecified Numeracy run count prevents inferring an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: Many original COCO scores and ablation values persist, but v2 adds substantial compositional, layout, comparator and latent-selection results. For example, its new layout experiment reports GLIGEN counting F1 of 66.58 without ISAC and 71.28 with ISAC. Numeracy values change from 54.3% to 55.0% for SD1.5+ISAC, 50.7% to 51.1% for SDXL, and 63.4% to 64.0% for SDXL+ISAC, now with 30-seed reporting; these are not established same-setting gains. Changed SD1.5 efficiency values in v2 Table 2 remain unreconciled with the older values retained in Table 15.

M1.justification: v1 combines instance separation with a class-overlap penalty. v2 Section 3.3 extends this to explicit token-pair repulsion and attribute binding, introducing a binding loss absent from v1. Appendix C.1 also adds an alternative inference procedure that selects candidates using accumulated ISAC losses without backpropagation. The underlying clustering, MPO and attention-propagation components remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Separate preliminaries are condensed into method background, the method is organized into named phases and a scheduling subsection, and experiments and appendices are substantially reorganized. Terminology changes from class disambiguation to semantic separation accompany this broader narrative revision.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening comparison, redraws the method overview, restructures the main results table and adds heatmaps, parser examples, layout comparisons, failure illustrations and analysis tables. Several earlier standalone figures disappear. Retained displays are distinguishable from additions: for example, v1 Figure 2 becomes v2 Figure 3, and v1 Figure 15 becomes v2 Figure 22.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around training-free guidance, count supervision, layout control and benchmark limitations. New discussions include Self-Cross, GLIGEN, Attention Refocusing, HRS-Bench, OverLayBench and TIFA. CountGen, already cited in v1 as Make It Count, receives substantive comparative and complementarity analysis. The earlier MCR/TweedieMix discussion and several segmentation/distillation references disappear.

T1.justification: v2 formally defines repulsion/binding token-pair sets and the binding objective based on 1 minus MPO in Section 3.3, extending v1's class-only objective. The central MPO, foreground-mask, clustering and attention-propagation definitions remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's largely counting-focused evidence: Tables 2–4 add broader compositional tasks, comparisons on SD3.5-M and layout evaluation using shared box inputs. Parser documentation, quantified seed variability and concrete failure analyses address important reproducibility and applicability gaps. Conflicting exact-versus-fractional accuracy definitions and unreconciled efficiency figures weaken reporting, and the quality metrics measure deviation from SDXL rather than directly proving aesthetic preservation. Nevertheless, the expanded comparative evidence and methodological documentation provide a substantial net improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ISAC research, with matching authors, core framework and retained experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds compositional benchmarks, layout-conditioned generation, latent-selection results, quality analyses and seed-variability measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations and qualitative analyses in Section 5 and the appendices, including Tables 1–4 and 8–11.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central ISAC and IntraCompBench contributions remain. The abstract, introduction and conclusion now emphasize improving open-weight models and narrowing their gap with commercial systems. The abstract also qualifies v2's claim of requiring no external models to requiring no external vision models.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of count-mismatch failures, the value of frequent reclustering, and difficulties with small or thin foreground objects. It interprets new commercial-model and VLM results as evidence about applicability and detector bias. Appendix C.3 replaces the earlier A&E-based quality discussion with stronger claims about preference and absence of quality trade-offs; the existing 3D/transparency limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 reports code and IntraCompBench availability through a project link, replacing v2's future code-release promise. Appendix A.1 newly specifies omitting global or ambiguously assigned attribute-binding pairs, and Figure 2 documents averaging masks over denoising timesteps. These are access and implementation disclosures, not demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use HRS-Bench, T2I-CompBench including Numeracy, and IntraCompBench with the same 37 COCO classes and 2–5-instance tasks. Text-to-image and layout-to-image coverage remain. Added backbones, evaluators and internal-control perturbations do not introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated comparisons with DOS in Table 2, CO3 and DeLeaker in Table 11, and GPT-Image-1.5 and Nano Banana 2 in Table 13. Conversely, A&E is removed from the image-quality comparison corresponding to v2 Table 13 and v3 Table 15, although it remains elsewhere.

E3.justification: Added evaluation settings include Flux.2-dev latent selection, 8-step Z-Image-Turbo and 4-step Flux.2-klein-4B generation, GPT-5.5 evaluation, and PickScore/HPSv3 metrics. New controlled experiments perturb internal counts and clustering frequency. These extend the evaluation design; the original benchmark sampling and retained experiments' stated settings largely remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds foreground-threshold sensitivity, quantitative coordinate ablation, internal-count mismatch tests, clustering-frequency trade-offs and detector-independent validation. The existing loss comparison gains Dice and top-5%/top-10% MPO variants. Commercial-model failure examples and preference analysis also extend the supplementary evidence; earlier schedule, clustering-algorithm, seed and layer analyses remain.

E5.justification: v3 Table 14 introduces statistical agreement analysis through Pearson correlations between detector and GPT-5.5 evaluations, reporting 0.73 and 0.75. The existing 30-seed Numeracy means and standard deviations, and 10-seed IntraCompBench practice, remain unchanged; no additional confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover modern comparators, few-step models, preference scores and sensitivity tests. For example, v3 Table 5 newly reports Flux.2-dev class/instance averages of 88%/87% without ISAC and 92%/92% with latent selection. Retained accuracy results mostly match. Table 2 changes TEBOpt's SD3.5-M costs from 139 s/74.5 GB to 42 s/28.8 GB, while Appendix Table 19 retains the older values. Table 4's percentage-to-fraction conversion is only equivalent rounding.

M1.justification: Foreground gating, self-attention clustering, MPO losses, semantic binding and the linear loss schedule are retained. Both latent optimization and latent selection already appear in v2; moving Algorithm 2 into the main text and introducing the ISACLO label do not change the method. Expanded parser details do not establish a procedural revision.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Latent selection moves from Appendix C.1 into Section 4.3, the loss-metric discussion moves into the appendix, Appendix C is reorganized, and references move before the appendices. Terminology, title and author information also change.

P2.justification: v3 substantially redesigns page layout, typography and figure/table placement, including paired Tables 3–4 and Figures 6–7. It adds threshold, commercial-performance, commercial-failure and clustering-frequency figures, plus new comparison tables and preference columns. Some displays are reused: Figure 7 draws examples from v2's appendix, and latent-selection displays move into the main text.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially around open-weight versus commercial systems and contemporary methods including DOS, CO3 and DeLeaker. Related work more explicitly distinguishes CLIP-dependent embedding methods and token-conditioned structural grouping from ISAC. v2's categorical claim of being the first training-free method for instance-level control in Section 2 is removed.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix C.6 newly defines top-k% MPO alternatives by averaging the largest overlap products, extending the loss definitions used in ablations. The principal attention, masking and loss equations remain equivalent after renumbering; no new theorem, proof or derivation is added.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens an already extensive empirical study with useful count-sensitivity tests, VLM cross-checks and contemporary comparisons, improving support for applicability and robustness. The gain is moderated by removing A&E from the quality comparison, treating automated preference scores as stronger evidence of preserved visual quality than they establish, and leaving revised TEBOpt costs unexplained against retained appendix values. Overall, the added validation provides a positive but limited net improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ISAC and IntraCompBench. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and reports additional model comparisons, evaluator validation, preference scores and sensitivity analyses.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations and seed-stability measurements, including Tables 2–6 and the appendices.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same benchmark, annotation-pipeline and MVSM contributions, including the 46.24-point improvement claim. Additional validation does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly interprets the format experiment as evidence against multiple-choice shortcut learning and the backbone experiments as evidence of architecture-independent applicability. Appendix B.2 also replaces the description of balanced directional frequencies with primary-direction dominance interpreted as natural spatial-language usage. The limitations in Appendix A remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub access link and discloses default API parameters and default Transformers generation settings in Appendix C.2. The PDFs do not verify repository contents or availability. Existing training hardware, batch size, epochs and time are moved from Section 5.1 to Appendix C.1 without substantive changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same ScanNet, MS-COCO and Spatial-MM sources, five ViewSpatial-Bench tasks, two VSI-Bench subtasks and indoor/outdoor VSI-App scenarios. The larger stated VSI-App sample count and additional training configurations do not establish new domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds GPT-4o to the quantitative VSI-Bench and VSI-App comparisons; v1 Table 2 compares only Qwen2.5-VL-3B and MVSM. GPT-4o already appeared in the main benchmark and qualitative examples, but its participation in these quantitative transfer comparisons is new.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds controlled multiple-choice versus direct-answer training and fine-tuning experiments with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL2.5-2B. Appendix B.4 also revises VSI-App from 50 scenes, split 25/25, to 200, split 100/100. These substantially extend the evaluation design, although Section 5.3.1 still states 50 scenes, leaving the precise setting of the revised transfer results inconsistently documented.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 and Table 6 test whether gains depend on multiple-choice shortcuts and whether training benefits extend across backbones and model sizes. These add substantive controlled robustness evidence beyond v1's transfer experiments and qualitative perspective-confusion analysis. The earlier qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix C.2 newly states that each model is evaluated five times on ViewSpatial-Bench and reported scores are averages. v1 does not disclose this practice there; the PDFs do not establish an increase in runs. VSI-App's five option-order tests and voting remain unchanged, and neither version reports confidence intervals or run variability.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores are unchanged between v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2. New Table 6 reports 79.34% for direct-answer training, 83.01% for Qwen2.5-VL-7B MVSM and 76.45% for InternVL2.5-2B MVSM. Transfer results add GPT-4o and replace VSI-App indoor/outdoor/overall scores: Qwen3B changes from 24/20/22 to 18/27/22.5, and MVSM from 44/24/34 to 41/36/38.5. Given the revised sample count, these are replaced results rather than established same-setting improvements.

M1.justification: The proposed annotation algorithms and MVSM fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged, including the frozen vision encoder and projector. v2 adds experimental answer-format and backbone variants without replacing the primary method or introducing an algorithmic component.

P1.justification: v2 condenses related-work prose, makes local terminology and typo corrections, moves distribution discussion to Appendix B.2 and training details to Appendix C.1, and adds Appendix C.3. Most prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds benchmark-comparison and robustness tables, adds a row to the transfer table, redraws the directional-distribution and object-frequency plots, and revises the word cloud. The distribution figure moves to the appendix, and the retained example figures are grouped on the final page. The overall document layout remains similar.

R1.justification: New Table 1 provides a structured comparison with eight spatial benchmarks. v2 adds citations for All-Angles Bench, GSR-Bench, STI-Bench and Transformers, while removing several references, including Attention Is All You Need and the spatial-frame-of-reference study. The central positioning around insufficient multi-perspective evaluation remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, the head-to-body angular-offset calculation and coordinate-to-direction mapping remain unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or mathematical derivations.

improvement.justification: The new format controls and additional-backbone experiments strengthen validation beyond v1's single trained backbone, while evaluation disclosures improve transparency. These benefits are limited by inconsistent VSI-App reporting: Section 5.3.1 retains 50 scenes and gains of +20/+4, whereas Appendix B.4 states 200 scenes and Table 3 gives +23/+9. The added validation supports a modest net improvement, but the revised transfer evidence is less clearly documented.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViewSpatial-Bench and MVSM study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithms and Appendices A–C are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations in Tables 2–3 and adds training-format and backbone experiments in Appendix C.3 and Table 6.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, MVSM fine-tuning results and transfer experiments in Tables 1–2, together with qualitative analyses.

C1.justification: V1 presents identifying centroid prediction as a key counting component and constructing an improved baseline as central contributions. V2 drops that emphasis and foregrounds C-REX as a plug-in applicable to any REC architecture, demonstrated on three architectures. Its headline improvement claims change from over 22% MAE and 10% RMSE to up to 28% and 24.5% under the revised comparisons.

C2.justification: V2 introduces discussion of negative-token scarcity in extremely dense scenes and potential scaling with larger backbones. It interprets the joint-loss and Molmo experiments as support for specialized visual supervision, explicitly qualifies paraphrase robustness for CAD-GD, and illustrates accurate-looking counts that still select incorrect instances in Figure 8. V1's top-N label-noise justification and centroid-centered explanations are removed.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents 20/30-epoch training schedules, learning-rate decay, checkpoint/retraining provenance, and CAD-GD density-map construction. It omits v1's explicit AdamW optimizer, weight decay of 1e-4, and loss weights of 1, 5, and 0.005. The direct code-repository link becomes a project-page link. These are documentation and access-instruction changes; the PDFs do not establish changes to omitted parameters or actual resource availability.

E1.justification: REC-8K and FSC-147 remain, but v2 removes the CARPK drone/parking-lot evaluation, eliminating v1's separate cross-dataset transfer test. V2 adds evaluation on paraphrased REC-8K expressions, introducing a linguistic-variation scenario.

E2.justification: V2 adds CAD-GD comparisons, including its density-guided inference variant, and Molmo2-4B. The FSC-147 comparison removes exemplar-based methods including FamNet, BMNet+, CounTR, and CACViT. Earlier REC comparators such as ZSC, TFOC, CounTX, and CountGD remain in supplementary Tables 6–7; their relocation is not removal.

E3.justification: Reported detection thresholds change from 0.30/0.36 to 0.25/0.35 for CLS/other tokens. V2 adds Swin-B configurations alongside Swin-T, reports precision and recall separately, evaluates density-guided CAD-GD inference, and specifies zero-shot and two-shot Molmo protocols. The count-range analysis also merges the three lowest bins into 0–20. These are substantive protocol changes, beyond newly disclosed training details.

E4.justification: V2 adds image-text versus image-only versus joint-loss ablations and paraphrase robustness testing. Its selection ablation adds bipartite matching and removes the N + 2log2(N) alternative. Count-range and qualitative analyses expand to paired comparisons across three architectures, while v1's attribute-wise MAE analysis and centroid-baseline component ablation disappear. The positive-anchor loss ablation is retained in Table 4b.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The sample counts accompanying count-range plots describe evaluation examples, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: V1's REC MAE/RMSE of 5.06/17.53 survives as the top-N ablation in v2 Table 4a. New matching-based GroundingDINO+C-REX results are 4.38/17.93 with Swin-T and 4.20/16.76 with Swin-B. V2 adds extensive architecture, paraphrase, and Molmo results while removing CARPK and attribute-level scores. Findings include CAD-GD paraphrase MAE worsening from 6.85 to 8.02 with C-REX. Changed methods and protocols preclude treating cross-version scores as same-setting gains.

M1.justification: V1 selects positive tokens by cosine similarity to the class-masked referring expression, taking the top N tokens. V2 instead uses bipartite matching between predicted locations and ground-truth points, changing the contrastive labeling procedure and supervision. It also integrates C-REX into GroundingREC and CAD-GD by replacing their image-text losses while retaining their other objectives. The positive-anchor contrastive loss itself remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around embedding-space choice and architectural portability. The baseline-centered method subsection disappears, remaining method explanations are reordered and expanded, and the supplementary narrative is reorganized. This is substantial editorial restructuring beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The original pipeline figure is replaced by two conceptual comparisons, tables are rebuilt around paired baseline/C-REX configurations and backbones, and qualitative grids are extensively revised. The earlier REC comparison is split and moved to supplementary tables; the count-range plot is regrouped and the attribute-wise chart removed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands research positioning: CAD-GD becomes an important REC predecessor, counting VQA is distinguished from localized REC, intra-image contrastive learning is related to person re-identification, and VLM/tool-based counting is discussed. These additions introduce substantive comparisons and citations beyond v1's focus on GroundingREC and detection-versus-density counting.

T1.justification: The positive-set definition changes from the cosine-similarity arg-top-N construction in v1 Equations 2–3 to location-based bipartite matching in v2 Section 3. The supervised and modified contrastive-loss formulas otherwise remain algebraically unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central embedding-space and portability claims through three-architecture comparisons and direct image-text/image-only/joint-loss ablations, addressing important gaps in v1. Paraphrase and expanded failure analyses also clarify applicability. These gains outweigh the removed CARPK and attribute analyses and reduced hyperparameter disclosure. Some conclusions still overgeneralize: Table 4a shows worse test RMSE for matching than top-N selection, and Table 2 shows GroundingREC test MAE worsening from 10.12 to 12.46 with C-REX.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe C-REX for referring expression counting, despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments across three architectures on REC-8K and FSC-147, plus contrastive-loss ablations, paraphrase robustness tests, and Molmo evaluation.

before.justification: V1 reports original C-REX and baseline experiments on REC-8K, FSC-147, and CARPK, including quantitative results, ablations, and qualitative examples.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the advertised benchmarking contribution from detection, pose estimation, and depth estimation to 2D/6D detection. The central claims concerning industrial complexity, accurate annotations, and difficulty relative to household benchmarks remain. Sub-millimeter accuracy receives greater prominence, but v1 already claimed accuracy below 1 mm.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets YOLOX's comparable cross-dataset performance as occurring under an 'overfitting setup.' Its conclusion replaces v1's explicit warning about working-distance and object-scale limits on generalization to other materials and shapes with a broader future-expansion statement. The depth-specific interpretation of insufficient industrial precision is also removed.

D1.justification: v3 omits v1 Appendix B's batch sizes, training budgets, GPU specifications, and runtimes for YOLOX, GDRNet, and SurfEmb. It also omits the detailed five-view selection instructions, direct download/evaluation/toolkit links, and dataset directory diagram. Some split information moves into Section 4.1, which additionally specifies frame counts and 10–60 simulated instances; these disclosures do not establish changed experimental settings.

E1.justification: v3 adds explicit performance comparisons across YCB-V, T-LESS, LM-O, IC-BIN, and TUD-L, whereas v1's benchmark results concern XYZ-IBD. Conversely, v1's monocular-depth evaluation and TRICKY task disappear. The underlying XYZ-IBD objects, scenes, and synthetic training coverage remain substantially unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds NIDS-Net for unseen-object 2D detection and MatchU for unseen-object 6D detection. The earlier 2D/6D comparators remain, including GDRNet renamed GDRN in the table and SAM-6D under varying labels. Depth Anything V2 disappears with the depth evaluation.

E3.justification: v3 adds an average AP across five BOP datasets and removes the depth-specific scale/shift alignment, material-subset evaluation, and depth metrics. The retained 2D IoU-based AP, 6D MSSD/MSPD-based AP, detection-mask priors, and synthetic-training/real-testing design remain unchanged. The relocated split description does not establish a changed XYZ-IBD split.

E4.justification: v3 adds validation/test scene-density histograms in Figure 9 and qualitative detection/pose comparisons in Figure 10, including examples of incorrect object identities. The cross-dataset instance-distribution analysis already existed in v1 Appendix C and is relocated to v3 Figure 4. Annotation validation and noise-sensitivity analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report annotation errors of 0.999 mm with standard deviation 0.12 mm and 0.432 degrees with standard deviation 0.08 degrees, using the same stated simulation sampling. Neither adds baseline run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Relabeling the existing instance-statistics chart does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Between v1 Table 5 and v3 Table 4, reported XYZ-IBD 6D AP changes from 0.274 to 0.247 for SurfEmb, 0.547 to 0.564 for FoundationPose, and 0.438 to 0.578 for SAM-6D. The leading method consequently changes from FoundationPose to SAM-6D. v3 also adds cross-dataset results and NIDS-Net/MatchU entries, while removing depth results. The PDFs do not explain whether the revised shared scores reflect corrections or reruns.

M1.justification: The collection and annotation procedure remains unchanged: calibrated viewpoints, anti-reflection coating, multi-view depth fusion, manual CAD alignment, multi-scale ICP, and pose propagation. Simulation-based error quantification also retains the same procedure. Added baseline evaluations do not introduce a new proposed method.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Benchmark sections are reorganized around dataset splits and seen/unseen tasks, selected supplementary material moves into the main text, and the separate supplement disappears. Author information changes and an acknowledgements section is added. These are extensive narrative and structural revisions despite the stable annotation method.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reworks page layout and figure placement, expands and transposes the benchmark table into cross-dataset comparisons, revises sample montages, and adds split histograms and qualitative prediction grids. The depth tables and directory diagram disappear. Existing CAD and pipeline illustrations are retained or relocated, while the instance-statistics chart moves from v1 Figure 9 to v3 Figure 4 with revised legend labels.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations and discussion for MatchU, NIDS-Net, and Grounding DINO, while removing Depth Anything V2, GDRNPP, and some depth-benchmark references. The household-versus-industrial dataset positioning and most of Section 2 remain unchanged. The introduction adds criticism of measurement biases in existing industrial ground truth.

T1.justification: The MSSD, MSPD, and AP equations are retained without substantive mathematical revision. Neither version introduces additional theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations. Removing the depth-metric explanation changes evaluation documentation rather than theoretical content.

improvement.justification: v3 Table 4 provides direct cross-dataset evidence for the central industrial-difficulty claim, and the qualitative comparisons make failures easier to assess. However, removing v1's baseline training recipes and practical evaluation guidance materially reduces reproducibility, while the limitations become less explicit. The changed shared-method scores are also unexplained. These substantive gains and losses leave the net effect on overall paper quality uncertain.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XYZ-IBD dataset and annotation pipeline. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. v1's supplementary Sections A–C were compared against the complete v3 PDF, allowing relocated material to be distinguished from omissions.

after.justification: v3 retains the original annotation-error evaluation and reports detection and pose-estimation experiments in Table 4, supplemented by dataset statistics and qualitative predictions.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-error simulations and experimental results for object detection, 6D pose estimation, and monocular depth estimation, including Tables 4–6.

C1.justification: v3 makes a dedicated, reproducible evaluator with interpretable reasoning a central contribution, extending v1's claim of a fine-grained VLM questioning framework. Reference-image-based style assessment also becomes an explicit contribution in the abstract and conclusion. The hierarchical benchmark and GNED contributions are retained.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes consistent rankings from two off-the-shelf evaluators; v3 instead develops an argument for task-specific adaptation using Qwen3VL-8B verification tests. It justifies choosing reasoning over the slightly more accurate classifier for interpretability and explains how aspect-ratio matching should reduce layout-related style mismatches. The stated limitations concerning English, common objects, and linguistic register remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 documents the evaluator backbone, balanced 218K-question training set, annotation process, one-epoch training, revised evaluation prompt, reference-image sources, aspect ratios, and checklist statistics. v1's project-page pointer is omitted. However, style aggregation is inconsistent: Section 3.3 averages CSD and DINOv3, whereas Appendix A4.2 additionally includes SigLIP2.

E1.justification: The original 5,000 English prompts and evaluation dimensions are retained, but v3 introduces an evaluator-training corpus of generated images and annotated binary questions, whereas v1 performs no evaluator training. It also adds style-reference image sets and extends empirical prompt-diversity analysis to additional benchmark corpora, including Gecko, WISE, and LongT2I-Bench.

E2.justification: The main comparison adds Qwen-Image, FLUX.2 Dev, BAGEL, Emu3.5 variants, and Nano-Banana variants, while removing several earlier rows, including Playground, LlamaGen, and LightGen. In the corresponding GenAI Bench and CompBench++ comparisons, Nano-Banana replaces FLUX.1 Pro and MidJourney v7 replaces the reported v6/v6.1 comparator. Evaluator validation also introduces comparisons against off-the-shelf Qwen3VL-8B.

E3.justification: v3 changes benchmark scoring through its trained evaluator and reference-based style metric. New experimental protocols include a balanced 560-question held-out validation set, one-epoch training for three evaluator paradigms, a 100-case text-metric preference study using identical OCR outputs, and per-generator AUROC validation. The earlier ten-participant, three-sets-per-dimension ranking protocol is retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds evaluator-training ablations, human-label validation across eight generators, and a controlled comparison of GNED, PNED, and OCR Recall. It expands semantic-redundancy analysis but removes the earlier t-SNE analysis, GPT-4o/Qwen2.5 ranking-agreement analysis, and explicit full-benchmark versus testmini consistency checks.

E5.justification: v3 newly specifies two generation rollouts per model over all 5,000 prompts when constructing the evaluator corpus. This is repetition information for new data collection, not evidence that the earlier benchmark experiments received additional repeated runs. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The main leaderboard contains extensively revised entries and rankings, including NB-Pro scores of 93.1/93.3 in v3 Table 2. New findings include 91.07% reasoning-evaluator accuracy and 83%/94%/99% human-preference agreement for Recall/PNED/GNED. Earlier full-set and Qwen-scored tables disappear, while the human Spearman correlations are retained. Changed scoring prevents interpreting leaderboard differences as same-setting performance gains.

M1.justification: v1 uses off-the-shelf GPT-4o or Qwen2.5-VL-72B for checklist evaluation. v3 introduces a trained Qwen3VL-8B TIIF-Evaluator that generates reasoning before binary answers, and replaces yes/no style assessment with aspect-ratio-matched reference-image similarities. Prompt composition and the GNED formula remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, evaluation discussion, and model analyses undergo extensive rewriting. The separate user-study section is merged into Section 4.2, appendices are reorganized around statistics, prompts, experiments, and visualizations, and references move after the appendices. Model terminology and author information also change.

P2.justification: The original multi-panel diversity figure is replaced by an expanded benchmark comparison, and the construction pipeline is redrawn. v3 adds PNED and AUROC figures plus statistics and text-metric tables, removes several earlier results tables, and relocates the concept-pool table and human-study illustration. Typography, page layout, and numerous captions also change substantially.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands discussion of question-based evaluation, newer reward models, long-prompt benchmarks, and reasoning benchmarks. It distinguishes unified models from autoregressive generators and positions TIIF-Evaluator against closed-API evaluation and unadapted general-purpose VLMs. These are substantive positioning changes beyond reference updates.

T1.justification: The binary-match scoring equation and GNED definition, normalization, and bounds are unchanged. v3 Figure 6 adds a concrete counterexample to PNED's length comparability: duplicating the target and omission pattern changes PNED from 1 to 2 while GNED remains 0.5. No new theorem or general proof is introduced.

improvement.justification: The new human-labeled evaluator validation and controlled text-metric study strengthen evidence beyond v1's ranking correlations and qualitative examples. However, v3 removes full-set and cross-evaluator checks while introducing conflicting style-score definitions and unexplained discrepancies between the Text scores in Table 2 and GNED values in Table A3. Because these issues affect core evaluation reliability and reproducibility, the PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TIIF-Bench and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across extensive revision, renumbering, and relocation.

after.justification: v3 reports benchmark results, evaluator-training ablations, human-labeled evaluator validation, and a new text-rendering metric preference study.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-model benchmark results, human-preference correlations, qualitative evaluations, and appendix experiments using GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-VL-72B.

Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains confidence-guided augmentation for distillation under unknown covariate shift. However, v1's blanket superiority claim is qualified in v3's abstract and conclusion to best or second-best sample mean accuracy, while the claimed evaluation scope expands to BAR and CelebA-HQ.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning estimation of the theoretical constants and augmentation distribution, applicability to location-sensitive tasks, and failures caused by unnatural generation or stalled optimization. It proposes domain mismatch as an explanation for weaker Hyper-SD results. The earlier two-augmentation optimum is replaced by dataset-dependent scaling conclusions, and the teacher-dependence discussion is revised around the new teacher setup and weaker-teacher experiments.

D1.justification: Appendices B, C and N greatly expand reproducibility information: inversion and denoising settings, separate optimization learning rates, stopping rules, background regularization, Hyper-SD/IP-Adapter configuration, checkpoint references, teacher-logit aggregation and baseline-specific parameters. FLOP measurement assumptions and generation multipliers are documented. Conversely, v1's V100 generation-time measurements are no longer reported.

E1.justification: v3 adds BAR activity classification under place shift and five-shot Oxford Pets evaluation without deliberately imposed covariate shift (Appendix L). It also substitutes CelebA-HQ for CelebA while retaining bird and ImageNet classification. These changes substantially broaden the represented tasks and evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Diff-Mix and Diff-II join the evaluated diffusion baselines in v3 Tables 2–3. The TAB combination experiments in v1 are replaced by LfF and uLA comparisons in v3 Table 8; plain Stable Diffusion and CutMixPick evaluations disappear. GIF, DistDiff, DA-Fusion and ActGen remain, with DA-Fusion's spelling change not treated as a new method.

E3.justification: Training changes from 100 epochs with cosine decay and validation-selected checkpoints to 300 epochs with constant learning rates and final-checkpoint evaluation. Main generation budgets become approximately FLOP-matched rather than equal augmentation counts. SpuCo Birds switches from a specially fine-tuned ViT-B teacher to zero-shot CLIP with species aggregation. CelebA-HQ uses reversed official split roles and eight groups rather than sixteen; ImageNet training changes to 100 spurious-feature-selected images per class.

E4.justification: v3 adds component-isolation, weaker-teacher, replacement-probability, target-class and single-step-generator studies, together with explicit failure cases and no-shift evaluation. ConvNeXt experiments replace the TinyViT/ResNet studies, and the ERM-plus-EDRM loss ablation is removed. Existing augmentation-count, stronger-augmentation and synthetic-sample difficulty analyses are revised rather than simply added anew.

E5.justification: Reported group-shift results change from means and standard deviations over three trainings in v1 Table 1 to six in v3 Table 2. Appendix B additionally states that synthetic datasets are generated once and ImageNet training is performed once per method. The uncertainty-reporting framework otherwise remains mean plus standard deviation, without new confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Core results are replaced under revised conditions: ConfiG's ViT-T ImageNet accuracy is 93.3% in v1 Table 2 and 80.02% in v3 Table 3, which is not a same-setting performance decline. Substantial new results include BAR, where ConfiG's mean SMA is 58.66% versus Diff-Mix's 59.28%, and Oxford Pets, where ConfiG trails both evaluated baselines at the smaller augmentation budget.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes generation from original-class latent optimization to inter-class prompt-to-prompt initialization followed by optimization toward a different target class. Equation 7 changes from maximizing teacher confidence plus transformed student uncertainty to minimizing student confidence plus transformed teacher uncertainty, jointly optimizing latent, null-text and conditioning. Appendix E also introduces a Hyper-SD variant using IP-Adapter guidance.

P1.justification: The method exposition is reorganized into named discussions of empirical motivation, latent optimization, inter-class mixing and the auxiliary student. Experimental and limitations prose is extensively rewritten, and implementation material is consolidated into Appendix B. The former A.1–A.13 appendix structure is substantially reordered into topical Appendices A–O, with some analyses moved out of the main text.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different document template and extensively redesigns tables and figures. The large ERM/EDRM comparison table becomes separate comparison and ablation tables; v1's combined Table 2 is separated into ImageNet results and appendix diagnostics. Qualitative panels now emphasize inter-class mixing stages, with new failure-case and generator-variant displays, additional diagnostic plots and revised legends and captions.

R1.justification: The cited literature substantially expands around inter-class augmentation, prompt-to-prompt editing, consistency models, Hyper-SD, IP-Adapter and newer augmentation and robustness research. Diff-Mix becomes explicit motivation for a method component, while additional discussion positions ConfiG relative to fast diffusion and context-guided generation. These are substantive additions beyond citation renumbering or publication-metadata updates.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix A replaces v1's infinity-norm approximation assumptions with a KL-divergence teacher bound and explicit risk-gap assumptions. Proposition 1 revises the mixing-rate constraint and changes the final bound from min{Ω−Θ, Ω/2} to max{Ω−αΘ, Ω/2}. The lemma and proof are rewritten, and a new derivation connects teacher-label concentration and confidence separation to the required risk gap.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs the unsupported final bound in v1's Proposition 1 and explicitly limits the theory's practical interpretation. It replaces the specially fine-tuned bird teacher, which v1 acknowledged was impractical, with a zero-shot procedure, strengthens component and applicability testing, and documents systematic approximate compute matching. Failure cases and unfavorable Oxford Pets results provide useful boundaries. Although some earlier ablations are lost and changed settings prevent direct performance comparisons, the gains in mathematical soundness, experimental scrutiny and reproducibility substantially improve the paper.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConfiG research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and support reliable comparison despite substantial methodological and experimental revisions.

after.justification: v3 reports original experiments on CelebA-HQ, SpuCo Birds, BAR and ImageNet-100, plus Oxford Pets experiments and extensive appendix analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and distillation experiments on CelebA, SpuCo Birds and Spurious ImageNet, together with quantitative ablations and qualitative augmentation examples.
