Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central claims of improved lexical order, semantic accuracy, and state-of-the-art performance on the same two datasets remain. v2 refines the contribution emphasis toward LTF and temporal grounding, broadening the criticized mechanism from sentence-level conditioning to global fusion even when gloss conditions are available.

C2.justification: v1 explains face attention as potentially redundant or noisy because facial expressions lack diversity; v2 instead interprets facial cues as complementary and supports full IPA. v2 also interprets comparisons with NAT-EA as evidence that temporal-gloss conditions alone are insufficient, adds smoothness-based interpretations, and explicitly identifies the need for a text-to-gloss model when transferring to another language.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the 529-dimensional motion representation, 50 diffusion steps, 14-layer denoiser, dimensions and attention heads, convolution settings, duration-estimator architecture, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, training iterations, and RTX 4090 hardware. It adds a project-page link. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although evaluator details are deferred to unavailable supplementary material.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Chinese and German text-to-sign generation on CSL-Daily and PHOENIX-2014T. The added smoothness analysis and revised gloss/duration controls concern the retained coverage; no additional dataset, language, population, or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds G2P-DDM and NAT-EA and removes T2S-GPT. NAT-EA joins the opening qualitative comparison and replaces NSA in the later qualitative figure. Spoken2Sign becomes an evaluated comparator in the new smoothness study, alongside NSA, MoMask, and NAT-EA.

E3.justification: v1 describes a resource-constrained reimplementation of the back-translation encoder; v2 reports retraining all methods with a common face-inclusive representation and matching evaluator. Test-length ablations and train/test-length main results give way to estimated-duration results with a test-duration control. v2 also introduces peak-velocity/jerk metrics and random duration perturbations. The revised settings prevent direct cross-version performance comparisons.

E4.justification: v2 adds motion-smoothness measurements and two jerk-curve case studies, a ground-truth-gloss control, random duration perturbations, and the previously missing face-only IPA configuration. It removes the pooled-text and pooled-gloss controls from Table 1 and the +8 duration perturbation. Qualitative examples and comparators are also revised.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates only. v2 Table 5 introduces ± statistics for peak velocity and jerk, but does not define their meaning or report repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals. This establishes changed variability reporting, not an increase in experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 extensively replace numerical results under revised settings. Table 2 reverses the face-attention ranking: v1 favors excluding face attention, with BLEU-4 13.27 versus 12.79; v2 favors full IPA, with 15.60 versus 13.59 without face attention. New Table 5 reports SIGNER peak velocity 0.38±0.10 and peak jerk 0.35±0.12. These are not same-setting cross-version gains.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 replaces training-set gloss-length statistics and an unseen-gloss fallback with an MLP that predicts durations from gloss embeddings. Section 4.3 and Figure 4 expand IPA from body-hand interactions to include face-body interactions. These change generation and feature exchange; renaming TAC to LTF largely preserves the AdaLN-plus-convolution fusion mechanism.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around temporal grounding and global versus local fusion. GLOS/TAC terminology becomes SIGNER/LTF throughout. Preliminary and method explanations are reorganized, and dedicated implementation, training-objective, and limitation passages are added.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a three-way conditioning comparison, Figure 3 is reorganized into three stages, and Figure 4 adds face-attention paths. Qualitative panels are revised, and Table 5 plus the jerk-curve Figure 6 are added. Table 4 gains gloss-free/gloss-based grouping, while the document adopts a different page template and relocates figures.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work newly engage NAT-EA and G2P-DDM as closely related gloss-conditioned generators, acknowledging prior temporal-gloss conditioning and positioning local fusion as the distinguishing contribution. This substantially revises the earlier positioning around predominantly sentence-level conditioning, beyond routine citation or bibliography changes.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.3 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the diffusion loss as expected original-token negative log-likelihood, whereas v1 only references variational lower-bound training. The existing VQ-VAE and diffusion-transition equations are retained. No theorem, proof, or formal guarantee is added.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper through comparisons with closely related gloss-conditioned methods, concrete implementation settings, smoothness evidence, and an explicit transfer limitation. These improve support for the contribution and reproducibility relative to v1. The gain is limited by removed conditioning controls, undefined ± statistics, and unavailable supplementary evaluator details and cross-evaluator results. The revised scores themselves cannot establish improvement because the method and evaluation settings changed.

A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from GLOS to SIGNER, and their supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. Neither includes a substantive appendix. However, v2 explicitly refers to supplementary evaluator details and cross-evaluator results that are absent from the supplied file, limiting comparison of those components.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, revised ablations and robustness experiments, qualitative comparisons, and new motion-smoothness measurements in Table 5 and Figure 6.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, conditioning and attention ablations, robustness tests, and qualitative generation results on CSL-Daily and PHOENIX-2014T.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain automated large-scale affordance annotation and unified 2D/3D grounding. v2 explicitly extends the pretraining-benefit claim to prior architectures and emphasizes gains on unseen categories. It drops v1's explicit claim of being the first to integrate the separate 2D and 3D research streams.

C2.justification: v2 interprets filtered-pretraining gains as evidence beyond category overlap, attributes cross-domain asymmetry primarily to training volume, and explains early 2D saturation through the synthetic-to-real domain gap. It adds substantive CoT, mask-selection and error-propagation explanations. v1's frozen-encoder rationale, detailed critique of prior heatmaps and partial-view robustness discussion are removed. Existing background and action-detail limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents smallest-mask selection, category-filtering instructions, explicit instance/view/query separation, and interpolation when training and test resolutions differ. It adds a project-page link while retaining the dataset URL. Model checkpoints, hardware, training budgets and most implementation recipes remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds qualitative zero-shot evaluation on cluttered Open X-Embodiment robot-workspace images (Figure 7) and removes the Affogato-Partial evaluation of partially observed furniture objects (v1 Appendix C). The principal Objaverse-derived, LASO and AGD20K coverage remains. Affogato-750K renames the existing annotation collection rather than introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: The LASO comparison expands beyond OpenAD and PointRefer to include Referring Transformer, 3D-SPS, ReLA and IAGNet (v2 Table 2). AffordanceNet, associated with RAGNet, is added to both zero-shot and supervised AGD20K comparisons (Table 4). These are substantive additions to the reported comparator sets.

E3.justification: v2 replaces direct LASO–Affogato transfer comparisons with LASO seen/unseen comparisons using pretraining followed by target-dataset fine-tuning. It adds category-filtering, training-volume and point-resolution controls. Human validation now describes disjoint annotator assignments and removal of incorrect queries. The reported 2D image count falls from 300,208 to 150,104, consistent with retaining only the most visible viewpoint instead of also sampling a neighboring view.

E4.justification: v2 adds held-out-category filtering, pretraining-scale and volume-matching analyses, training/test resolution sensitivity, qualitative CoT and mask-selection ablations, and stage-specific failure analysis (Section 5.4; Appendix C). These investigate overlap, scaling, design choices and error mechanisms previously untested. The partial-view robustness study is removed; the background-augmentation ablation remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The added scores and failure percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation or change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for pretraining, new comparators and controls; its new LASO comparison reports Espresso-3D unseen aIoU of 18.7 without versus 20.8 with pretraining. Human validation changes from 72.3% good, 12.3% ok and 15.4% not good to 84.8% success with an error breakdown. Direct cross-dataset and partial-view results disappear. Retained Affogato and Espresso-2D scores match after accounting for percentage rescaling.

M1.justification: The documented Espresso-3D objective changes from equally weighted Focal and Dice losses to BCE and Dice losses (v1 Appendix A.2; v2 Appendix B.2). Section 4 also changes frozen encoders to fine-tuned encoders, although v2 Appendix B.2 still states that the vision backbone is frozen, leaving the actual policy unresolved. The core architectures and three-stage annotation pipeline remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Separate 2D/3D related-work discussions are consolidated, Affogato becomes the framework name and Affogato-750K the dataset name, a dedicated analysis subsection is introduced, and the appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: The overview and pipeline diagrams are redrawn, the prior-dataset failure figure is replaced by human-validation and pipeline-error displays, and several analysis tables and figures are added. Tables are reorganized around pretraining comparisons. The former zero-shot Figure 7 moves to Appendix Figure A4, selected supervised examples move into Figure 9, and partial-view displays are removed. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of 2HandedAfforder, RAGNet, LMAffordance3D and recent 2D-to-3D transfer work. It acknowledges automated large-scale 2D datasets and contrasts their single-view supervision with multi-view aggregation. These update the competitive context while retaining the underlying positioning around affordance-data scarcity and open-vocabulary coverage.

T1.justification: Neither version provides theoretical propositions, proofs or substantive derivations. The coverage and diversity definitions remain equivalent, and the added empirical analyses introduce no new formal theory.

improvement.justification: v1's main 3D evidence for dataset utility relied on cross-dataset performance gaps. v2 directly tests pretraining benefits across architectures and checks held-out-category overlap (Tables 2 and 5), substantially strengthening the central empirical argument. Scaling, volume controls and pipeline-error analysis further improve validation. The contradictory encoder-training descriptions in Section 4 and Appendix B.2 impair reproducibility, and partial-view validation is lost, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the stronger evidence for the dataset's principal contribution.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Affogato dataset, annotation pipeline and Espresso models. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring and renaming.

after.justification: v2 reports original grounding experiments, human validation, pretraining comparisons, filtering controls, scaling and resolution analyses, and qualitative robot-scene evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-quality evaluation, quantitative 2D and 3D grounding experiments, background-augmentation ablations and partial-view experiments.

Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The first-real-time-transformer claim and four principal component contributions remain. V2 adds out-of-distribution robustness as a headline claim and more specific efficiency comparisons. V1's explicit claim of competitive inference without quantization libraries is dropped, while v2 foregrounds TensorRT FP16 measurements.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning component synergy, pretraining effects, annotation requirements, capacity-dependent inference reductions, and possible overfitting by larger OCHuman baselines. It omits v1's explicit tracking and keypoint-visibility limitations. The transpose-related latency limitation is retained in the conclusion, with stronger causal attribution to group attention.

D1.justification: V2 supplies important previously missing details: 100 positive and 100 negative denoising queries, attention-mask direction, area estimation, KSVF constants, backbone-specific learning rates, augmentation details, and comparator letterboxing with padding masks. Appendix A documents RTMO's pretraining configuration. The code link remains, but v1's explicit TensorRT version numbers are no longer supplied.

E1.justification: V2 adds COCO-trained evaluation on OCHuman, extending coverage to a distinct occlusion-heavy distribution-shift scenario. Appendix B also evaluates object detection alongside pose estimation when studying NMS. COCO validation coverage already existed in v1's appendix and is not a new benchmark.

E2.justification: V2 adds YOLO26 comparisons and introduces YOLO-Pose, ED-Pose, and GroupPose into the COCO validation comparison. Conversely, its COCO test-dev table removes DirectPose, FCPose, CID, InsPose, CenterNet, and RTMO-R50; its CrowdPose table removes PETR and QueryPose. V1's ED-Pose† is matched to v2's ED-Pose-Swin-L-5S rather than counted as newly added.

E3.justification: V1's 12-epoch sequential ablation becomes a fully trained component-combination study with FDR already included in the baseline. Reported CrowdPose training schedules change, including DETRPose-S from 150 to 156 epochs and X from 80 to 48. V2 moves latency benchmarking to an RTX A5500 and adds FP32 comparisons, NMS confidence-threshold controls, and inference configuration sweeps.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands analysis beyond v1's sequential component additions. Tables 6–8 test component interactions, alternative pretraining, dependence on keypoint constants and segmentation areas, and query/depth tradeoffs. OCHuman robustness tests, NMS sensitivity experiments, and convergence curves add evidence about generalization, latency, and training mechanisms.

E5.justification: V2 newly specifies median latency aggregation through the Roboflow benchmarking tool (Section 4.3); v1 leaves aggregation unspecified. Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial OCHuman, ablation, convergence, and modified-inference results. Existing HGNet-based COCO test-dev AP values remain unchanged, but COCO validation DETRPose-L AP changes from 72.5 to 72.7, and CrowdPose-S AP_H changes from 5.93 to 59.3. Parameter and latency entries also change extensively; the different benchmarking hardware prevents interpreting latency differences as same-setting speedups.

M1.justification: The denoising, FDR, Pose-LQE, and KSVF core remains. V2 adds DETRPose† inference variants that remove queries and later decoder layers without retraining (Section 4.5 and Appendix D). It also explicitly describes projection-layer removal, although the PDFs do not establish whether that optimization is new or newly documented.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Results are reorganized into datasets, variants, implementation, comparisons, and expanded analysis; COCO validation moves into the main text. The appendices are restructured, and the retained latency limitation moves into the conclusion.

P2.justification: V2 changes the page template and substantially redesigns the evidence presentation: comparison tables gain resource and training columns, the sequential ablation becomes a component matrix, and new convergence and cross-dataset plots appear. The architecture and Pose-LQE drawings are largely relocated, while denoising panels are reordered and captions revised.

R1.justification: V2 adds a focused denoising-related-work subsection and citations covering spatial queries, localization-quality estimation, VarifocalNet, segmentation resources, OCHuman, and YOLO26; CenterNet is removed. These clarify attribution and update the comparison context while retaining the central positioning as a GroupPose/D-FINE-based real-time pose estimator.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the denoising scale definition from a normalized quantity to human segmented area bounded by image area. V2's Equation 4 removes the extra wh factor appearing under the square root in v1, making it consistent with Equation 3, and explicitly defines the CrowdPose bounding-box-area proxy. These are localized mathematical corrections and definitions.

improvement.justification: Full-training component/pretraining ablations, explicit implementation details, and OCHuman testing improve support and reproducibility relative to v1's short sequential ablation. The net gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies and omitted limitations. For example, v2 Section 4.4 claims DETRPose-X surpasses all COCO validation comparators, but Table 3 reports 73.3 AP versus 75.7 for ED-Pose-Swin-L-5S. V1's explicit tracking and visibility caveats also disappear.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DETRPose, with matching core components, equations, and benchmarks. All main-text and appendix pages were readable, including figures and tables, supporting comparison despite substantial rewriting and expansion.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds OCHuman evaluation, expanded ablations, convergence analyses, NMS experiments, and reduced-query/depth evaluations.

before.justification: V1 reports original DETRPose results on COCO and CrowdPose, latency measurements, and component ablations, including COCO validation results in Appendix A.

Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central claim of label-efficient, language-guided segmentation remains. However, v2's abstract and introduction emphasize semantic pixel grouping and class discrimination, dropping v1's explicit headline promises of preventing instance collapse and cleanly separating overlapping objects. The introduction also states a more specific first-use claim for image-adapted textual object queries in semi-supervised segmentation.

C2.justification: v2 develops an interpretation of textual queries as semantic cluster centers and explains instance queries as helping group diverse appearances into the same class. v1 emphasizes spatial grounding and separation of overlapping instances. The limitation concerning inherited CLIP biases and poorly represented domain-specific classes remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents six pixel-decoder layers, 1,500 warm-up iterations and rare-class sampling, and changes reported hardware from one to two RTX-3090 GPUs. Conversely, it removes v1's numerical regularization weights, temperature value, module-specific learning-rate multiplier and sliding-window overlap specification. These additions and omissions substantially change reproducibility information without proving that every newly documented practice is new.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate semi-supervised semantic segmentation on Pascal VOC, COCO, ADE20K and Cityscapes. The represented datasets, class coverage and tasks remain unchanged; neither introduces an actual domain-shift evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds UniMatch-v2 with DINOv2-S and DINOv2-B alongside the retained comparators across the four benchmarks. The component ablation also replaces its SemiVL reference with a randomly initialized-query Mask2Former baseline. These changes substantially revise the comparison against prior methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds EVA02-L with 14-pixel patches to the original CLIP ViT-B/16 configuration. Section 4.1 changes the reported dataset-specific base learning rates to a uniform 0.0001, while retaining the labeled splits, crop sizes and epoch budgets. It states both polynomial and linear decay, leaving the precise schedule inconsistent. These reported setting changes do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablation changes from testing additions to SemiVL to testing textual semantic queries against randomly initialized Mask2Former queries. Later component rows, the class-wise ablation and the regularization comparisons retain their results. The qualitative cases are redistributed across figures, without adding new test cases or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The segmentation results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the original ViT-B/16 scores but adds EVA02-L and UniMatch-v2 results across the benchmarks. For example, COCO with 232 labels gains a newly reported EVA02-L score of 59.4 alongside the retained ViT-B/16 score of 54.5; this is not a same-setting improvement. The ablation reference changes from 84.0/87.3 to 82.0/83.3, while class-wise and regularization scores remain unchanged.

M1.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit diversity loss between hierarchical query levels. It also describes direct query-pixel mask products in place of v1's MLP-generated mask kernels. These are local revisions within the retained hierarchical-query, bidirectional-alignment and dual-query architecture; HSQG-to-HTQG and CMSAM-to-PTRM renaming alone does not establish a method change.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Numbered method subsections become component paragraphs, many displayed equations move inline, terminology changes throughout, and the conclusion is substantially compressed. Citations also change from numbered references to author-year style.

P2.justification: The architecture diagram is substantially redrawn with staged components and a separate attention panel. v1's qualitative Figure 4 is split and rearranged into v2 Figures 1 and 5 using the same cases. Table 1 gains backbone columns and changes its caption/highlighting convention, while the paired component and regularization ablations become separate tables.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused toward semi-supervised learning and query design, with detailed positioning against SemiVL, UniMatch-v2 and Mask2Former. Newly discussed works include kMaX-DeepLab, MP-Former and MDETR, while earlier discussions and references covering LXMERT, ViLBERT, VisualBERT, OpenSeg and LSeg disappear. This goes beyond citation-format changes.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a mathematical definition of cross-level query diversity using squared cosine similarity. v1's separate squared-distance query-to-text alignment objective is no longer specified. The prompt-topology, anchor and masked-consistency formulations remain substantially equivalent; no theorems or proofs are added.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful UniMatch-v2 and EVA02-L comparisons and clearer explanations of semantic grouping. However, it removes important reproducibility settings and introduces conflicting learning-rate schedules. Section 4.2 attributes a 3.4-point Cityscapes gain to UniMatch-v2 although Table 1 provides no result for that comparator at 100 labels; Section 4.3 reports a 5.6-point ablation gain where Table 3 implies 6.6. It is unclear whether the broader evidence outweighs these losses in reproducibility and internal consistency.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical vision-language segmentation framework, renamed from HierVL to HVL. All 12 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports additional backbone results and revised ablation results.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation results on four datasets, class-wise scores, component and regularization ablations, and qualitative predictions.

Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: V2 emphasizes domain-invariant textual queries, domain-shift generalization and the dual-query decoder. V3 centers dataset/image-conditioned domain awareness and decoder-layer consistency, adding a claim of first consistency-driven refinement within a mask-transformer framework. The broad claim of strong low-label performance across four benchmarks remains.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations involving dataset-specific semantics, accumulated decoder misalignment, soft relevance weighting avoiding discarded true positives, and downweighting strong augmentations to preserve domain awareness. Its interpretations increasingly distinguish spatial gating from token-similarity attention. V2's explicit limitation about inherited CLIP biases and classes absent from training disappears, although a narrower Cityscapes small-object caveat remains.

D1.justification: V3 specifies frozen GPT-4o, four descriptions per dataset-class, objective weights, the 0.95 confidence threshold, segmentation-loss coefficients and temperature. Appendix A.1 supplies dataset attributes and their generation procedure; A.2-A.4 document refinement and loss implementation. V3 also promises future GitHub code/results without supplying a repository link. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although ambiguities remain.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate semi-supervised semantic segmentation on Pascal VOC, COCO, ADE20K and Cityscapes. The additional prompting analyses and qualitative examples reuse this coverage; no new evaluated dataset, domain or task is established.

E2.justification: V3 adds reported comparisons with TQDM and Pseudo-SD across all four benchmarks, and POS on VOC, COCO and Cityscapes. It removes DualTeacher from VOC and several Cityscapes comparators, including CPS and U2PL. The component-ablation baseline changes from Mask2Former to TQDM. Figure 1 also reattributes identical prediction panels from SemiVL to UniMatch V2 without explaining the change.

E3.justification: The main benchmark splits, crop sizes and epoch budgets remain unchanged. Implementation statements change from one textual query per class to three, while COCO comparator backbones change from Xception-60 to XC65. New analyses introduce controlled hierarchy/threshold settings and a mean-cosine-similarity evaluation in A.5. These reported settings do not establish that every retained benchmark experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2's VOC component and regularization ablations are replaced by cumulative HTQG/PTRM/CMCR studies on low- and higher-label VOC and COCO splits. V3 adds prompting comparisons, absent-class weighting variants, hierarchy-depth sensitivity, PTRM versus cross-attention comparisons, and quantitative alignment analysis. The class-wise without-HTQG row disappears, while Figures A.1-A.5 add qualitative cases across the four datasets.

E5.justification: V2 gives no run or seed count. V3 Section 4.1 newly states that results are averaged over three random data-sampling seeds. Neither version reports dispersion, confidence intervals or significance tests. This establishes additional reporting, not an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: The EVA02-L benchmark mIoUs are retained, but some ViT-B results change: VOC-92 goes from 87.1 to 85.4 and Cityscapes-186 from 79.0 to 79.9. Class-wise results change, and extensive comparator, ablation and alignment results are added, including 0.54/0.62/0.77 in Table A.2. These concern revised methods, not controlled same-procedure improvements. V3's ADE20K-158 gain reporting is inconsistent: 41.6 versus TQDM's 25.3 implies 16.3, not the stated baseline gain of 13.5.

M1.justification: V3 adds GPT-4o-generated dataset-conditioned descriptions and replaces CLIP zero-shot class relevance with a trained adapter. PTRM changes from bidirectional cross-attention to convolutional spatial gating. The additional instance-level query set in v2's DQTD disappears, and mask/class aggregation changes. V2's topology/anchor and class-occlusion regularizers are replaced by TQDM-derived regularization and layer-wise cross-view/modal consistency. These are substantive procedural changes beyond renaming.

P1.justification: The title and framework name change, and the abstract, introduction, related work, methodology and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Method components receive numbered subsections, the narrative is reorganized around domain awareness and consistency, and a structured supplement is added. This exceeds terminology updates or edits accompanying new results alone.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column layout. V2's wide benchmark table is split and reoriented into v3 Tables 2-3; Figure 2 is redrawn, and the separate regularization diagrams disappear. Existing qualitative examples are retained and relocated, including Figure 5 becoming Figure 3, while new analysis tables and five supplementary qualitative figures substantially expand the displays.

R1.justification: Previously cited TQDM becomes the explicit baseline and source of inherited losses, with its one-way alignment and domain-generalization focus defining the proposed distinction. V3 adds substantive positioning against Pseudo-SD and references for POS and GPT-4o. The earlier broader query-design discussion is replaced by a more focused account of language-driven segmentation and domain awareness.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation changes substantially: spatial-gating equations replace PTRM's softmax-attention update, and new CMCR and inherited regularization objectives replace v2's topology/anchor and masked-feature objectives. Appendix A.2 additionally defines cross-scale refinement for reduced hierarchy counts. These are substantive mathematical definitions, although neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

improvement.justification: V3 improves scrutiny through targeted ablations, clearer TQDM attribution and fuller implementation documentation. However, identical Figure 1 predictions change attribution from SemiVL to UniMatch V2 without explanation, ADE20K gains conflict with Table 3, and the new class-consistency mixture is ambiguous in A.3.2. The explicit CLIP-bias limitation also disappears. The PDFs cannot resolve whether key comparative evidence was corrected or misattributed, so the documentation gains and reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Despite the new title and renaming HVL to HVLFormer, both PDFs describe the same research lineage and four segmentation benchmarks. All pages, tables, figures and equations were readable. V2 ends with references; v3 includes a seven-page supplement.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark results, expanded component and sensitivity experiments, qualitative predictions, and an appendix pixel-text alignment evaluation.

before.justification: V2 reports original segmentation results on four datasets, class-wise IoUs, component and loss ablations, and qualitative predictions.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the central claims: domain-aware textual queries, image-conditioned refinement and consistency regularization improve low-label segmentation, with claimed state-of-the-art performance across the same four benchmarks. Their overall scope and novelty positioning remain stable.

C2.justification: Prompting improvements are now attributed to dataset attributes supplied directly to the VLM, replacing the GPT-4o enrichment explanation. V3's supplementary discussion of strong augmentations harming domain awareness and motivating reduced loss weighting is absent. The limitation involving small and distant Cityscapes objects remains.

D1.justification: V4 omits v3's dataset-attribute lists, implementation for fewer query hierarchies, confidence threshold of 0.95, segmentation-loss weights of 5/5/2 and regularization temperature of 0.07. It adds parameter counts and explicitly states supervised SRE training beforehand. Hardware, main training settings and the promise of future GitHub availability remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate semi-supervised semantic segmentation on Pascal VOC, COCO, ADE20K and Cityscapes. Additional backbone configurations and class-specific measurements do not introduce another dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: The comparison set is selectively reduced: v3 Table 3 includes PseudoSeg and PC2 on COCO and CutMix on ADE20K, which are absent from v4 Tables 2 and 4. Several UniMatch configurations also disappear, while the principal SemiVL, Pseudo-SD, UniMatch and TQDM comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Reported backbone settings change from EVA02-L to SigLIP2 for corresponding TQDM and HVLFormer rows, with additional EVA02-S evaluations and ViT-B TQDM controls. Training budgets, crops and the main mIoU metric remain unchanged. V4's ADE20K table changes its split headings from 158–2.5k to 232–3.7k images, contradicting its retained 158/316-label discussion; actual split changes cannot be established.

E4.justification: V4 removes the separate GPT-4o factor from the prompting study, adds chair/sofa/table IoUs across hierarchy levels, and reports SRE score statistics. Conversely, v3's full per-class VOC comparison, direct pixel–text alignment analysis in Appendix A.5 and extended qualitative cases are absent. These substantially change the evidence examining the proposed mechanisms.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over three random data-sampling seeds. Neither reports additional uncertainty intervals, dispersion estimates or significance tests. The new SRE score summary describes model outputs rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Numerous reported entries change: ViT-B VOC-92 mIoU becomes 87.3 instead of 85.4, and the PTRM ablation becomes 84.1/52.3 instead of 83.1/50.3 on VOC-92/COCO-232. EVA02-S results and hierarchy-specific class IoUs are added. The previous EVA02-L result vectors reappear unchanged under SigLIP2 labels. Changed method and backbone descriptions prevent interpreting these revisions as controlled same-setting gains.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces frozen GPT-4o generation of four descriptions per class and averaging their text embeddings with direct encoding of a learnable dataset-aware prompt, tk = ET(pk). The architecture diagram also removes the MLLM and averaging stages. This substantially changes query construction, while HQG, SRE, PTRM and CMCR remain.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. Localized rewrites update the abstract, prompting description, query-hierarchy explanations and experimental discussion, with keywords and affiliation formatting added. The scientific omissions are more substantial than the changes to the main narrative.

P2.justification: V4 replaces the two-column format with a single-column layout, redraws the architecture diagram and combines v3 Figures 1 and 3 into Figure 2. The multi-dataset table is split, parameter-count and class-IoU columns are added, and the supplementary tables and five qualitative figures are absent.

R1.justification: V4 newly cites SigLIP2 and Dong et al.'s MaskCLIP work, while GPT-4o, PC2 and several supplement-related references disappear. Much bibliography shortening reflects consolidation or metadata changes. The substantive positioning against SemiVL and TQDM remains largely unchanged.

T1.justification: The averaged MLLM-derived embedding definition is replaced by direct prompt encoding. More substantially, v3's supplementary cross-scale refinement equations and explicit CMCR, segmentation and regularization loss definitions are absent from v4, which retains aggregate objectives and supplementary references. This reduces the documented mathematical specification; it does not establish removal of those losses from training.

improvement.justification: V4 adds useful model-size comparisons, parameter counts and class-specific hierarchy results. However, the supplied version omits essential loss definitions, reproducibility settings and direct alignment validation while continuing to reference supplementary material. Its ADE20K split headings also contradict the text. These losses substantially weaken the ability to reproduce and verify the central method, outweighing the added comparisons.

A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same HVLFormer work, with matching authors, architecture and benchmarks. The complete supplied files support comparison: v3 includes supplementary Sections A.1–A.5 and additional figures, whereas v4 ends after its references. Judgments concern these supplied contents, without assuming what an unprovided supplement contains.

after.justification: V4 reports original segmentation results across four datasets, multiple model configurations and component analyses in Tables 1–8.

before.justification: V3 reports original segmentation results, component ablations and qualitative comparisons in Section 4, plus pixel–text alignment measurements in Appendix A.5.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a procedurally extensible 60-task embodied-memory benchmark, hierarchical VLM/navigation evaluations, and diagnostic efficiency metrics. The three introduction contribution statements retain their meaning. Explicitly mentioning fine-tuned open-source models in v2's abstract highlights an approach already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 corrects the SC-SR/DTG-SR interpretation in Section 5, distinguishing distant-but-visible receptacles from nearby targets. Appendix B.4 newly explains that retaining a valid goal frame does not preserve the context needed to select it. The transfer results receive a sim-to-real interpretation. Appendix A's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B.5 and F provide substantial new reproducibility information: DeepSeek-based trace-generation and rephrasing prompts, filtering rules yielding 72,973 labeled samples, data mixtures, frame budgets, hardware, optimization settings, and checkpoint selection. These document the added training pipelines; the PDFs do not establish newly released code or data.

E1.justification: v2 adds Video-R1-CoT-165k and Video-R1-260k training data and evaluates transfer to real-world egocentric video reasoning on VSI-Bench, including multiple-choice and numerical questions. This extends coverage beyond the retained simulated embodied-navigation tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds GLM-4.1V-Thinking to the existing FindingDory comparison (Figure 2 and Table 4). The new transfer comparison also introduces zero-shot, Video-R1-only SFT, and Video-R1-only GRPO controls against FindingDory-augmented training (Table 3), substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces protocols for 2,490 multiple-choice and 2,640 numerical questions, with 48-frame SFT training/inference and 32-frame GRPO training with 64-frame inference, distinct budgets, and checkpoint selection rules. Separately, the main-text training count changes from 82,174 to 79,213, while v2 Appendices B.1 and D.5 retain 82,174; the actual dataset-size change is unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled comparisons with and without FindingDory training to investigate transfer, alongside mixing-ratio and frame-count sensitivity findings in Appendix F. Appendix B.4 explicitly tests whether 96-frame subsampling removes valid goal frames. The original frame-count, navigation-error, sanity-check, and qualitative analyses are retained, although some move.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed estimates, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests, or comparable uncertainty measures. The new results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing Figure 2 scores are retained; GLM's 23.49% overall success is added. New Table 3 reports SFT MCQ accuracy of 35.06 with FindingDory versus 33.33 without it, but numerical accuracy of 32.35 versus 32.67. GRPO reports 35.42/34.82 versus 33.57/33.90 for MCQ/numerical accuracy. These are newly evaluated training conditions, absent from v1. Appendix B.4 also adds approximately 1% solvability loss after subsampling.

M1.justification: The original benchmark construction and hierarchical agents remain. Beyond v1's goal-index supervised fine-tuning, v2 adds an oracle-conditioned reasoning-trace generation, rephrasing, and filtering pipeline, plus GRPO co-training with a custom goal-frame precision reward (Appendices B.5 and F). These substantially extend the training procedures.

P1.justification: v2 substantially condenses and rewrites the benchmark description, merges the overview and task subsections, reorganizes the results discussion, shortens the conclusion, and moves sanity checks into Appendix B.6. These are extensive editorial and structural revisions beyond the newly added experiments.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column conference formatting, relocating and resizing figures and tables. v2 adds Tables 3–4 and Figures 6–9, updates Figure 2's series and legend, and swaps Figure 3's object/receptacle panels. Table 4 largely redisplays existing Figure 2 results, supplemented by GLM.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Video-R1, DeepSeek-R1, GLM-4.1V-Thinking, and vLLM/PagedAttention, while removing explicit ABO, Google Scanned Objects, and AI2-THOR references. The related-work discussion and positioning around isolating memory from exploration remain largely unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds a formal reward definition: zero for mismatched subgoal counts, otherwise the fraction of predicted frames belonging to their reference sets. Existing success and SPL definitions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper with real-world transfer evidence, an explicit subsampling-solvability analysis, clearer numerical reporting, and a corrected relaxed-metric interpretation. These provide useful validation beyond v1. The gains are limited by conflicting training-set counts and an overly broad 'consistent gains' description despite Table 3's slight SFT numerical-accuracy decline. Overall, the added evidence and clarification support a limited net improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FindingDory with the same authors, benchmark design, and task suite. Text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and added content.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds GLM evaluation, subsampling-solvability results, and original VSI-Bench transfer experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated-agent evaluations, supervised fine-tuning results, frame-subsampling experiments, and navigation failure analyses in Figures 2–4 and the appendices.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims of general-purpose distillation across heterogeneous token types, efficient student VLMs, and competitive benchmark performance. Removing one contribution bullet and replacing 'compatible' with 'agnostic' do not materially change those claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations supporting two decoder blocks and a practical 5M training subset, and attributes cross-tokenizer baseline weaknesses to padding/truncation and token matching. It removes Appendix G's qualification that answer-only distillation can accommodate different image embeddings when text tokenizers match. The original feature-alignment and regularization explanations remain.

D1.justification: The hardware and batch-size disclosures change substantially. v2 also removes gradient-checkpointing and LoRA implementation details, including rank/alpha 64 and dropout 0.05, and drops the project-page link. It adds Recalibrator parameter/FLOP information and clarifies regularization propagation in Appendix E. Omitted optimization details do not establish that the underlying techniques were abandoned.

E1.justification: Table 5(g) adds text-only LLM distillation evaluated on MMLU, GPQA, and MATH, substantially extending the original vision-language task coverage. The original visual benchmarks and 9M training-data mixture remain; their dataset description moves to Appendix F.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds evaluated ULD and MOT cross-tokenizer baselines, InternVL2.5 teacher/student SFT controls, and additional LLM and VLM baselines. Conversely, v1 Appendix G's answer-only MiniLLM, DistiLLM, and LLaVA-KD comparisons disappear. Their original same-token comparisons remain in Table 4.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported setup from 256 to 8 A100 GPUs and effective batches from 16K/8K to 512/256. New experiments vary Recalibrator depth, training sample counts, positional embedding, teacher fine-tuning, and model pairings; the answer-only experiment is removed. These are reported setting changes, without evidence establishing reruns of the retained results.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds analyses of computational overhead, decoder depth, positional re-embedding, dataset scale, and SFT effects. These examine efficiency and design choices beyond v1's regularization and dataset-composition analyses, which remain. The answer-only distillation analysis from v1 Appendix G is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies independent-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results continue reporting point estimates; Table 5's averages summarize benchmark scores rather than uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical numerical results, while Table 5 adds substantial new results. For example, Table 5(f) reports four-benchmark averages of 69.4 for ULD, 70.8 for MOT, and 76.4 for GenRecal. Additional ablation and compatibility scores are new, while Appendix G's answer-only scores are removed; these are not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the two-decoder Recalibrator, pre/post projections, mixed student-question/teacher-answer features, alignment regularization, and three-stage training. Positional re-embedding already appears in v1. Expanded explanations and corrected KL pseudocode clarify the existing logit-based procedure; they do not establish a new method.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanation, training description, and extended related work undergo extensive rewriting. Validation and Recalibrator analysis are merged, computational analysis and a separate discussion are introduced, and the conclusion is separated. Dataset documentation moves to Appendix F, while Appendices G–H are removed.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive figure/table repositioning and resizing. Figure 1 moves before the abstract, a nine-panel Table 5 is added, and the Appendix G table disappears. Existing plots and diagrams are largely reused rather than replaced.

R1.justification: v2 adds word-embedding alignment literature as motivation, cites MOT and additional model papers, and directly positions GenRecal against cross-tokenizer methods. ULD was already cited in v1, so its publication-version citation is not a new research work. Some references disappear with removed material, while the broader related-work account remains.

T1.justification: Appendix E corrects the KL expression in Algorithms 1–3: the second operand changes from the hidden feature r_al to VLM-head_l(r_al), repairing the written loss definition. The newly displayed main-text equations otherwise restate existing computations; no new theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: The new cross-tokenizer comparisons and controls for depth, positional encoding, data scale, and SFT strengthen empirical support, while corrected KL pseudocode improves technical clarity. These gains are tempered by removal of the informative answer-only comparison, optimization details, and project link. The unexplained GPU/batch-size revision alongside unchanged Tables 1–4 also leaves reproducibility questions, limiting the overall improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenRecal, with matching authors, architecture, and principal experiments. All pages, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison. Material was matched across the layout change, including the relocated dataset description and the removal of v1 Appendices G–H.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Table 5 with computational measurements, ablations, cross-tokenizer comparisons, and additional LLM/VLM evaluations.

before.justification: v1 reports original GenRecal benchmark results, teacher–student comparisons, regularization ablations, representation analyses, and appendix experiments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims of general-purpose distillation across heterogeneous token types, broad model compatibility, and strong benchmark performance. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes distribution matching through KL loss from hard-target supervision through autoregressive loss and interprets the new ablation accordingly. Section 4.4 expands the representation-mismatch explanation and interprets the new cost comparison as supporting competitive training efficiency.

D1.justification: Reported hardware changes from 8 to 128 NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs, while training durations change from days to stage-specific ranges of 2–4, 8–11, and 4–6 hours. Table 7 newly documents ULD/MOT two-epoch budgets and GenRecal stage timings, materially revising resource and reproducibility information.

E1.justification: The training-data mixture, vision-language benchmarks, and MMLU/GPQA/MATH evaluations are retained. v2 Appendix F becomes v3 Appendix E with the same dataset composition and domain analyses. The added experiments use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 6(h–i) adds teacher comparison rows for InternVL2.5-78B, Ovis1.6-Gemma-27B, Qwen3-VL-32B, and InternVL3.5-38B, absent from the corresponding v2 Table 5 panels. The existing distillation comparator set, including ULD and MOT, is retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes reported effective batch sizes from 512/256 to 8192/4096, a substantial training-protocol revision. Table 7 also introduces comparative FLOPs and runtime evaluation. These reported changes do not establish that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds an autoregressive-loss removal ablation for two students across the existing benchmarks (Table 5) and a comparative training-cost analysis (Table 7). These targeted additions extend the retained regularization, depth, positional-embedding, dataset-size, and appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new benchmark averages and runtime measurements do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports averages of 55.0/59.8 without autoregressive loss versus 75.8/77.1 with it. Table 7 adds training times of 18.8, 22.2, and 25.0 hours for GenRecal, ULD, and MOT. Teacher reference scores are added; the earlier benchmark and ablation values are retained.

M1.justification: The Recalibrator architecture, three-stage training, autoregressive/KL losses, regularization, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 move from v2 Appendix E into the main text; projection-layer renaming and removal of unused Algorithm 2 inputs do not alter computation.

P1.justification: Localized revisions move Algorithms 1–3 into the main text, add a projection-layer subsection, reorganize the discussion, and simplify projection terminology. Most introductory, methodological, and appendix prose is retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a narrower single-column layout, extensively resizing and repositioning figures and tables. v3 adds Tables 5 and 7 and expands the former Table 5, now Table 6. Existing plotted content is retained, but dense table text becomes smaller.

R1.justification: The Qwen3 technical-report citation is replaced by the distinct Qwen3-VL technical report. Discussion further develops GenRecal’s relationship to ULD and MOT, while the main related-work section and appendix survey remain substantially unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 and the loss computations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations appear; the expanded alignment explanations are conceptual.

improvement.justification: The new loss ablation and comparative runtime evidence in Tables 5 and 7 modestly strengthen support for the existing method, while moving algorithms into the main text improves accessibility. These gains are tempered by smaller tables and unexplained hardware/batch-size revisions that are not linked to reruns of the retained results.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenRecal research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved from the appendix into the main text.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds autoregressive-loss ablation results and comparative training-cost measurements.

before.justification: v2 reports original GenRecal benchmark results, component ablations, representation analyses, and dataset-domain experiments, including Appendix F.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central cross-tokenizer distillation and performance claims remain. Section 4.4 and Appendix F explicitly restrict general-purpose applicability to open-weight teachers, while the rewritten conclusion adds that gains arise primarily from recalibration rather than the multi-stage recipe.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of nonlinear hidden-state alignment, teacher-head regularization versus feature matching, and gains beyond SFT or data scale. Appendix F states the closed/API-teacher limitation and SFT fallback; Appendix I interprets the results as transferring teacher error structure and calibration.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly discloses collecting correct teacher responses with more detailed reasoning before training. Appendix J adds baseline stage/data budgets, optimization comparability, and FLOPs/timing conventions. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and batch settings remain documented as before.

E1.justification: The training corpus, represented domains, and benchmark/task coverage are retained. Appendix I pools MathVista, MM-Vet, MMMU, and AI2D, all already evaluated in v3. Newly disclosed teacher-response collection is described as applying to all experiments, not as added coverage.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds SFT-only as an explicit comparator to the retained data-scale study, unlike v3 Table 6(d). The named distillation baseline set is unchanged; Table 15 reports computational comparisons for methods already compared in Table 4.

E3.justification: v4 adds intermediate-checkpoint evaluations, alternative regularization controls, and pooled error/calibration evaluation using error categories, JSD, ECE, and wrong-answer confidence. Table 10 also describes random approximately 70% Stage 3 subsampling, conflicting with the VQA-removal procedure retained in Section 4.1(c). This is a changed protocol description, not evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 9 adds evidence separating Stage 2 gains from final SFT; Appendix H tests feature-MSE, KL-only, and CE-only regularization; Appendix I analyzes error structure and calibration. These substantially extend the analyses. Appendix G's component table consolidates existing ablations rather than introducing new ones.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added ECE and wrong-answer confidence values evaluate predictive calibration rather than uncertainty in the reported experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results. New entries include Stage 2's 74.3 average in Table 9, regularization alternatives scoring 71.7/73.5/74.6 in Table 13, error/calibration outcomes in Table 14, and baseline FLOPs/timings in Table 15. Several other added tables redisplay existing results, so they do not establish improved performance over v3.

M1.justification: The architecture and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. However, new Table 9 lists 'Recalibrator + Student' as trainable during Stage 2, whereas Figure 3(b) and Algorithm 3 in both versions indicate a frozen Recalibrator and trainable student body. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents a procedure change or an erroneous summary.

P1.justification: v4 extensively edits existing related-work, implementation, and validation paragraphs, condenses and reorganizes Section 4.4, and rewrites the conclusion. It also expands Appendix C, introduces Appendices F–J, revises the Section 3.1 heading, and updates author information.

P2.justification: Tables 8–15 substantially expand the presentation with decomposition, checkpoint, data-budget, consolidated-ablation, calibration, and compute displays; several reorganize existing results. Figures 4–5 are enlarged and the author block is reformatted. Existing figures and Tables 1–7 are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds discussion and citations covering newer VLM training, distillation, pruning, and agent work. Section 4.4 positions novelty in the stable teacher-head distillation recipe, and the acknowledgements identify X-Token as follow-up work. Publication updates to existing references are not new research additions.

T1.justification: Table 13 newly specifies a squared feature-distance objective for the alternative MSE regularizer. The original Equations (1)–(2) and default loss formulations remain unchanged; no new proofs or formal guarantees are added.

improvement.justification: The added checkpoint and regularization evidence, explicit teacher-access limitation, and training disclosures improve interpretability. However, Table 9 conflicts with the retained Stage 2 freezing scheme, and Table 10 conflicts with the retained Stage 3 data-selection description. These unresolved inconsistencies concern the procedure underlying the results, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenRecal and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably, including Appendices A–E and v4's additional Appendices F–J.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds checkpoint, regularization-form, error/calibration, and computational-cost results.

before.justification: v3 reports original GenRecal benchmark evaluations, distillation experiments, component ablations, and training/data analyses.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains automated, query-conditioned visual-prompt ranking. v2 adds an explicit introductory claim of generalization to captioning, grounding, and classification, and strengthens quantitative headline claims, including Qwen2.5-VL's MMMU improvement from 1.9 to 3.8 points.

C2.justification: v1's limitations discussion concerning teacher strength, frozen-parameter reuse, and prompt quality is removed. The pool-size interpretation changes from acknowledging small degradations to asserting that individually harmful prompts preserve or improve performance. The recommended pool limit also changes from fewer than five to fewer than seven candidates.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies LLaVA-OneVision as the retrieval source for the closed-source models, specifies the API layer/color variants used in qualitative examples, and quantifies additional inference computation as 0.8 TFLOPs. Existing training-data composition, hardware, optimizer framework, epochs, batch size, and learning rate are retained.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from six to fifteen benchmarks. Table 1 adds MMStar and MathVista; new Table 5 adds CVBench, BLINK, Real-World QA, MMVP, COCO2017 captioning, RefCOCO+ grounding, and ImageNet-1K classification, substantially extending task coverage. The training-data sources remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the base models, FGVP, Circle, API, fixed-prompt retrieval, random retrieval, and MoE/GateNet. New Table 5 uses existing base-model and API comparators. VTPrompt and TVP enter the candidate-pool ablation, rather than being evaluated as standalone competing methods.

E3.justification: The main candidate pool changes from four API attention prompts to those four plus RedCircle and FGVP. Table 3 also changes the cumulative prompt sequence and tests sizes 1–8 instead of 2–8. Backbone sizes and the reported training budget, batch size, and learning rate remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing pool-size sensitivity study is revised to introduce a one-prompt condition and VTPrompt/TVP candidates, replacing the earlier expansion through additional attention layers. Retrieval comparisons, transfer analyses, and qualitative cases are retained. The new inference filter is not separately ablated.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 includes a statistical-significance section and appendix reporting five MMMU seeds, paired t-testing, a mean difference, standard deviation, and a p-value threshold. This newly documents repeated-run evidence; it does not establish an increase over v1's undisclosed run count. The reported mean gain of 2.06 points conflicts with Table 6's differences, which average 2.46.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 extensively revise AutoV and comparator scores, and Tables 5–6 add benchmark and repeated-run results. For example, LLaVA-OneVision's VizWiz scores change from 59.4 to 68.4 for AutoV and 58.7 to 66.9 for API. AutoV's changed pool and inference procedure prevent treating its revision as a same-setting gain. Table 4's closed-source results remain unchanged.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 adds an inference pre-filter that removes the candidate whose visual features are farthest from the others by cosine distance. The feature extraction, ranking architecture, pairwise reward loss, and highest-ranked-prompt decoding remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes to Loss-Oriented Ranking for Automated Visual Prompting in LVLMs, several analysis passages and headings are streamlined, and the supplementary material gains a contents list and reorganized training-data subsections. The main section sequence and much of the methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document switches from a single-column design to a two-column conference layout. Table 1 gains benchmark columns and revised color coding, Table 3 is transposed and redesigned, and Tables 5–6 are added. Existing diagrams and qualitative figures are largely retained but resized and repositioned; Figure 6's panels change from horizontal to vertical arrangement.

R1.justification: Related work adds an explicit distinction from RORA-VLM and Re-Align, contrasting internal prompt selection with external retrieval and model fine-tuning. References also expand for added prompt types, benchmarks, and statistical methods. The overall positioning remains adaptive visual-prompt retrieval.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same feature extraction, interaction, scoring, reward-loss, and attention-prompt mathematics. Assignment notation and explanatory wording change, but neither version adds formal theoretical results or proofs.

improvement.justification: Broader task coverage and explicit repeated-run evidence strengthen validation, but v2 removes substantive limitations and introduces unresolved numerical inconsistencies. Besides Table 6's incorrect mean summary, Table 1 lists InternVL2 MathVista scores of 58.3 and 70.5 while labeling the difference as 2.2. The added tasks' exact evaluation metrics are also insufficiently specified. These benefits and reliability concerns prevent a confident net-quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoV, despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

after.justification: v2 reports revised evaluations and ablations, additional benchmark results in Table 5, and original repeated-seed results in Table 6.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, retrieval and prompt-pool ablations, transfer experiments, and timing measurements in Section 4 and Tables 1–4.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. Totals cover reported usage only; unknown or launched attempts without usage may still have consumed tokens. Finalized known pre-launch failures are counted as not launched.

C1.justification: The central retrieval and automatic loss-ranking contributions remain intact. V3 adds prompt-engineering saturation and difficult human prompt annotation to its central motivation, and strengthens the conclusion to claim that effectiveness does not depend on individual prompts' intrinsic quality. The headline benchmark gains are retained.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations linking regression weakness to noisy absolute losses and list-wise weakness to optimization complexity. It interprets filtering diagnostics as stronger visual grounding and discusses teacher-scale efficiency tradeoffs. The practical pool-size recommendation changes from fewer than seven to fewer than nine candidates; v2's MoE-overfitting explanation is removed.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix C specifies the loss-annotation model as LLaVA-v1.5 7B and estimates the annotation workload at half a day on one A100-40G. Section 5.8 supplies token counts and component-level computational accounting. Existing training epochs, batch size, learning rate and training hardware remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 narrows reported benchmark coverage from fifteen to fourteen and removes POPE results from Table 1, although Appendix B still describes POPE. Other benchmark and training datasets are retained; v3 Table 2 matches v2 appendix Table 5. V3 also adds a query-only diagnostic on existing training data.

E2.justification: V3 Table 3 adds absolute-loss regression and list-wise ranking to the retrieval comparison previously reported in v2 Table 2. Fixed prompts, random selection, MoE and pairwise AutoV remain. The principal benchmark comparators—FGVP, Circle and API—are unchanged.

E3.justification: Several new evaluation protocols vary decoder layers, pre-filtering with six or eight candidates, strategy-teacher sizes of 0.5B and 4B, and pool size, model size and visual-token count for computational measurements. Appendix D introduces query-only and GPT-4o-judged filtering diagnostics. These substantially extend experimental controls without establishing changes to the retained experiments' training settings.

E4.justification: V3 adds substantial analyses of ranking objectives, layer selection, inference pre-filtering, computational scaling, language-prior filtering and teacher scale. These test previously unexamined design choices and assumptions. Conversely, v2's ten-case appendix retrieval gallery is omitted, although two examples reappear in v3 Figure 1.

E5.justification: The paired t-test reporting and five MMMU runs with seeds 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 are unchanged. V2 Appendix E/Table 6 becomes v3 Appendix F/Table 9, retaining the same reported mean, standard deviation and p-value threshold. No additional uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results for the new comparisons and analyses, including regression/list-wise average scores of 39.6/40.6 and query-only accuracy falling from 32.7% to 13.2% after filtering. Shared benchmark cells, closed-source results and prompt-pool scores remain unchanged. POPE entries are removed; revised cross-benchmark averages cover seven rather than eight tasks and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

M1.justification: The proposed AutoV procedure remains unchanged: frozen feature extraction, first-layer modality interaction, mapping networks, pairwise reward supervision, cosine-distance pre-filtering and highest-score selection. Regression and list-wise ranking are added experimental alternatives rather than replacements for the proposed method.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, retrieval-comparison discussion, efficiency discussion and conclusion are substantially revised. Analysis becomes a separate main section, related work receives numbered subsections, and the appendices are reorganized. This exceeds simple renumbering or prose added solely for new experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, extensively restyles tables and redraws Figure 1 as a two-panel motivation figure. Extended benchmark results move from the appendix to main Table 2, new analysis tables are added, and the appendix retrieval gallery is removed. Table 1 drops POPE and average columns.

R1.justification: V3 adds the original Gemini technical report and removes VisionZip and SparseVLM references. Related work places greater emphasis on diminishing returns from prompt engineering and complementary prompt retrieval. Most cited work and the distinction from external retrieval-augmented methods are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), including feature extraction, scoring, pairwise reward loss and attention-prompt construction, are retained. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new analyses are empirical.

improvement.justification: The new ranking comparisons, component ablations and language-prior diagnostics give the unchanged method better empirical justification, while annotation-cost details improve transparency. The net gain is limited by removal of POPE evaluation and incomplete consistency checks: Appendix B still lists POPE, and the retained five-seed gains average 2.46 points although the statistical summary reports 2.06.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoV and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite the revised title, substantial reformatting and relocation of results.

after.justification: V3 retains original evaluations and adds ranking comparisons, component ablations, computational measurements and training-data diagnostics.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, retrieval comparisons, prompt-pool experiments, transfer results and repeated-seed measurements, including in its appendices.
