M1.justification: Both versions use a Cellpose-inspired flow predictor with foreground probabilities and a SAM-pretrained ViT-Base backbone, alongside SDXL adaptation using LoRA and learned tokens. v2 newly explains size-model removal, LSJ augmentation and CUDA flow computation as adaptations of Cellpose; it does not establish that these replace a different procedure in v1. Renaming UniEM-Net to UniAIMS is not an algorithmic change.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark discussion and implementation/prediction appendices are extensively rewritten. Dataset construction moves before methodology, the flow explanation expands into dedicated appendix sections, and Open Problems becomes a separate section. Dataset/model terminology, authorship text and citation presentation also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with substantial resizing and relocation of displays. v2 adds annotation, transfer and codebase tables and subgroup, hardware and memory figures. The retained pretraining and t-SNE plots are merged into Figure 6; prediction grids are revised, generated examples expanded, and attribute charts redrawn.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of query-based segmentation, adds OmniScience and privacy/data-sharing literature, and explicitly positions UniAIMS as an implementation adaptation of Cellpose. The underlying materials-dataset gap and principal research lineage remain, making this a bounded expansion and refinement of positioning.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theorems, proofs or substantive formal derivations. v2 Appendix 8 expands the explanation of existing Cellpose flows, scale normalization and reconstruction. The AP formula is retained; distinguishing it from COCO-style AP is clarification rather than a new mathematical definition.

improvement.justification: v1 describes expert annotation review without measuring its reliability; v2 supplies a 300-image independent-annotation audit and stagewise agreement results, addressing an important evidence gap for a dataset paper. Explicit failure conditions, clearer Cellpose attribution and fuller protocol documentation substantially strengthen credibility and interpretation. New reporting flaws temper the gain: the blanket zero-shot superiority claim conflicts with EMPS scores of 0.89 versus 0.92 in Table 5, and the revised 84.9% SEM figure contradicts retained 'over 90%' prose. These flaws do not outweigh the central validation improvements.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dataset, segmentation baseline and diffusion-model project, renamed from UniEM-3M/UniEM-Net to EM3M/UniAIMS. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including tables and rendered figures, and support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation and generation experiments and adds annotation-agreement measurements, external-dataset evaluations and supplementary performance analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation benchmarks, real-versus-synthetic training experiments, generative-model evaluations and dataset analyses, including Tables 2-4.

C1.justification: The first unified sparse-tracking HOI framework claim remains. However, the abstract, introduction and conclusion replace the conveyor-inference contribution with smooth inpainting, remove the standalone novelty claim for the head-centric representation, and explicitly add robustness claims concerning intermittent hand tracking and sensor noise.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of overlap blending and training stability, interprets substantial hand-tracking degradation as emerging around 75% missing input, and refines limitations concerning dynamic environments, finger detail and missing RGB-based datasets. The central interpretations about contacts connecting modalities and AMASS supplying human-motion priors remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation: rotary embeddings, AMASS conditioning tokens, guidance weights and update scale, a 30-frame overlap, and blending factor 0.4 are specified. Loss weights, training hardware and timing reports are revised; inference timing now includes guidance. Both versions still promise future code and model release.

E1.justification: BEHAVE, OMOMO and AMASS remain the principal training and evaluation datasets. v2 adds intermittent hand-tracking scenarios and qualitative evaluation on one Aria Digital Twin sequence with novel motion and objects (Figure 6), providing a limited extension of the existing HOI task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 substantially revise the comparator set. Standalone BoDiffusion disappears from both comparisons, and the original AMASS EgoAllo comparison is replaced by EgoAllo+H+O, which also enters the HOI comparison. BoDiffusion+Obj is retained as BoDiffusion+O; that renaming alone is not an addition.

E3.justification: Reported model size, training steps and learning rate change from 47.3M, 400k and 1e-4 to 57.7M, 300k and 5e-4. Contact accuracy replaces quaternion difference in Table 1. Sparse-observation percentages change from 1/5/10/25/100 to 10/25/50/100, and new hand-dropout protocols are introduced. Dataset splits, 30-fps processing and 60-frame training windows remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds hand-dropout robustness tests on both HOI datasets, a smooth-inpainting ablation, and NoAMASS evaluation on AMASS. It removes the NoAuxLoss and NoCan ablations from both dataset-specific ablation tables. Appendix Table S2 also extends the additional-modality analysis to OMOMO.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported aggregation for Tables 1–2 from four runs to three. Table 1 newly supplies uncertainty values for foot-contact scores. Both versions otherwise retain the same general mean-and-variance reporting approach.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced under revised models and settings. ECHO's BEHAVE MPJPE changes from 61.4 mm to 6.8 cm, object vertex error from 29.5 to 33.5 cm, and AMASS MPJPE from 93.9 mm to 7.4 cm. v2 adds contact-accuracy, dropout and additional conditioning results. Changed configurations and comparator membership prevent interpreting these as controlled same-setting gains or losses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 replace window-based canonicalization with per-frame head-centric representations and conveyor inference with smooth overlapping-window inpainting. Human root transformation is inferred through head alignment rather than diffused. Binary contacts become continuous, conditioning changes, and training uses clean/noisy modality combinations with synchronized noise. Appendix losses replace object vertex reconstruction with object-motion smoothness.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work gains numbered subsections, and the appendix gains a roadmap and separate implementation-details and metrics sections. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond edits required by the new experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figures 2–4 are substantially redrawn; qualitative comparisons are reorganized between Figure 5 and Figure S1 with an added comparator. Figure 6 and dropout tables are added, while existing tables receive revised columns, rows and captions.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions its representation as extending EgoAllo and its inference as extending HMD2, replacing the earlier conveyor lineage through Diffusion Forcing and The Matrix. Related work adds distinctions from EgoGrasp and WHOLE and expands coverage of recent egocentric methods. These change methodological attribution and positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

T1.justification: v2 revises mathematical definitions of human state, contacts and egocentric conditioning, changes the loss formulation, and adds explicit guidance and smooth-inpainting equations in Appendix Section 9. These substantially change the formal specification. The new skating equation, Eq. 18, sums consecutive joint positions, which appears inconsistent with its stated skating-penalty purpose.

improvement.justification: The dropout experiments, HOI-adapted EgoAllo comparison and fuller inference documentation provide a modest net improvement in empirical support and reproducibility. Benefits are tempered by removal of motion-only comparisons and two ablations, the apparent skating-equation error, and Table S2's blanket contact-conditioning claim despite better OMOMO object errors with human conditioning. These limitations prevent a clear substantial overall improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ECHO's sparse egocentric human-object interaction framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and included appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments, revised comparisons and ablations, hand-tracking dropout tests, and qualitative generalization on Aria Digital Twin.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on BEHAVE, OMOMO and AMASS, including baseline comparisons, sparse-conditioning experiments and ablations in the main text and appendix.

The introduction strengthens the novelty claim by explicitly stating that existing HOI methods cannot simultaneously learn motion priors and interaction dynamics from these data sources within one framework.

C2.justification: v3 attributes A-FT's degradation to the joint/tri-variate formulation rather than data access and explains BoDiffusion+O's lower BEHAVE penetration score through insufficient contact and floating objects. These are new interpretations; the limitations discussion is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 promises a future code and trained-model release. v3 states that both are available and supplies repository and project-page links. The existing implementation details and hyperparameters are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use BEHAVE, OMOMO, and AMASS and show Aria Digital Twin generalization. The added analyses use existing datasets and tasks; newly cited datasets do not expand the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: New Table S2 introduces ECHO A-FT as a training-strategy comparator, using AMASS pretraining followed by HOI fine-tuning. BoDiffusion+O and EgoAllo+H+O remain the external baselines; newly discussed related methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds the two-stage training control and evaluates minimum human-object distance, contact percentage, penetration depth, and penetration score. The existing experiments retain their splits, preprocessing, training settings, and inference procedures.

E4.justification: Two focused supplementary analyses extend the existing suite: joint versus sequential training, beyond v2's NoAMASS ablation, and quantitative contact/penetration analysis. Existing component ablations, missing-tracking tests, and conditioning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe the main comparisons as reporting mean and variance across three runs and use ± reporting. The added tables continue that convention without introducing new run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and v2 Tables S2–S4, retained as v3 Tables S4–S6, are unchanged. New results include A-FT's AMASS MPJPE of 15.9±0.7 cm and physical-plausibility measurements. On BEHAVE, ECHO has 79.5% contact versus BoDiffusion+O's 54.0%, while BoDiffusion+O has lower penetration score, 0.021 versus 0.037 cm.

M1.justification: The proposed ECHO representations, tri-variate diffusion architecture, joint training, losses, contact guidance, and smooth inpainting remain unchanged. A-FT is an added experimental control using the same architecture.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the introduction and related work, accompanied by grammatical corrections, clearer runtime wording, and affiliation and acknowledgment updates. The main section order and supplementary organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds supplementary Tables S2–S3 and renumbers the former S2–S4 as S4–S6. Figure 1 labels explicitly identify three-point tracking alongside sparse conditioning; retained figures and tables are resized or relocated without changing their underlying qualitative examples.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of IMU-HOI, I’M HOI, Glove2Hand, and other works, with fourteen additional references. It also sharpens distinctions from TriDi and the AMASS-prior strategies of InterDreamer and HOI-Diff while retaining the original research positioning.

T1.justification: The mathematical representations, diffusion objectives, losses, guidance, inpainting equations, and existing metric definitions are retained. The new physical metrics are introduced as empirical evaluation measures without new formal derivations or proofs.

improvement.justification: The new training control and contact/penetration measurements provide more direct evidence for claims previously supported by v2's existing ablations and qualitative comparisons. Expanded related-work distinctions and access information also help. The gain is limited: the same-architecture A-FT control supports joint training more directly than it isolates the tri-variate formulation itself, making the accompanying causal interpretation too strong.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECHO study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary Sections 6–10 are readable and support reliable comparison, including relocated and renumbered material.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds results for two-stage training and quantitative physical plausibility in supplementary Tables S2–S3.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments on BEHAVE, OMOMO, and AMASS, alongside ablations, conditioning tests, and qualitative results.

C1.justification: The central claim that specialized signing, fingerspelling, and lipreading experts improve translation through fusion remains. v3 extends the headline state-of-the-art claim to BOBSL and adds provision of generated pseudo-gloss and phoneme annotations for BOBSL and How2Sign as a contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning gating's suppression of irrelevant mouth signals, benefits of diverse pre-training, and the tradeoff between content-word accuracy and function-word reconstruction. Appendix C discusses instructional-domain bias, while Appendix E explains proper-name hallucinations and semantic drift through weak conditioning and LLM priors. v1's discussion was substantially narrower.

D1.justification: v3 adds exact glossing prompts, phonemization tools and fallback handling, parameter counts, fusion architecture dimensions, training schedules, LoRA configuration, hardware, computational costs, and decoding settings. These substantially expand v1's sparse implementation documentation. However, v3 contains conflicting descriptions of epochs, full fine-tuning versus LoRA, and training-time totals.

E1.justification: v3 adds training and evaluation on BOBSL, extending coverage from American Sign Language to British Sign Language and interpreted broadcast footage. YouTube-ASL, How2Sign, and ChicagoFSWildPlus remain in use.

E2.justification: Geo-Sign is newly included in the How2Sign comparison, having only been cited in v1. The new BOBSL comparison includes GFSLT, Sign2GPT, Albanie, Sincan, and Lost in Translation. Appendix B additionally compares concatenation/MLP and cross-attention fusion alternatives and multiple YouTube-ASL baseline configurations. The fingerspelling comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds zero-shot transfer and How2Sign-only training controls, standalone phoneme evaluation, and POS accuracy analysis. It drops BLEU-2/3 from the main benchmark comparison and no longer reports sequence-classification accuracy. Optimization is reported as AdamW rather than v1's Adam; most other newly supplied hyperparameters are disclosures, not established changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds fingerspelling, fusion, and sequencer removal ablations; standalone expert tests; alternative fusion comparisons; pre-training/transfer analysis; POS analysis; and label-length analysis. Qualitative cases are replaced and extended to BOBSL. Conversely, v1's quantitative comparison of random, frequency-based, keyword, and LLM glossing methods is removed rather than relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional v3 results continue to use point estimates.

E6.justification: Reported How2Sign BLEU-1/BLEU-4 changes from 46.0/23.5 to 49.4/22.1, while ROUGE remains 41.2 and fingerspelling accuracy remains 73.2%. The no-lipreading BLEU-4 changes from 16.6 to 13.6. v3 adds BOBSL BLEU-4 of 6.8, zero-shot 8.3, How2Sign-only 13.7, and numerous analytical results. These are revised or newly reported results, not established same-setting performance gains.

M1.justification: The expert-routing, CTC, gated-fusion, and LLM pipeline remains. v3 changes manual inputs from hand crops to full frames and changes the main-text gate from manual-only conditioning to concatenated manual/lip features (v1 Equation 10; v3 Equation 12). It also describes independent decoder training on generated gloss/text pairs instead of v1's final training on fusion outputs.

P1.justification: Beyond the title and model rename, v3 extensively rewrites the introduction and method, reorganizes the pipeline into numbered stages, and develops a structured appendix with a contents list and dedicated analysis and implementation sections. This is substantial narrative restructuring, not merely added experimental content.

P2.justification: v3 adds an opening modality illustration, redraws the architecture diagram, replaces the earlier routing visualizations with different translation displays, and introduces a POS heatmap and label-length plots. Comparison tables are restructured, and new appendix tables document analyses, configurations, and intermediate fused outputs.

R1.justification: v3 adds related-work coverage including SAGE, SLTUNET, hierarchical feature alignment, and Lost in Translation, alongside component references such as DINOv2, Gumbel-Softmax, and LoRA. The underlying positioning remains the absence of explicit fingerspelling/lipreading integration in prior SLT systems; publication and bibliographic updates do not constitute additional scientific changes.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a mathematical complexity comparison between O(T) gating and O(T²) cross-attention operations. Expanded CTC formulas mostly unpack losses already present in v1. Neither version presents a theorem or proof framework.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves important components and fusion choices weakly tested and provides few implementation settings. v3's expanded component tests, direct fusion comparisons, BSL evaluation, transfer analysis, and explicit failure discussion substantially strengthen the evidence and make the method easier to assess. Removal of the glossing-method ablation and inconsistent training disclosures weaken parts of the revision, but do not outweigh these substantial gains in scientific support and transparency.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same three-expert sign-language translation framework, renamed from MultiStream-LLM to SignBind-LLM. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials support a reliable comparison.

after.justification: v3 reports original results on How2Sign, ChicagoFSWildPlus, and BOBSL, together with additional component, fusion, transfer, and linguistic analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original How2Sign translation and ChicagoFSWildPlus fingerspelling results, component ablations, temporal-alignment experiments, and qualitative examples.

C1.justification: V4 adds prominent claims that performance advantages persist at matched 250M decoder scale and that training requires 259 GPU-hours, approximately 124 times less than SSVP-SLT. These architectural-attribution and comparative-efficiency claims become central in the abstract, introduction and conclusion; the three-stream design and state-of-the-art claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 Appendix B.1 favors lightweight gating because cross-attention offers negligible benefit at greater complexity. V4 instead emphasizes cross-attention as the mechanism resolving variable temporal offsets. It also explicitly limits the lipreading stream to mouthings rather than grammatical mouth gestures and adds occlusion/resolution/motion-blur explanations for letter confusions. Semantic-drift failures were already documented in v3.

D1.justification: V4 adds routing-label construction, temperature annealing details, the BOBSL realignment source and a planned code/data/model release, while revising compute reporting. The supplied v4 lacks v3 Appendix D’s detailed prompts, phonemization fallback, optimizer/LoRA tables and inference settings. This substantially changes available reproducibility documentation, although retention in the referenced but unavailable supplement cannot be established.

E1.justification: Both versions use YouTube-ASL for pre-training and evaluate How2Sign, ChicagoFSWild+ and BOBSL, covering ASL/BSL translation and fingerspelling. Zero-shot YouTube-ASL-to-How2Sign transfer and How2Sign-only training already appear in v3 Appendix B.2.

E2.justification: The main How2Sign and BOBSL comparator sets are retained. V4 Table 3 omits Pannattee et al. and Gajurel et al., reported at 48.0% and 48.4% in v3. V4 Table 7 also omits several YouTube-ASL comparison configurations from v3 Table 9, including its joint-training block.

E3.justification: The decoder study changes from 1B/3B/7B Llama models to 250M/780M/3B Flan-T5 models, introducing a decoder-size-matched comparison with prior methods. The reported fusion transformer changes from six layers in v3 Appendix D.3.2 to four in v4 Section 4.3. V4 additionally reports fingerspelling precision and recall.

E4.justification: V4 adds a fingerspelling confusion matrix and revises the fusion comparison to test gating plus cross-attention. Component removal, stand-alone experts, decoder variation, temporal offsets and transfer analyses already existed in v3. V4 retains selected POS findings, but its referenced full supplementary analysis is unavailable.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Results remain point estimates; the added confusion matrix and precision/recall do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Reported best results change from 22.1 to 23.1 How2Sign BLEU-4, 6.8 to 7.0 BOBSL BLEU-4, and 73.2% to 73.6% fingerspelling accuracy. Component, temporal-alignment and stand-alone results also change, and new decoder-scale, routing-accuracy and precision/recall results appear. These are revised results under changed architecture/decoder settings, not established same-setting improvements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.5 change fusion inputs from expert logits to penultimate embeddings, explicitly discarding the expert CTC heads. Manual–lip sigmoid mixing is replaced by manual-query/lip-key-value cross-attention; cross-attention was previously an alternative ablation. The default decoder also changes from LLaMA-2-7B to Flan-T5-XL.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Related work contracts from four subsections to two, ablations become a separate main section, and selected supplementary analyses are integrated into the main narrative.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a single-column layout and redraws both overview diagrams. Table 1 gains decoder, parameter and compute columns; fusion/pre-training tables are consolidated; selected v3 supplementary examples are reformatted into Table 4; and a new confusion-matrix figure appears. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting Flan-T5, improved BOBSL alignment and the linguistic rationale for fusion, while dropping several background and omitted-baseline references. The central positioning around jointly modeling signing, fingerspelling and lipreading remains. Related-work compression is primarily a structural revision.

T1.justification: The fusion definitions are substantively revised: v3 Equations 10–12 project logits and apply sigmoid mixing, whereas v4 Equations 8–12 project embeddings and define multi-head cross-attention with residual/FFN processing. This changes the mathematical formulation, but adds no theorem or proof.

improvement.justification: Matched-decoder comparisons and clearer fusion documentation strengthen v4. However, its unavailable supplement prevents checking the retention of detailed reproducibility and limitation evidence. New inconsistencies also weaken reliability: Table 7 gives gated fusion 22.3 BLEU-4 while the prose says 23.1, and Table 3 implies a 2.5-point fingerspelling advantage despite the claimed 2.1 points. These benefits and unresolved problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SignBind-LLM, and their main text, equations, figures and tables are readable. However, v3 includes supplementary Sections A–F, while v4 ends after its references despite repeatedly referring to supplementary material. Comparison of those later supplementary details is therefore limited.

after.justification: V4 reports original benchmark results, decoder-scale comparisons, component and fusion ablations, and a fingerspelling confusion matrix.

before.justification: V3 reports original translation and fingerspelling results on How2Sign, BOBSL and ChicagoFSWild+, with ablations, linguistic analyses and qualitative examples in the main text and supplement.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the first fully quantized intermediate-fusion system, near-full-precision accuracy, 3.2-fold latency reduction, a +9.5 mAP30 gain, and improved scaling under memory constraints. New experiments support these existing claims; the revised conclusion emphasizes the deployment focus already present in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix D.5 adds a focused explanation of rounding-bias accumulation and complementary AdaRound/alignment roles, including stronger language about reaching a globally optimized state. Appendix E.2 acknowledges that intertwined online error sources limit attribution. Existing V2X-ViT and 2-bit limitations remain discussed, although the dedicated main-text limitations paragraph is removed.

D1.justification: v2 explains how codebook weights are generated through Gumbel-Softmax, explicitly specifies nL=128 and nR=1, and documents Gaussian positional/heading perturbations for the retained robustness experiment. It also describes ROS-bag packaging for online evaluation. These improve documentation; the established hardware, training budgets, and promised code release remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds online perception evaluation through ROS-bag streaming on V2X-ReaLO across V2V, I2I, and V2I modes (Appendix E.2, Table 12). This substantially extends evaluation beyond static and simulated-latency accuracy settings. v1 already discussed the deployment platform and measured latency, but did not report this online accuracy evaluation.

E3.justification: New protocols include INT2/8 evaluation, AP70 assessment by distance, four system configurations across three fusion architectures, and offline-versus-online evaluation on V2X-ReaLO. Existing training/calibration budgets and the simulated communication-delay protocol remain unchanged. These additions substantially expand evaluation design without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained calibration, alignment, codebook, and pose-error studies, v2 adds computation-versus-communication decomposition (Figure 6), a 2-bit failure test (Table 5), and analyses of AdaRound/alignment complementarity using strict localization metrics and naive-rounding controls (Tables 10-11). These directly test previously underexamined component roles and operating limits.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averaging latency over 10 runs, in v1 Appendix D.1 and v2 Appendix E.1. v2 adds no seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Most matched results remain unchanged, including Tables 1-3 and power measurements. v2 adds online QuantV2X mAP30/50 results of 50.1/40.1, 58.0/45.7, and 45.9/36.6 for V2V, I2I, and V2I, plus decomposition and alignment results and INT2/8 AP30/50 of 40.8/37.0. One retained codebook-ablation value changes: system mAP50 for 128 codes and one selection rises from 41.9 to 42.2 (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 14), matching the main table.

M1.justification: The three-stage pipeline, codebook objectives, calibration algorithm, and heterogeneity/spatial alignment losses remain unchanged. Section 2.3 newly explains Gumbel-Softmax training weights and hard inference selections, but does not establish a change to the previously described procedure.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 moves related work into the appendix, places references before the appendices, reorders model-level appendix material, and makes localized explanatory and terminology edits. It also updates author/contact information and adds acknowledgements.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different document template with changed typography, margins, headers, and float placement. It redraws the overview, adds the two-panel decomposition Figure 6 and Tables 5 and 10-12, and rearranges retained displays. The scaling plot's axis notation changes from mAP0.3 to equivalent mAP30 without changing its results.

R1.justification: v2 adds STAMP to the cooperative-perception discussion and bibliography. The broader positioning against communication-only optimization remains unchanged. Moving related work to Appendix A and updating citation styles or publication metadata do not introduce additional substantive positioning changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(10) are retained, with only equivalent notation changes. The new computation-latency grouping restates the existing latency decomposition. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

improvement.justification: v1 supported deployment claims mainly through measured timing and simulated-latency accuracy. v2 adds online streaming evaluation across three collaboration modes and controls testing model/communication contributions and alignment at stricter precision thresholds. This substantially strengthens the central deployment argument and exposes operating limits. The new global-optimization language exceeds the formal evidence, and online attribution remains confounded, but these limitations do not outweigh the improved experimental support.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QuantV2X and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite substantial reformatting, renumbering, and relocation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds online V2X-ReaLO evaluation, system-component comparisons, and further quantization and alignment ablations.

before.justification: v1 reports original perception experiments on DAIR-V2X, V2X-Real, and OPV2V, together with quantization ablations, latency measurements, and power measurements.

C1.justification: The claimed contribution changes from a three-metric framework to a two-metric protocol with a human study as an explicit additional contribution. v2's conclusion claims human validation of the automated metrics, while removing v1's conclusion that decay rates matter as much as initial scores. The central case for cyclic evaluation remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that understanding generally exceeds generation fidelity and that MGG reflects human judgments better than single-pass GenEval. It removes SDR-based interpretations of decay rates and later-generation behavior. Existing explanations involving compositional binding, BAGEL's scale/training, and LLaVA+SDXL's semantic weaknesses largely remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code-release statement from a future promise to reported availability at the same repository. Model parameter counts and generation resolutions are retained. The new human-study procedure is described, but sample and annotator counts remain undisclosed; repository availability was not independently checked.

E1.justification: ND400 becomes Nocaps+Docci400, retaining the described sampling of 200 NoCaps and 200 DOCCI pairs. GenEval Rewritten and the I2T/T2I tasks remain. Human ratings add an assessment procedure, without documenting an additional dataset, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: The seven evaluated model systems remain unchanged. However, v2 Figure 13 adds an explicit comparison of single-pass GenEval against MGG through their correlations with human rankings, providing a new comparative validation of the proposed metric.

E3.justification: v2 drops SDR from the evaluation metrics and introduces a substantial human-evaluation protocol: independent ratings of generation-1 outputs, hidden model identities, separate understanding/generation rankings, and Good/Medium/Poor fidelity categories (Section 3.3). The existing cyclic evaluations retain their stated datasets, embedding backbones, model sizes, and resolutions.

E4.justification: v2 adds human validation of automated metrics, an analysis of understanding-versus-generation fidelity, and nine annotated fidelity combinations in Appendix F. Conversely, v1's SDR decay-curve analysis and fitted-parameter table are removed entirely. The CLIP-backbone and six-category GenEval analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 adds Pearson correlations, R-squared values, and shaded regression bands in Figures 12–13. The bands' estimation procedure and confidence level are unspecified. Multiple independent annotators are mentioned without counts or agreement statistics; neither version reports seeded-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Similarity curves and overall/category GenEval scores are extensively revised. For example, BAGEL's generation-1 and generation-19 overall scores change from 0.99/0.88 in v1 Figure 8 to 0.90/0.70 in v2 Figure 7. v2 also adds human results, including correlations of -0.821 for MGG versus -0.753 for GenEval. The PDFs do not explain the benchmark-score replacements, so these are reported revisions rather than established performance gains or losses.

M1.justification: v2 removes SDR's power-law fitting and parameter aggregation from the proposed evaluation framework. The alternating generation procedure and MCD/MGG computations remain unchanged; renaming UCF-UM to SDP does not itself change the method. No model architecture or training modification is documented.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it distinguishes cross-consistency from semantic drift, rewrites the introduction and findings, moves unified-model literature discussion into Appendix B, restructures the appendices, and places references before them. Framework and dataset terminology are revised throughout.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, with redesigned diagrams and replotted charts, revised legends and generation axes, and different heatmap colors. The experimental-summary table and SDR displays disappear; human-rating plots, correlation plots, and illustrated appendix cases are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including BLIP-2, X-Former, PixArt-alpha, Safe-LLaVA, HumaniBench, SB-Bench, and ALM-Bench, modestly broadening the research context. It also replaces the unrelated Reiter–Belz GENEVAL reference with Ghosh et al.'s object-focused GenEval. Positioning relative to Bahng et al.'s cycle-consistency work remains essentially unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 removes the SDR definition y = alpha times g to the power of minus beta, plus gamma, its parameter interpretations, and the parameter-averaging construction from v1 Section 3.2. The chain definitions and MCD equations remain equivalent. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

improvement.justification: Human ratings and correlations add useful validation absent from v1, and GenEval attribution is corrected. However, v2 omits human-study sample and annotator counts, replaces many benchmark scores without explanation, and introduces reporting inconsistencies: Figure 9's caption states 10% for a BAGEL error category whose plotted cell shows 5%. These unresolved reliability issues prevent a confident judgment of net quality improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Telephone Game evaluation work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching renamed methods and relocated material.

after.justification: v2 reports cyclic-generation results and adds original human fidelity ratings, model rankings, correlations with automated metrics, and annotated examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original cyclic-generation experiments on seven models, numerical similarity and GenEval results, fitted drift parameters, and qualitative failure examples.

C1.justification: The principal SDP, MCD, MGG, benchmark and human-validation contributions remain. The abstract newly claims that degradation is typically catastrophic rather than gradual and specifies collapse within five generations for VILA-U and Janus variants, sharpening the characterization of failure.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive arguments that drift is not solely an embedding-alignment, recaptioning-prompt or detector artifact. It develops an irreversible-error and saturation interpretation, explains the generation horizon, and explicitly limits proprietary-model results to diagnostic subsets. Emu3's poor performance receives a resolution-related explanation.

D1.justification: v2 primarily lists model sizes and resolutions. v3 adds inference steps, guidance, temperatures and fixed-policy information; specifies 200 human-study examples, six annotators, two judgments per example and randomized output ordering; and supplies exact recaptioning prompts. It also updates code and benchmark access information and documents release of evaluation pairs.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image understanding and generation using NoCaps, DOCCI and GenEval-R. The new common/novel, simple/complex and smaller-subset evaluations reuse existing data and task coverage; additional models and scorer variations do not introduce new domains or tasks.

E2.justification: The seven primary systems remain, but v3 Table 7 adds Emu3, ChatGPT and Gemini in a shared small-subset comparison. Table 11 also adds Mask2Former and GroundingDINO as alternatives to OWLv2 in the detector audit, substantially broadening evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include 80-example diagnostic subsets, comparisons using 20 NoCaps samples and 20 GenEval-R prompts per task, controlled recaptioning-prompt and scorer substitutions, and detector agreement/F1 evaluation at early and late generations. v3 also introduces first-failure-generation measurement. Newly disclosed human-study settings do not establish that the original study was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained CLIP comparisons, category heatmaps and qualitative examples, v3 adds SigLIP2 scoring checks, a Show-o tokenizer ablation, prompt sensitivity, detector reliability, common/novel and simple/complex diagnostics, and semantic-collapse analysis. New joint human-fidelity heatmaps extend the analysis beyond BAGEL.

E5.justification: v3 Table 4 newly reports seed 42 for BAGEL and BLIP3-o. This is additional seed disclosure, not evidence of increased repeated runs. The existing correlation analyses and shaded regression plots remain; no new repeated-run uncertainty procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 7–12 add substantial diagnostic, comparison and robustness results. Human fidelity distributions also change: Figure 9 reports BAGEL's Good-Generation/Poor-Understanding frequency as 0% in v2 and 5.9% in v3. Most original benchmark curves and category heatmaps are retained, although some new summary values conflict with those plots.

M1.justification: The core SDP procedure, alternating text-first and image-first chains, MCD computation, and GenEval-R/OWLv2-based MGG remain unchanged. Alternative scorers, prompts and Show-o variants are introduced as validation experiments.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. The original Unified Models section and appendix related work are integrated into a main-text Related Works section, and the appendix is reorganized into numbered experimental and analytical sections. Retained findings receive substantial explanatory rewrites.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a substantially different document layout and adds numerous diagnostic and consolidated tables. Appendix correlation plots are combined and moved into the main text, human-fidelity graphics are redesigned, and six joint-fidelity heatmaps are added. Retained qualitative examples are reformatted into individual-page displays.

R1.justification: v3 adds explicit positioning against Uni-MMMU's coupled understanding–generation tasks, plus citations for Janus-Pro, Emu3 and additional evaluation research. Some earlier references, including DINO and MPNet, disappear. The central positioning around repeated composition versus isolated evaluation remains.

T1.justification: v3 Supplementary Sections 3.6–3.7 introduce a first-failure-time definition of semantic-collapse generation: the first generation at which a task's semantic property is no longer preserved. The original chain definitions and MCD equations remain unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.

improvement.justification: v3 improves validation and reproducibility through targeted scorer, prompt and detector checks and much clearer inference and annotation details. However, quantitative consistency worsens in places: new Table 6 gives VILA-U's text-to-text MCD as 0.336, while Figure 7 retains approximately 0.46, matching v2. These unreconciled summaries limit confidence in the expanded evidence, leaving a limited net improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Semantic Drift Protocol study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated or reformatted in v3.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional model comparisons, controlled diagnostics, sensitivity tests and a human audit of detector reliability.

before.justification: v2 reports original cyclic evaluations of seven systems, MCD and MGG results, human judgments and qualitative failure analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the central theoretical contribution from a claimed proof of signal/noise decomposition to approximate separation under a multiplicative assumption. The abstract also replaces the headline 'up to 75%' improvement with a seven-benchmark claim focused on visual perception and recent as well as earlier models. CARVE's training-free contribution and attention-complexity observations remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains gains in terms of perceptual task demands, scale normalization, and model capability. Its main-text limitations and Appendix J identify loss of global spatial context, demonstrate a depth-ordering failure, acknowledge nonlinear attention interactions and imperfect uniformity, and discuss the accuracy–inference-cost tradeoff. These materially qualify applicability beyond v1's discussion of excessive masking.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code link, specifies lambda=0.05, documents extended dataset splits and sample counts, attention-fusion settings, mask parameters, scoring procedures, and resource-measurement conditions. Hardware reporting expands from four RTX A6000 GPUs to an A6000/H20 allocation. These are substantial documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish that newly disclosed settings changed existing experiments or verify the linked code's availability.

E1.justification: v3 retains A-OKVQA, POPE, V*, and TextVQA and adds evaluated document understanding, chart comprehension, and science-question reasoning through DocVQA, ChartQA, and ScienceQA (Table 3). Appendix J additionally examines a BLINK relative-depth failure case; this is a single case, not a full BLINK benchmark evaluation.

E2.justification: SD-RPN is newly evaluated alongside ViCrop and CARVE in v3 Table 3, adding a trained region-selection comparator. The existing SAM, YOLO, CLIP, and three ViCrop variants remain in the corresponding TextVQA comparison, moved from v1 Table 3 to v3 Table 5. The comparator membership change is limited.

E3.justification: New protocols include sampled DocVQA validation data, ChartQA and image-containing ScienceQA test sets, EM/ANLS/relaxed/multiple-choice metrics, component controls, temperature variation, and resource measurements over 100 ChartQA samples. Appendix I adds Qwen3-VL-2B/4B and Gemma-3-27B-it configurations. The retained external-tool timing comparison is relabeled from GPU time to end-to-end inference latency with unchanged values; this is a reported metric revision, not evidence that those measurements were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls testing direct question-attention masking and internal attention modification (Table 4), multiplicative versus additive contrast and attention uniformity (Appendix G), decoding-temperature robustness (Appendix B.3), measured inference overhead, and a BLINK depth-reasoning failure analysis. These substantially expand investigation of mechanism, robustness, and failure conditions beyond v1's retained time-step, layer, masking, and prompt studies.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix H adds V* bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples and paired McNemar tests for all four original models. Table 11 adds means and standard deviations for attention-uniformity measurements over 500 images, and Appendix B.1 specifies a DocVQA sampling seed. The existing Figure 5 confidence intervals and ten-trial prompt study remain; their presence is not new.

E6.justification: Substantial new benchmark, ablation, newer-model, timing, memory, and failure-case results are reported. Existing values also change: Table 1's LLaVA-1.5-13B Tfull scores move from 76.5 to 76.9 on A-OKVQA and 70.0 to 70.2 on V*. Table 2 changes Qwen2.5-VL-3B's [20,25] V* score from 57.1 to 56.5 and LLaVA-1.5-7B's corresponding TextVQA score from 58.2 to 57.9. These are reported numerical revisions, not established performance gains from a changed method.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same general/task-specific attention extraction, regularized attention ratio, weighted fusion, top-p thresholding, top-K connected-region selection, masking, cropping, resizing, and final inference. Additive contrast and internal attention modification are experimental alternatives, not revisions to CARVE. Appendix I explicitly applies the unchanged pipeline to newer models.

P1.justification: v3 extensively condenses and rewrites retained introduction, related-work, attention-analysis, and results passages. Section 3 and its subsections receive clearer descriptive titles, 'Method Analysis' becomes 'Experiments,' and implementation, validation, statistics, and limitations receive expanded organization. This exceeds the structural changes attributable solely to added experiments.

P2.justification: The paper adopts substantially different typography, margins, headers, float placement, and table styling. Existing results tables replace green highlighting and parenthesized gains with bold/underlined rankings and superscript gains. Numerous new tables and two new case-study figures are added. The original prompt table and masking visualizations are retained and renumbered, not replaced.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused toward visual-token processing, attention-head methods, and trained grounding/zooming systems, adding discussion of CogCoM, CogAgent, Ferret-UI, and visual-explanation methods. v3 explicitly credits ViCrop as inspiration and introduces SD-RPN positioning. Earlier discussion and references concerning RECIPE, DistiLLM-2, BLIP-2, and other works are removed; retained works' publication updates are not counted as new research.

T1.justification: The decomposition becomes an explicit modeling assumption, and Appendix C qualifies uniqueness and the retained results as properties of an idealized model. v1's approximation-error bound, optimal-regularization proposition, and entropy-monotonicity theorem in C.4–C.6 are removed. Convexity and closed-form derivations remain. The computational analysis is retained with corrected numerical examples, including combined speedup changing from 1.24 to 1.19.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important evidential gap: new component and additive-contrast controls directly test CARVE's central design choices, while V* significance analyses support the large gains on a small benchmark. Broader evaluations, measured overhead, and a concrete failure case improve assessment of applicability and practical cost. Explicit theoretical assumptions and removal of overstated results also improve claim calibration. The decomposition remains an idealized model, but the paper now provides substantially stronger empirical support and clearer boundaries.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CARVE research, with matching authors, title, algorithm, and original experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, component ablations, statistical analyses, resource measurements, newer-model experiments, and a failure case.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, CARVE evaluations on four benchmarks, comparisons with other methods, and hyperparameter and prompt experiments.

C1.justification: v2 removes v1's claim to be the first layout-conditioned AR text-to-image framework. Its abstract and introduction add claims of transfer to standard next-token models and exposure-bias mitigation, while the contributions emphasize validation across multiple benchmarks. These materially revise novelty and applicability claims beyond the retained structured-masking and quality/layout-control contributions.

C2.justification: The main interpretation of masking and the quality/layout tradeoff remains. v2 adds explanations for exposure-bias mitigation, global-prompt disambiguation of overlaps, and complementary reward weaknesses: VQA can overlook inaccurate boundaries and false positives, while detection can neglect detailed semantics. It removes v1's speculation that a stronger AR backbone could close the image-quality gap.

D1.justification: v2 discloses SFT runtime of three days on eight MI300X GPUs, GRPO runtime of four hours on eight MI250 GPUs, reward coefficients, and which baseline results were imported or reproduced. Conversely, v1's approximately one-million-sample SFT disclosure and Qwen3-14B redundancy-filter identification disappear. Their omission reduces documentation and does not establish a change to the SFT sample count.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained LayoutSAM training data and LayoutSAM-Eval evaluation, v2 adds OverLayBench-Complex for densely overlapping layouts and T2I-CompBench for compositional generation, including numeracy and spatial reasoning. These broaden the evaluated input conditions and task requirements. Simple/Regular OverLayBench results are referenced but not supplied.

E2.justification: In the corresponding LayoutSAM-Eval comparison, v2 removes Ranni and Be Yourself and adds PlanGen, InstanceAssemble and SiamLayout-FLUX. The original SiamLayout comparator is retained as SiamLay-SD3. Additional reported comparisons include EliGen on OverLayBench and SDXL, PixArt-alpha, DALL-E 3 and Show-o on T2I-CompBench. PlanGen adds a direct autoregressive competitor absent from v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds Grounding DINO filtering requiring training-sample mIoU and precision above 0.9, increases the within-box layout-advantage weight from 1.1 to 1.2, and evaluates detection metrics on 895 selected LayoutSAM-Eval samples. It removes IS reporting and introduces OverLayBench-specific metrics and GPT-5.2-generated layouts for T2I-CompBench. The principal SFT and GRPO iteration counts, batch sizes and learning rates remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's HPS-versus-CLIP-layout ablation is replaced by an expanded analysis separating HPS, VQA and detection rewards. v2 Table 5 and Figure 6 test whether semantic rewards miss localization/false-positive errors and whether detection rewards sacrifice attribute fidelity. The retained masking ablation gains detection metrics and qualitative failure examples in Figure 5. Referenced supplementary tokenizer and weight studies cannot be inspected.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both present point estimates. The unchanged GRPO group size of four describes training rollouts, not repeated experimental trials.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces SMARLI's spatial/IR values of 95.33/69.08 with 95.55/74.81 under revised reward and training settings; FID remains 18.16. These are not controlled same-setting gains. New benchmark tables and revised reward ablations add substantial results, while the original masking-ablation values are retained. The expanded comparison also changes rankings: SiamLay-FLUX leads spatial accuracy and PlanGen leads FID in v2.

M1.justification: The layout reward changes substantially: v1 averages cropped-region CLIP similarities, whereas v2 combines VLM-based binary VQA scores with Grounding DINO mIoU and precision scores. This introduces new reward components targeting semantic consistency, localization and false positives. The tokenizer, structured masking and stepwise GRPO trajectory replay remain substantially the same; their expanded explanations do not establish additional algorithm changes.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Preliminary material moves inside Method, masking is organized around named principles, and experiments are divided into separate layout-to-image and text-to-image evaluations. Front matter also changes, including an additional author and affiliation, keywords and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. Figure 1 moves before the abstract with refreshed examples; Figure 2 changes its reward diagram; and Figure 3 revises the comparison grid. New overlap and ablation figures are added. Tables gain parameter counts and detection metrics, and the reward table separates VQA and detection components. The original ablation tables are matched despite renumbering.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions SMARLI relative to PlanGen, explicitly acknowledging an existing AR layout-generation approach and motivating improvements to interference and image quality. It adds discussion of InstanceAssemble and literature supporting the new rewards and benchmarks. The earlier TwFA/LayoutEnc discussion and citations disappear. This changes the novelty argument, not merely bibliography formatting.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 4 defines a new weighted VQA/mIoU/precision reward, replacing v1's prose definition of average regional CLIP similarity. This is a limited mathematical-definition change. The GRPO objective, tokenizer equations and overall advantage combination are otherwise retained, with no new theorem, proof or formal guarantee.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence beyond v1's single-benchmark, diffusion-only comparison: it adds a direct AR competitor, challenging overlapping-layout evaluation, and spatial metrics and reward-component controls that examine concrete failure modes. Its novelty positioning is also more qualified. These gains materially improve support for the central layout-control claims, rather than merely raising reported scores. Missing supplementary evidence, removed IS reporting and reduced training-data disclosure remain limitations, but do not outweigh the stronger main-paper validation.

A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of SMARLI, with identifiable corresponding methods, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement. However, v2 refers to unavailable supplementary Janus-Pro results, OverLayBench Simple/Regular results, and tokenizer/weight ablations, limiting verification of those additions.

after.justification: v2 reports original SMARLI evaluations on LayoutSAM-Eval, OverLayBench-Complex and T2I-CompBench, together with masking and reward ablations in Tables 1–5.

before.justification: v1 reports original SMARLI results on LayoutSAM-Eval, masking and reward ablations in Tables 1–3, and generated-image examples.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains NC-inspired feature disentanglement and alignment for multi-label label-skewed FL. The headline maximum gains change from 2.87% macro-AUC and 7.29% macro-F1 in v1's introduction/conclusion to 3.92% and 4.93% in v3's abstract/conclusion, without expanding the claimed task coverage.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges that the method does not lead in ChestX-ray14 micro-AUC and argues that its macro-AUC advantage indicates better minority-disease performance. It also adds explanations for ETF-only degradation and interprets the new attention maps as class-specific spatial selection. The existing clustering interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v3 documents spatial feature-map reshaping and fixed 2D positional encoding, specifies uniform model averaging in Algorithm 1, and assigns lambda1 explicitly to 1 for CIFAR-10 and 0.01 otherwise. v1 leaves these details absent or generic. These disclosures improve implementation specificity without establishing corresponding changes to earlier experiments.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic multi-label CIFAR-10 and DermaMNIST, PASCAL VOC, and ChestX-ray14 under the same eight label-skew settings. The new attention examples use existing DermaMNIST coverage; no dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain centralized training and the same six FL comparators: FedAvg, FedCurv, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, SphereFed, and FedLGT. FedMLP is newly discussed as related work but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Tables 5 and 7 add ETF-classifier-only controls to the DermaMNIST and CIFAR-10 ablation designs. The main benchmark settings retain the same client participation, beta/gamma configurations, backbone, training budget, optimizer, and metrics. Renaming overall metrics as micro metrics does not establish a metric change.

E4.justification: New ETF-without-LADM rows test whether fixed prototypes suffice without disentanglement. New Figure 5 provides DermaMNIST attention-map case studies supporting class-specific localization. Existing loss/query ablations, t-SNE plots, and cosine-similarity analyses remain, including their appendix counterparts.

E5.justification: v1 reports three-seed means and standard deviations only for CIFAR-10 at beta=0.5 in appendix Table 9. v3 states three-seed repetition generally and reports mean plus standard deviation throughout main Tables 1–4, substantially broadening uncertainty reporting. This does not establish an increase beyond three runs for the previously replicated setting; ablation tables still omit uncertainties.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 extensively revise reported scores and some rankings. For CIFAR-10 at beta=0.1, macro-F1 leadership changes from SphereFed (39.52 versus 38.14) to the proposed method (38.09 versus 36.83). Even the previously three-seed CIFAR-10 beta=0.5 proposed macro-F1 changes from 49.17 in v1 Table 9 to 48.17 in v3 Table 1. New ablation rows and attention maps add findings; these revisions do not demonstrate a same-setting implementation improvement.

M1.justification: The shared ETF, LADM, BCE, and two-regularizer design remains. However, v3 Equation 12 excludes a negative feature's own prototype, whereas v1 Equation 7 includes all class prototypes. Per-sample label averaging is also made explicit. The expanded spatial-attention specification alone does not establish that the underlying implementation changed.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and discussion are rewritten. FedNCAlign-ML becomes FedNCA-ML, sections and appendices gain numbering, the algorithm moves into the main method section, and detailed heterogeneous-FL related work moves to the appendix. This is extensive editorial restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redesigned to show label correlations and LADM internals, and Figure 5 adds attention maps. Main tables are reformatted for uncertainty reporting, with v1's appendix Table 9 incorporated into Table 1. Existing analytical plots are retained or relocated; captions and metric headers are also revised.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of FedMLP and positions LADM relative to DETR, while removing v1's specific criticism that MLC-NC does not address missing classes. The bibliography is unchanged, and new attributions contain unresolved citation placeholders. Existing heterogeneous-FL discussion is largely relocated to Appendix A.

T1.justification: Equation 1 corrects the ETF construction from I_C - J_C/(C-1) to I_C - J_C/C, making it consistent with the stated simplex geometry and inner products. The NC properties remain substantively unchanged, and neither version provides new theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: Broader uncertainty reporting, ETF-only controls, clearer implementation details, and the corrected ETF formula strengthen support for the existing contribution. The net gain is limited by unresolved citation placeholders, uncertainty-free ablation tables, and new text–table inconsistencies: Section 5.3 claims a 1.21-point ChestX-ray14 macro-AUC margin at beta=0.1, whereas Table 4 gives 71.28 minus 70.16, or 1.12 points.

A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same research work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching content across the method renaming and document reorganization.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, expanded uncertainty reporting, component and query ablations, and class-specific attention visualizations across the main text and appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original federated-learning comparisons on four datasets, component and query ablations, feature visualizations, and three-seed CIFAR-10 results in its appendix.

C1.justification: v4 adds an explicit contribution claim that class-wise attention enables NC alignment while preserving semantic relationships in the shared backbone. The central NC-inspired multi-label FL contribution, novelty claim and headline performance gains remain.

C2.justification: v4 acknowledges that a pooled embedding can encode multiple labels, then attributes difficulties under imbalance to entanglement and gradient interference. It adds explanations for preserving backbone semantic relationships and choosing stronger regularization during scratch training. The ChestX-ray14 micro-AUC qualification remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Figure 11 document the new COCO partition parameters, class cap and training/test/client label distributions. Existing optimizer, learning rate, training duration and loss-weight disclosures remain unchanged; no new code-access or hardware information is supplied.

E1.justification: v4 adds MS COCO evaluation, extending coverage to an 80-category natural-image benchmark with complex scenes and dense label co-occurrence, compared with the previous maximum of 20 categories. All four earlier datasets remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain FedAvg, FedCurv, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, SphereFed, FedLGT and the centralized reference. The added COCO experiment uses this same comparator set; newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The new COCO experiment uses beta=0.05 and gamma=0.75, allowing up to 60 of 80 classes per client. v4 also reports individual-class F1 for the DermaMNIST ablation. Existing benchmark settings, the 10-client design, backbone and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v4 Table 6 extends the existing DermaMNIST component ablation with per-class F1, exposing which classes benefit. Figure 5 replaces DermaMNIST attention examples with Grad-CAM examples on DermaMNIST and VOC. Existing component/query ablations, t-SNE plots and cosine-similarity analyses remain, including the appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs with different random seeds and report means and standard deviations for benchmark comparisons. The new results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds a complete COCO comparison: FedNCA-ML reports macro-AUC 94.10±0.18 and macro-F1 56.28±0.32, with the latter exceeding FedLGT's 55.68±0.83. It also adds seven-class F1 breakdowns and new Grad-CAM findings. All retained benchmark and aggregate ablation scores match; prose corrections include the DermaMNIST ablation F1 gain changing from 7.34 to 7.26 percentage points.

M1.justification: The LADM cross-attention module, shared fixed ETF queries/classifier, BCE and two regularization losses, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The explanation that ETF anchoring acts on class-wise features clarifies the existing procedure.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting, including a three-challenge narrative and revised contribution list. The separate related-work appendix is removed, dataset documentation moves before supplementary experiments, and missing citation references are repaired.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned, Figure 5 is replaced, the DermaMNIST ablation gains shaded per-class columns, and COCO results/distribution displays and CIFAR-10 sample examples are added. Numerous retained tables and figures are resized or relocated.

R1.justification: Section 2 introduces a local/post/pre-learning taxonomy and explicitly positions FedNCA-ML as pre-learning alignment. It adds discussion supported by works such as FedRS, model-contrastive FL and FedIIC, and clarifies FedMLP's partial-annotation setting. The original claim of first investigating multi-label FL through NC remains.

improvement.justification: COCO comparisons, per-class ablations and VOC Grad-CAM examples strengthen validation, while clearer explanations and corrected DermaMNIST gain calculations improve accuracy. These benefits are tempered by unnamed per-class columns and imprecise wording: v4 calls 30.27 the lowest per-class F1 although Table 6 also contains 23.83 in that row.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds original MS COCO comparisons, per-class DermaMNIST ablation results and Grad-CAM examples.

before.justification: v3 reports original federated-learning experiments on four datasets, component and query ablations, and feature visualizations, including additional CIFAR-10 analyses in the appendix.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same three central contributions: token-driven recurrent localization, SAM distillation without additional inference cost, and hierarchical RFEM. The central claims of state-of-the-art accuracy, fewer parameters, and competitive speed also remain. V2 expands supporting evidence and the recurrence rationale without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes attainable accuracy primarily to recurrence and treats complementary modules as improving the starting point. These are documentation and access-information changes; repository availability was not externally verified.

The original ground-to-satellite and drone-to-satellite dataset remains; its shortened name, CVOGL, does not denote another new dataset.

HALO is cited but has no reported comparison row.

V2 selects m=5 for both tasks, replacing v1's task-specific and inconsistent drone-step recommendations. Few-shot evaluation introduces pretrained-checkpoint fine-tuning with 28 training and 24 test samples. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

The existing step-count analysis is revised to examine validation performance and runtime. Component, RFEM, token-count, loss-weight, and backbone analyses remain, as do the existing attention visualizations and failure cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both present point estimates without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The headline drone Acc@0.25/Acc@0.50 changes from 78.21/72.35 to 77.60/72.05 under the revised step setting; the latter values already appeared at m=5 in v1. V2 revises portions of the motivation, related work, and experimental narrative, adds discussion subsections, moves metric definitions into the main text, and updates terminology, subsection numbering, authors, and affiliations.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning against recent CVOGL work, including TROGeo, GeoFormer, AttenGeo, and HALO. Additional citations support step selection, token scaling, and EdgeSAM; the PyTorch reference is removed.

improvement.justification: V2's validation-based step selection resolves v1's inconsistent drone-step recommendations and improves the reported evaluation procedure. improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for the central argument: stronger comparator coverage leads to appropriately narrower performance claims, loss and capacity controls better isolate WARM's contribution, and numerical-stability experiments and implementation details address previously unexplained whitening behavior. These gains improve evidential support and reproducibility despite unchanged benchmark scores. They outweigh the limited reporting losses, particularly the omitted FPS repetition/aggregation explanation and explicit backbone-freezing statement.

Appendix A.4 revises reported 50/20-epoch training times from 48/20 hours to 28/11 hours. These are added results and revised timing reports, not improved scores in the retained comparisons.

(7) replaces temperature-scaled Euclidean distances with normalized distances, explicitly excludes diagonal entries before softmax, and removes the explicit temperature. C1.justification: Despite renaming and rewriting, the principal contribution claims remain interference-aware graph-color scheduling, compatibility with existing optimizers, theoretical guarantees, gains across six main benchmarks, and the importance of recoloring and historical averaging. The expanded appendix evidence mainly elaborates and supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive interpretations of backbone-dependent benefits, refresh frequency versus noise/staleness, training-time grouping behavior, and TAG/sketching performance–cost tradeoffs. It qualifies gradient-energy guarantees by group size and discusses affinity-specific recovery limitations. Section 7.3.3 additionally extrapolates to generalization under distribution shift without adding a dedicated shift evaluation.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-access link and reproducibility statement describing preprocessing and configured training scripts. It also expands pseudocode and documents new experimental details, including synthetic timing procedures, sketch widths, the 0.1 TAG probe step, and three-epoch, batch-size-64 Taskonomy training. Repository contents cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

E1.justification: The original six benchmarks and auxiliary-task definitions are retained. v4 adds Taskonomy, including its Tiny subset, covering Euclidean and Z-buffer depth, occlusion and texture edges, keypoints, normals, curvature and reshading. This substantially expands evaluation on naturally occurring visual prediction tasks.

E2.justification: The nine standalone comparison methods in v1 Table 2 remain in v4 Table 1. Additional comparisons include graph-construction variants, SON-GOKU with TAG affinities, and a no-refresh timing control (Tables 1, 8–9). TAG is evaluated as an affinity replacement within the scheduler, not as a standalone grouping baseline.

E3.justification: The original benchmark settings are largely retained. New protocols include density-matched graph controls, synthetic timing workloads with 1024-dimensional gradients over 900 steps and varying task counts/refresh periods, and Taskonomy encoder-width and refresh-period sweeps (Appendices K, L and R). These are added evaluation designs rather than established reruns under changed original settings.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained static-coloring and single-step-history ablations, v4 tests alternative edge rules and density matching, approximation speed–accuracy tradeoffs, TAG affinities, and sensitivity to backbone width and refresh period. Appendix S adds task-group, conflict-density, convergence and graph-evolution analyses absent from v1.

E5.justification: v1 reports benchmark point estimates without empirical repeat counts. v4 adds ± values to retained results, standard deviations and repeated trials for timing/memory studies, two seeds for TAG evaluation, and percentile bands for graph statistics. Table 1 does not define its ± convention or run count; the PDFs do not establish increased replication of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Most original benchmark means remain unchanged. NYUv2 mIoU changes from 0.63 to 0.063 for MGDA, 0.65 to 0.065 for CAGrad, 0.69 to 0.069 for AdaTask, and 0.68 to 0.068 for scheduler AdaTask. v4 adds extensive ablation, Taskonomy, timing, memory and scaling results. For example, Table 8 newly reports depth RMSE of 18.6199 for cosine affinities versus 18.3034 for TAG; this is not a cross-version performance gain.

M1.justification: The core EMA, conflict graph, greedy coloring and cyclic update procedure remains. v4 restricts minimum-frequency task duplication to compatible slots (Section 4.4.1) and adds a tested TAG lookahead-affinity alternative to cosine scoring (Appendix P). Sketching options already appeared in v1 Appendix G.5.

P1.justification: The introduction and theoretical overview are extensively rewritten. Detailed related work, dataset descriptions and comparator descriptions move into appendices, existing proofs are reordered, and a reproducibility section is added. The title and author block change, and SON-GOKU replaces the generic scheduler terminology throughout.

P2.justification: The original pipeline figure is retained, while the performance table gains uncertainty entries and ablation rows and the dataset table moves to Appendix J. v4 adds numerous runtime, memory and Taskonomy tables, scaling plots, convergence curves and graph snapshots, and reformats the algorithm as numbered pseudocode. Table 11 redisplays the cosine results already in Table 8.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning against task-grouping approaches and presents the scheduler as compatible with alternative affinity estimators. Appendices P–R develop connections to clustered learning, gradient signal-to-noise and model capacity, adding works such as Jacob et al. (2008) and Michalkiewicz et al. (2023). Much earlier related work is retained in Appendix M.

T1.justification: v4 replaces the incorrect 1 - tau gradient-energy factor with 1 - tau(|S| - 1), introduces an aggregate conflict ratio, and substantially rewrites the convergence analysis. It also corrects EMA effective-sample-size calculations and randomized-class gradient scaling, and adds affinity and signal-to-noise derivations. Much of v1's graph-recovery and scheduled-versus-aggregated analysis is retained in renamed Appendices B–C.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects v1's group-size bound and adds useful controls, uncertainty reporting, Taskonomy evidence and reproducibility information. However, important inconsistencies remain: Section 5.2 attributes a tau-dependent convergence penalty that Appendix F no longer supports, Appendices D and N give unreconciled persistent-memory descriptions, and Figure 6(o) plots negative MSE without explanation. These affect central theoretical and efficiency claims and the credibility of new analyses. The benefits and reliability problems do not support a confident net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same interference-aware graph-coloring scheduler, renamed SON-GOKU in v4. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching material relocated between sections.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds original Taskonomy evaluations, runtime and memory measurements, additional ablations and training-dynamics analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across six benchmarks, including optimizer combinations and two scheduler ablations (Table 2).
