C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: grounded hypothesis-driven instance-level discovery, the GESD benchmark, detection/segmentation applicability, and actionable model repair. The headline P@10 advantage remains 0.73 versus 0.63.

C2.justification: v3 expands the explanation of data-driven hypotheses to include distribution-amplified rare patterns, interprets KD/DD results as complementary, and uses the matched-backend comparison to attribute gains to the framework. The conclusion's limitations concerning dataset coverage and incomplete hypothesis spaces remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Verified edits include disclosure of GPT-5.2 baseline implementations, confidence calibration and Spearman thresholds, addition of a face-dataset URL, and removal of the promise to release GESD upon acceptance. However, v2's prompts, hardware/runtime information and detailed repair settings have unavailable supplementary counterparts in v3. The overall extent of reproducibility-documentation changes cannot be determined.

E1.justification: Both versions retain GESD detection and segmentation using COCO, KITTI and face-detection data; Waterbirds, CelebA and NICO++ bias discovery; and detection/classification repair. NICO++ correlation settings remain 75%, 90% and 95%. The added comparisons concern existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a separately evaluated HiBug2 variant using Gemini-2.5-Pro alongside the GPT-backed HiBug2 comparator. FACTS*, HiBug*, and the comparator sets in the classification discovery and repair tables remain unchanged. This is a limited expansion through an additional baseline variant.

E3.justification: v2 specifies k=10 for all experiments; v3 makes it the default and additionally evaluates P@5 and P@20. v3 also introduces a matched-Gemini baseline control and KD-only/DD-only evaluations. Its newly disclosed GPT-5.2 baseline implementation does not establish that the corresponding v2 experiments used a different backend.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds an analysis of knowledge-driven versus data-driven hypotheses and their complementarity. Section 5.1 adds an aggregate FP/FN comparison with HiBug2. v3 also reports an FDR-control check and quantifies the Spearman alternative already mentioned in v2. Existing grounding, tag-comparison and threshold-sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: v3 explicitly reports a Spearman significance criterion of p<0.05 and stability under Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction, neither documented in v2. Tables 3–4 retain three repair repetitions and ten independent classification-repair runs with the same uncertainty reporting; no increase in run counts is established.

E6.justification: v3 adds P@5/P@20 results, including GH-ESD scores of 0.78/0.66, and Gemini-backed HiBug2 scores of 0.77/0.63/0.52 at k=5/10/20. It reports KD-only/DD-only/joint P@10 of 0.62/0.21/0.73, FP/FN breakdowns, and Spearman F1 of 0.78 versus slope F1 of 0.77. The HiBug2 slice count changes from 3,607 to 3,666. Existing P@10 and Tables 2–4 results remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding; supplementary results cannot be fully compared.

M1.justification: The documented core pipeline remains knowledge/data-driven hypothesis construction, grounded VLM matching, and sliding-window slope verification. v2 already reports evaluating Spearman alternatives; v3 specifies a multi-scale version and its thresholds without establishing a change to the existing algorithm. The default slope-based procedure remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammatical and explanatory edits, updates an author's name and affiliations, and fixes the suppressed-title running header. The main section sequence and narrative remain intact. Appendix A–D references become supplementary S1–S4 references, whose contents are unavailable for comparison.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands from one P@10 row to three cutoff rows and gains a HiBug2 backend column. Figure 4 is rerendered with minor label cleanup while retaining its examples and trends. Other main figures are retained, and several figures and tables move with text reflow. Supplementary displays cannot be compared.

R1.justification: The same 31 cited works remain. v3 refines VISLIX's description to emphasize expert interaction through ROI exploration and adds an argument that FACTS-style Bayesian correction assumes a stable tag space incompatible with open-ended hypothesis generation. These are limited positioning changes.

T1.justification: The shared main-text mathematical formulation, matching-score equation and slope statistic are unchanged. However, v2 Appendix C.5 supplies explicit repair-loss and GroupDRO weight-update definitions, while v3 directs readers to unavailable supplementary Section S3.5. Their retention or revision cannot be verified.

improvement.justification: The matched-backend control, KD/DD ablation, quantitative Spearman/FDR checks and corrected slice count strengthen the visible main text. However, v3's referenced supplement is unavailable, preventing assessment of the prompts, detailed segmentation evidence, repair formulas and implementation settings supplied in v2. These gaps prevent a reliable paper-level judgment about the net improvement in evidence and technical completeness.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GH-ESD and GESD, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v2 includes Appendices A–D, whereas v3 ends after the references and cites supplementary sections S1–S4 that are not supplied. Appendix-dependent comparisons are therefore incomplete; those references do not establish that the underlying content was deleted.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and model-repair results in Tables 1–4 and reports additional comparative and ablation outcomes in Sections 5.1–5.2.

before.justification: v2 reports original GH-ESD detection and segmentation results, component analyses, and model-repair experiments, including Tables 1, 3–4 and appendix Tables 7–8.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about grounded instance-level discovery, the GESD benchmark, detection improvement and segmentation applicability. The added dataset-availability statement does not redefine the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The supplement adds interpretations of limited sensitivity to LLM choice, the VLM efficiency tradeoff, and numerical-output instability versus categorical quantization. Section S3.3 also identifies the surfboard-on-land segmentation failure. The main discussion of dataset coverage and incomplete hypothesis spaces remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 supplies generation, matching and evaluation prompts; the HiBug attribute corpus; checkpoint provenance; repair hyperparameters and loss implementation; and A100/vLLM execution details. It also adds a public-availability statement and repository address for GESD. These substantially improve reproducibility information without establishing changes to existing implementations.

E1.justification: Both versions cover GESD detection and segmentation, constructed from COCO, KITTI and face-detection data, plus Waterbirds, CelebA and NICO++. The supplementary results concern these existing tasks and datasets, without establishing additional coverage.

E2.justification: Section S3.1 adds reported component comparisons using GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet for hypothesis generation, and SigLIP and GPT-4o alongside Qwen2.5-VL-7B for matching. The main slice-discovery and repair comparator sets in Tables 1–4 are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added matching-score experiment evaluates alternative score constructions using mAP on a benchmark subset, while Table S1 reports matching speed per 1,000 images alongside Precision@10. These augment the reported evaluation design; the original benchmark and repair settings are not reported as revised.

E4.justification: Section S3.1 supplies substantive additional analyses of LLM choice, VLM precision–speed tradeoffs and matching-score construction. The latter compares yes/no logits, numerical outputs and categorical responses, reporting mAP of 0.47, 0.23 and 0.18. These substantially extend the available component evidence beyond the retained Section 5.2 ablations.

E5.justification: Section S3.1 newly reports five runs for the matching-score ablation. Section S3.5 clarifies randomized seeds and standard-deviation reporting for classification repair. The existing three-repetition detection repair and ten-run classification repair reports remain unchanged; no increase in their run counts is established.

E6.justification: Tables S3–S4 add individual results for 21 detection and 21 segmentation slices, including segmentation average Precision@10 of 0.805 and one zero-scoring slice. Section S3.1 and Table S1 add model, speed and scoring-ablation results. Main Tables 1–4 are unchanged; detection Precision@10 of 0.729 is equivalent rounding of the retained 0.73, not a performance improvement.

M1.justification: The grounded hypothesis construction, VLM matching, monotonic verification and model-repair procedures remain unchanged. The supplement documents previously referenced prompts, implementation choices and the interactive tool; it does not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

P1.justification: The existing main-paper wording and section order are essentially retained. v4 adds an availability sentence and organizes supporting material into supplementary Sections S1–S4, without extensively rewriting or reorganizing the main narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures S1–S14 and Tables S1–S4: prompt panels, dataset-distribution plots, detailed result and attribute tables, and interactive-tool screenshots. This substantially expands the visual documentation. Existing main figures and tables retain their content, with only limited early-page reflow.

R1.justification: The supplement adds the PagedAttention/vLLM serving reference. Its LADDER and FACTS references repeat works already cited in v3. The main related-work discussion, novelty positioning and reference list are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section S3.5 newly formalizes the repair group attribute, weighted detection-head and total losses, and exponential group-weight updates, where v3 describes the weighting verbally. The core matching and trend definitions remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: v3 repeatedly references supplementary prompts, implementation details and segmentation results that its supplied PDF does not contain. v4 resolves this important documentation gap, making the method substantially more reproducible and its segmentation evidence directly assessable. Additional component analyses and dataset-access information strengthen the paper while its main results and scientific claims remain stable.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GH-ESD and GESD, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. v4 retains the main article and adds supplementary Sections S1–S4, which are referenced but absent from the supplied v3.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and supplies additional empirical results, including per-slice segmentation scores and model-selection and matching-score comparisons.

before.justification: v3 reports original slice-discovery experiments, component ablations and model-repair outcomes in Section 5, including Tables 1–4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the core contributions: an entity-centric narrative benchmark, CRP and an automated annotation pipeline. Claims about temporal-perceptual trade-offs, directional bias and limitations of scaling also remain. The revised title and additional evidence do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits applicability to human entities, explains why non-human tracking could confound evaluation, and identifies broader entity coverage as future work. Appendix 9.5 adds interpretations favoring generation-based evaluation and notes that likelihood evaluation is limited to open-source models.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page pointer, the 406-clip count, exact counts by reasoning dimension, more explicit QA-validity and correction criteria, and attribution of the failure examples to Video-LLaMA2-7B. OSNet and detector thresholds were already documented in v1's appendix. The PDFs do not establish that the expanded construction description reflects a newly rebuilt benchmark.

E1.justification: Both versions use AVA, Video-MME and LVBench sources for the same 1,006-question benchmark and retain the same reasoning dimensions and scenarios. V2's explicit human-only scope and newly reported 406-clip count clarify existing coverage; they do not establish a changed population or task.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LLaVA-Video-7B while retaining the distinct LLaVA-NeXT-Video models. Section 3.1 adds an OWLv2-only detection comparator alongside Detectron2 and the ensemble. GPT-4o's additional frame configuration changes settings rather than comparator identity.

E3.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o evaluation at 20 frames, matching the open-source models' frame budget while retaining its 128-frame evaluation. Appendix 9.5 introduces likelihood-based evaluation, and Section 3.3 reports an additional three-annotator assessment after cleaning. The original benchmark protocols remain represented.

E4.justification: New analyses examine answer-selection sensitivity through likelihood-based evaluation, GPT-4o performance under a matched frame budget, and cleaned-benchmark reliability through human assessment. The OWLv2-only result extends the detector-ensemble ablation. Existing temporal-direction, distractor, frame-density and reversed-video analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The 100-item, three-annotator audit, Fleiss' kappa of 0.767 and existing plotted uncertainty displays are retained. The new human and likelihood-based accuracies are point estimates; no new seed information, repeated-run protocol, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: All retained numerical rows in Tables 2 and 9 match. New Table 2 averages are 34.39% for LLaVA-Video-7B and 70.97% for GPT-4o at 20 frames; its 128-frame result remains 72.27%. V2 also adds OWLv2 recall of 0.801, post-cleaning mean human accuracy of 96%, and Table 10 likelihood-based averages of 46.82% and 37.97%. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

M1.justification: Appendix 9.5 adds an optional answer-selection procedure that scores candidates by normalized conditional likelihood and selects the highest-scoring answer. The entity-extraction pipeline, CRP dimensions and underlying model architectures remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially revises the abstract, introduction and benchmark-construction exposition. Section 3.3 develops separate discussions of QA formats, distractors and quality review, while appendix templates receive systematic language corrections. The paper is retitled and replaces video-specific terminology with video-specialized terminology throughout much of the prose.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column format, extensively resizing and relocating displays and restyling appendix prompt boxes. V2 redraws Figure 3's distribution chart, adds the QA-construction illustration in Figure 4 and likelihood results in Table 10, and expands Table 2. Most existing experimental plots are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds VELOCITI and a focused comparison contrasting its localized agent-action entailment with cross-scene entity continuity. The added likelihood evaluator explicitly draws on StrictVLE from that work. The remaining cited works are retained despite bibliography reformatting and renumbering.

T1.justification: Appendix 9.5 newly defines the normalized candidate-likelihood scoring function and its maximum-score selection rule. This is a limited formal addition accompanying the new evaluator. Existing entity-representation, detection-fusion and matching mathematics is unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation credibility by adding a 20-frame GPT-4o control to v1's comparison against 20-frame open-source models. Clearer construction and scope explanations, an additional detector comparator and post-cleaning human validation also help. The new human assessment lacks a stated sample size, and Table 10 uses model labels inconsistent with Table 2, limiting those additions. Overall, the gains are useful but incremental.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NARRATIVETRACK, with matching authors, benchmark, pipeline and core experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite the changed title and layout.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds model evaluations, a post-cleaning human assessment and likelihood-based evaluation results.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, detection and tracking validation, annotation-quality measurements, and temporal-reasoning and frame-density ablations.

token_usage.accounting_note: Input totals include cached input; output totals include reasoning output. These subsets are not added again. C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim that GPT-4o achieves the highest accuracy with Gemini-2.5-Pro as the leader. The abstract and conclusion retain the benchmark's novelty, CRP and pipeline contributions, and temporal-perceptual trade-off claims.

C2.justification: Sections 5 and 11.4 newly argue that the observed trade-off persists beyond basic entity-existence errors and qualify interpretation of model-category comparisons. v3 also expands the human-only scope rationale, motivates top-four selection and explains quality-balanced curation from the larger generated pool.

D1.justification: v3 adds a dataset access link, explicitly describes exact-match scoring and human verification of inferred attributes, and discloses the 3.8k generated QA pool and source-duration breakdown. Existing pipeline thresholds, components and appendix prompts are retained.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 1,006 QA pairs from 406 clips drawn from AVA, Video-MME and LVBench, covering the same reasoning dimensions. The newly disclosed generation-pool size and source breakdown do not establish expanded evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially expands proprietary comparisons beyond GPT-4o by adding Gemini-2.0-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Gemini-3-Flash, Gemini-3.1-Pro and GPT-4.1. All thirteen open-source models already appear in v2; changing their stated count from twelve to thirteen corrects the prose.

E3.justification: Section 11.4 introduces model-specific evaluation subsets selected by correct entity-existence predictions. Section 3.1 adds a 100-video audit with spatial-size and occurrence criteria. Existing open-source 20-frame and GPT-4o 20/128-frame settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds targeted checks of whether errors persist after correct entity-existence predictions (Table 10) and whether the top-four clusters capture salient characters. Existing directional, frame-density, distractor, text-only, reversed-video and likelihood analyses remain.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged, including the three-annotator review and Fleiss' kappa of 0.767. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds detailed results for six models; at 128 frames, Gemini-2.5-Pro leads with 83.80%, while GPT-4o retains 72.27%. All matched v2 Table 2 scores remain unchanged. New Table 10 reports conditioned real/synthetic accuracies of 52.9/58.6 for OGP models versus 41.4/43.7 for OVS models; source-length statistics and salience findings are also added.

M1.justification: The detection, tracking, contextual recognition, top-four entity selection, CRP and QA-generation procedures remain unchanged. The added selection rationale and human-verification description provide support and documentation rather than establish a revised method.

P1.justification: v3 moves qualitative results earlier, creates a separate Analysis section and promotes the appendix video-source discussion to its own section. Short explanatory additions, terminology corrections and updated cross-references accompany otherwise largely retained prose.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains six model rows, updated highlighting and a frame-setting caption; Tables 3 and 10 are added. Existing figures and template tables are retained and reflowed, including relocation of the failure examples from Figure 9 to Figure 5.

R1.justification: v3 adds distinct LLaVA-NeXT-Video and LLaVA-Video references and removes the LLaVA-OneVision reference previously used for those baselines. Research positioning remains largely unchanged; the expanded Video-MME reference identifies the same work.

T1.justification: The entity-representation definition, detector-fusion and matching equations, recall calculation and likelihood-based scoring formula are unchanged. The added empirical rationale introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

improvement.justification: The expanded proprietary comparisons provide a broader assessment of model capability, while explicit scoring, curation details and the dataset link improve transparency. The new diagnostic analysis adds useful evidence, but Table 10 compares groups on model-specific subsets and its gaps are described as performance drops, limiting the strength of the interpretation. C1.justification: The central fully Mamba-based architecture, retrieval, robustness, and resolution-flexibility claims remain. v2 adds scaling as an explicit abstract, introduction, and conclusion contribution, strengthening the assertion that architectural advantages should persist beyond the tested training regime.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for Mamba-1 versus Mamba-2 performance and Hydra's results, acknowledges NaFlex's DOCCI text-retrieval and image-geometry strengths, and discusses potential Transformer advantages for low resolution and visual-style shifts. It also removes v1's explicit large-scale verification limitation and strengthens architectural-versus-data-scale interpretations despite retaining the original scaling evidence.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public code-and-model availability statement with repository access information. Section 4.4 newly clarifies that every comparator processes complete captions and states the LLaMA baseline's 8K context. The dense-caption image resolutions were already disclosed in v1's appendix; their main-text appearance is relocation.

E1.justification: The explicitly identified evaluation datasets and tasks are retained. v2 additionally reports a ResNet comparison on 38 OpenCLIP benchmarks, but does not identify those benchmarks in the supplied material. The increased count alone cannot establish which data populations or task requirements were added.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens comparisons: Table 1 adds MetaCLIP-ViT-B/16; Table 10 adds RoPE-ViT with Qwen2-1.5B and VMamba with bidirectional Hydra; Section 4.1 reports comparisons against convolutional ResNet-based CLIP models. Exact ResNet variants are deferred to unavailable supplementary material.

E3.justification: The added MetaCLIP comparator uses vision weights pretrained on MetaCLIP-400M, introducing a different pretraining condition. The text-encoder ablation adds model configurations including Qwen2-1.5B. Existing CC12M training budgets, optimization settings, resolutions, and metrics remain unchanged; the full-caption clarification does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 10 extends v1 Table 8 with Qwen2 and Hydra, expanding the text-backbone ablation to another Transformer LLM and a bidirectional SSM. Existing spatial-shuffling, geometry, scaling, and qualitative analyses are retained across relocation. The new discussion of architectural failure conditions does not document additional robustness tests.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both present point estimates and plots without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds MetaCLIP scores of 25.7/56.9 Acc@1/5 and 66.4/76.2 IR/TR@5, Qwen2 and Hydra result rows, and a reported greater-than-four-point average advantage over ResNets. MetaCLIP's image recall exceeds CLIMP's 65.5 under different pretraining. Extensive per-dataset results from v1 Appendix Tables 9-10 are absent from the supplied v2, while matched retained numerical tables remain unchanged.

M1.justification: The proposed VMamba vision encoder, Mamba-1/Mamba-2 text encoders, last-token pooling, learned projections, and contrastive dual-encoder architecture remain unchanged. Additional encoders appear as experimental comparators, not revisions to CLIMP.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises the abstract, contribution list, and experimental discussion, integrates much of Appendix A into the main narrative, and replaces numbered analysis subsections with run-in headings. The separate Limitations section disappears, an Acknowledgments section is added, and citations change from author-year to numerical style.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout with widespread resizing and relocation. v1 Appendix Tables 11-14 become v2 Tables 4-7, and v1 Figures 2 and 5 merge into v2 Figure 2. Summary displays are replaced by existing detailed tables, comparator rows are added, and v1 Tables 9-10 and Figure 6 are absent.

R1.justification: v2 adds explicit positioning against LLM2CLIP and UniViTAR, clarifies its distinction from hybrid CLIP-Mamba architectures, and adds discussion and citations concerning SSM length extrapolation, caption adaptation, and interpretability. These extend the context while preserving the central fully SSM-based novelty claim.

T1.justification: The continuous and discrete SSM equations, last-token pooling definition, and scalar-transition decay argument are retained. Added intuitive explanations and discussion of Mamba variants introduce no new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

improvement.justification: Added comparators, clearer full-caption evaluation, code-access information, and the corrected qualification of DOCCI performance improve transparency. However, detailed benchmark breakdowns are unavailable in v2, and stronger scaling claims replace an explicit limitation. Section 4.5 claims an advantage across all data sizes although the retained Figure 4 shows RoPE-ViT ahead at 1M and 3M. These benefits and losses, together with the missing referenced supplement, prevent a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe CLIMP, and their supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. Much of v1 Appendix A can be matched to v2's main text. However, v2 references supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF, limiting comparison of detailed benchmark results and its new ResNet evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains original CLIMP experiments and adds reported MetaCLIP, Qwen2, Hydra, and ResNet comparisons.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, retrieval, robustness, resolution-scaling, embedding-geometry, and ablation results, including detailed results in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The central claim that internal guidance can match or surpass externally guided REPA is retained. v2 expands the abstract's demonstrated scope to both class-to-image and text-to-image generation; v1 treated text-to-image applicability as future work.

C2.justification: v2 adds a task-dependent hyperparameter-tuning limitation and interprets the one-stage variant's weakness as unreliable early EMA guidance. Its applicability boundary becomes image generation generally. The new claim of smaller memory overhead than REPA needs qualification: Table 5 reports a higher initial peak, 12.34 versus 10.39 GB, followed by lower memory after early stopping.

D1.justification: Section 7 newly specifies three linear MLP layers with two SiLU activations, documenting the existing alignment component. v2 also discloses peak memory requirements. Conversely, the explicit 512×512 preprocessing description using 64×64×4 Stable Diffusion VAE latents is replaced by a reference to REPA's pipeline. The code-access link is unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual text-to-image generation with MMDiT in Section 10/Table 8, extending evaluation beyond class-conditioned generation. Figure 8 identifies MS-COCO for the qualitative examples, although the training dataset is not named locally. ImageNet 256×256 and 512×512 coverage is retained; the latter moves to the supplement.

E2.justification: v2 adds vanilla MMDiT as a comparator in the text-to-image experiment and an EMA-based one-stage variant in Table 6. The existing ImageNet comparator sets remain unchanged; REPA also participates in the new text-to-image comparison.

E3.justification: The training-cost comparison changes its stated budget from 200 epochs/1 million iterations to 400 epochs/2 million iterations and adds peak GPU memory as a measurement. New experiments specify 150,000 iterations for MMDiT and an 80-epoch, 50,000-sample one-stage comparison. These are reported setting additions or revisions, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 6/Table 6 adds a focused test of two-stage training against joint training with an updated EMA teacher. Figure 2 revises the proposed method's feature-separability visualization and scores. Existing component, hyperparameter, early-stopping, and layerwise feature analyses are largely retained, with several relocated to the supplement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The same-seed control for qualitative training comparisons is retained. Changed logistic-regression accuracies in Figure 2 are result changes, not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports text-to-image FIDs of 6.23, 4.90, and 4.56 for MMDiT, REPA, and Self-Transcendence at 150,000 iterations. Table 6 adds one-stage FID 34.50 versus two-stage 20.49. Figure 2 changes Self-Transcendence FID from 22.30 to 20.49 and classification accuracy from 0.9804 to 0.9961, crossing REPA's unchanged 0.9882. The 300K-teacher ablation changes from FID/IS 22.91/71.32 to 23.05/70.32, and the loss-weight discussion corrects 23.91 to 22.91. Cost results use a longer budget and add memory values. Main ImageNet comparison tables retain their scores.

M1.justification: The narrative retains VAE warm-up, a frozen guiding model, feature-level classifier-free guidance, and early stopping; VAE Structure Guidance renames VAE-based alignment. However, v2's Eq. (3) drops parentheses that materially change the guidance rule. The PDFs do not establish whether this is an intended procedure change or a typesetting error.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the title, abstract, introduction, and explanatory passages, emphasizing structurally clean and semantically discriminative guidance. It renames the first stage and reorganizes early stopping, high-resolution experiments, and feature visualization into an explicitly introduced supplementary section.

P2.justification: The two-column design becomes predominantly single-column with wrapped tables and a redesigned title/abstract. Figure 1 swaps panel groups, Figure 2 changes from a grid to a horizontal arrangement, and Figure 3 merges the framework with the former Figure 4 learning curve. New cost, one-stage, and text-to-image tables and a text-to-image figure accompany extensive relocation of retained displays.

R1.justification: v2 adds Singh et al., 'What Matters for Representation Alignment: Global Information or Spatial Structure?' as reference 37 and connects it to the structural-guidance motivation. The established positioning against external guidance and existing self-contained methods remains substantially unchanged.

T1.justification: The printed definition in Eq. (3) changes from f_u + omega*(f_c - f_u) to f_u + omega*f_c - f_u, which simplifies to omega*f_c. This is mathematically inequivalent, although its intent is unresolved. Other equation edits are equivalent notation changes; neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence for text-to-image applicability and the two-stage design, plus MLP and memory disclosures. However, Eq. (3) introduces an unresolved ambiguity in the central method specification. The revised cost comparison also reports 58.87 hours where its stated speed and budget imply 59.87, and its broad memory advantage needs qualification. These gains in validation coexist with regressions in mathematical accuracy and resource interpretation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Self-Transcendence, with matching authors, the same central training framework, and corresponding ImageNet experiments despite the changed title. All supplied pages, including v2's supplementary sections, are readable and support comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains original ImageNet experiments and adds text-to-image results, a one-stage training comparison, and GPU-memory measurements.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation results, component and hyperparameter ablations, feature analyses, and training-time measurements.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: self-contained two-stage guidance and competitive or superior generation and convergence relative to REPA. The added probing evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly acknowledges generally lower linear separability than REPA despite stronger generation results, attributing this to better alignment between teacher and student diffusion settings. Existing limitations concerning model capacity, hyperparameter tuning, and untested generative modalities remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link and advertises models alongside code, whereas v2 advertises source code only. Existing MLP architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time disclosures are retained.

E1.justification: v3 adds explicit ImageNet linear probing, but v2 Figure 2 already reports logistic-regression accuracies. The classification datasets and class sets are insufficiently specified to establish whether this expands coverage or only extends the probing protocol. ImageNet generation and text-to-image coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched generation, ablation, and supplementary comparisons. The added linear probe reuses vanilla SiT-XL/2 and REPA, already jointly compared with Self-Transcendence, without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 adds linear probing at t = 0.5 using features from layers 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, and 24. Existing generation settings, evaluation sample counts, training budgets, and early-stopping procedures remain unchanged. Probe training and data-split details are not supplied.

E4.justification: The new layer-wise probe quantitatively examines discriminative representations across model depth, complementing the existing t-SNE, logistic-regression, and PCA evidence. Earlier component ablations, hyperparameter studies, one-stage comparisons, and early-stopping analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new Table 7 provides point scores without additional run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing statistical-reporting practices and same-seed qualitative comparisons are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds classification scores across six layers. At layer 12, vanilla SiT, REPA, and Self-Transcendence score 16.25%, 52.07%, and 49.13%, respectively; at layer 16, Self-Transcendence slightly exceeds REPA, 50.00% versus 49.76%. Matched generation, ablation, and cost results are unchanged.

M1.justification: Equation 3 corrects the written guidance calculation from fg = fu + ω·fc − fu to fg = fu + ω·(fc − fu). This revises the mathematical specification of a core component, while the two-stage pipeline remains unchanged. It appears to repair the already-described CFG operation; an implementation change is not established.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. v3 moves the text-to-image experiment into Section 4.2, reorganizes supplementary sections as Appendices A–E after the references, and adds Section 4.5. Other edits include author-contribution information, keywords, and limited wording corrections.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns the document throughout with institutional headers and footers, different typography, margins, heading styles, and front matter. Retained figures and tables are extensively resized and repositioned, including moving text-to-image displays into the main text. Table 7 is new; the original scientific figure images are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to REPA, SRA, LayerSync, and other prior methods are retained. Reference reordering and bibliographic formatting corrections do not introduce new research positioning.

T1.justification: Equation 3 receives a mathematically substantive grouping correction: v2's expression cancels the unconditional feature, whereas v3 scales the conditional–unconditional difference, consistent with Equation 2. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is added.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation 3 resolves an inconsistency in the reproducible method specification. The added layer-wise probe provides useful evidence about representation quality and qualifies its relationship to generation performance, while retaining earlier results. The improvement is limited because the probing protocol remains underspecified and the proposed mechanism is not directly tested.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Self-Transcendence work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary sections are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds layer-wise ImageNet linear-probing results in Section 4.5 and Table 7.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation results, ablations, training-cost measurements, and supplementary ImageNet 512×512 and text-to-image experiments.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about reference-based temporal effect transfer, the large training dataset, joint conditioning, unseen-effect generalization, and superiority over baselines. The introduction clarifies the framework's components without changing these claims.

C2.justification: V4 newly interprets its bootstrap deviations as confirming statistical reliability and discusses the near-chance input-adherence result against No Ref. This reliability interpretation is stronger than near-chance entries warrant. The under-editing explanation and Appendix A limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix C documents MTurk recruitment, randomized presentation, 30 distinct annotators per experiment, five practice trials, and the study interface. V4 also specifies Wan2.1 in the main implementation description and changes the project-page link target. Existing training, inference, hardware, and runtime details are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LoRA-derived I2V, neural V2V, and programmatic V2V coverage. Section 4.1 retains 28 unseen LoRA effects, 56 reference videos, and the existing V2V scenarios. V4 clarifies their organization and use of real input videos without establishing newly added coverage.

E2.justification: V4 adds Lucy Edit to the code-based V2V human-preference and similarity comparisons in Tables 1 and 4, where v1 has dashes. The comparator sets in the other corresponding comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The primary human evaluation changes from five-level ratings to two-alternative forced choice and adds Overall Match alongside the existing adherence criteria. V1 reports 669, 455, and 252 annotations across its three tasks; v4 reports over 15,000 annotations from over 500 annotators. Training and automatic evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 1–2 extend the existing No Ref ablation to Overall Match, adding evidence about reference conditioning's contribution to jointly transferring effects and preserving input content. The guidance sensitivity example in Figure 8 and failure analysis in Figure 9 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: V1 reports win rates and mean preference scores without uncertainty estimates. V4 reports bootstrap standard deviations throughout Tables 1–2; Appendix C specifies 10,000 iterations resampling annotators and trials. This adds uncertainty estimation to the primary evaluation, without establishing additional model-training runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace the human-study results and add Overall Match scores. For example, I2V preference against Wan2.1 changes from 74.7% to 57.1 ± 2.4% under the revised procedure, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Table 4 adds Lucy Edit's code-based input/reference similarities of 0.8882/0.6539. Tables 3 and 10 remain unchanged.

M1.justification: The data-generation pipelines, reference-latent concatenation, conditioning masks, training procedure, and inference guidance remain unchanged. References to an 'updated conditioning' scheme describe the architecture already documented in v1, rather than a new procedure.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized revisions to the introduction, method overview, dataset terminology, validation description, and user-study discussion. It inserts a user-study appendix, renumbers the subsequent appendix sections, and adds acknowledgments while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain Overall Match columns and revised captions, and Figure 10 newly illustrates the study interface. V4 also changes a Figure 3 transition label, identifies Table 5 as a subset, and relocates Table 4. Existing qualitative and architecture illustrations are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion remain unchanged. The positioning against text-driven editing, static reference conditioning, and effect-specific finetuning is retained; reference back-reference changes reflect pagination.

T1.justification: The triplet construction definitions, guidance equations (1)–(5), and supplementary motion-quality expression (6) are retained. No mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations are added or revised.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens the paper's primary empirical validation. It replaces a sparsely documented preference study without uncertainty reporting with a larger, explicitly specified study, adds joint assessment of effect transfer and content preservation, and reports annotator/trial bootstrap uncertainty (Section 4.3 and Appendix C). These changes address important weaknesses in assessing and reproducing the central evidence. The blanket reliability claim remains overstated for near-chance results such as 51.3 ± 3.1%, but the evaluation is materially more transparent and informative.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RefVFX research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including the expanded user study in v4.

after.justification: V4 retains original generation and quantitative results and reports a revised human study, including Overall Match judgments and bootstrap uncertainty.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation comparisons, human preference results in Tables 1–2, similarity measurements in Tables 3–4, and supplementary video-quality measurements in Table 10.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: individualized asymmetric candidate selection, efficient global dependency modeling, and state-of-the-art SR performance under comparable computational budgets. Updated numerical margins and supporting analyses do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 more explicitly attributes the main gains to propagation and sparsification's main benefit to computational savings. It adds explanations linking late SF-FFN placement to more reliable similarities and additional fused neighbors to redundancy. Appendix G newly acknowledges higher memory use than ATD/IPG and explains the lower usage relative to PFT.

D1.justification: v2 revises the documented neighbor-count schedule, adds tensor dimensions to architecture diagrams, and documents preferred SF-FFN placement in the final two blocks through ablations. These additions do not establish a previously different SF-FFN implementation. Appendix training recipes, GPU information, and the code-link target were already present and remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Coverage remains DF2K training for IET, DIV2K training for IET-light and ablations, and evaluation on Set5, Set14, BSD100, Urban100, and Manga109 for classical and lightweight SR at ×2, ×3, and ×4. The added analyses do not establish a new task or data domain.

E2.justification: The external benchmark comparators and the appendix's ATD, IPG, and PFT runtime comparators are unchanged. However, Table 1 revises the internal comparison variants: DLSG-centered combinations are replaced by propagation/sparsification/SF-FFN combinations, including sparsification-only and explicitly SF-FFN-disabled controls.

E3.justification: v2 describes Table 1's baseline as fixed dilated attention, whereas v1 specifies local attention with d=1. It adds neighbor-ratio and SF-FFN configuration sweeps, extends the depth sweep to one step, removes the inference-dilation-5 case, and adds memory as an evaluation measure. These are reported protocol changes within retained tasks; the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 substantially expands component validation: Table 1 is redesigned, depth ablations gain FLOPs and an additional setting, and new Tables 4–6 test k1/k2 ratios, SF-FFN placement, and fused-neighbor counts. New Figure 2 examines global-attention neighbor overlap. These additions investigate previously untested design choices, especially SF-FFN, while most existing visual analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial ablation and memory results and replaces several component/depth entries. Benchmark updates are small: classical ×2 Urban100 PSNR changes from 35.07 to 35.09, Manga109 from 40.61 to 40.60, and lightweight ×2 Urban100 from 34.00 to 34.03. These are revised reported results, not established same-configuration gains. Appendix runtimes remain unchanged, while Table 9 adds memory values but retains older ×2 IET PSNR values inconsistent with Table 7.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the second-hop neighbor-selection schedule k2 from [12, 11, 9, 8] to [12, 10, 7, 6], altering the propagation budget. The core attention procedure, SF-FFN, losses, and model architecture remain unchanged; renaming expansion as propagation does not constitute another method change.

P1.justification: v2 renames expansion as propagation, replaces DLSG terminology with dilation-based initialization, rewrites parts of the motivation and ablation discussion, adds related-work subheadings, reorders the depth/dilation discussion, and condenses the conclusion. Much of the abstract, introduction, method description, and supplementary training text remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively converted from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 gains attention-matrix illustrations, the former initialization Figure 2 is replaced by a similarity analysis, Figure 3 is redrawn, and Figures 4–5 gain dimensional annotations. Ablation tables are added and restructured, and the appendix runtime table gains memory and PSNR columns. Existing reconstruction images are retained and resized.

R1.justification: The same 48 referenced works are retained after matching renumbered entries. A new sparse-attention paragraph explicitly contrasts IEA with spatial-window SwinIR, dilated-window ART, hash-based NLSA, and clustering-based ATD, providing a limited expansion of research positioning.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly states the asymptotic attention-cost comparison O(N²) versus O(kN). This is a limited addition to mathematical cost characterization; Equations (1)–(8), the candidate-selection definitions, and the expander-graph initialization argument remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

improvement.justification: The added SF-FFN and propagation ablations, FLOPs comparisons, and memory measurements make design choices and efficiency tradeoffs better supported than in v1. The gain is limited by unresolved experimental-setting ambiguities and a new reporting inconsistency: v2 Table 9 retains ×2 IET PSNR values of 35.07/40.61 while Table 7 reports 35.09/40.60. Overall, the additional diagnostic evidence improves the paper modestly despite these shortcomings.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IET super-resolution work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections F–H are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and reports additional ablations, token-similarity observations, and memory measurements.

before.justification: v1 reports original IET and IET-light reconstruction results, component and parameter ablations, attention visualizations, and inference-time measurements.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the Perception Gap claim, attention-guided latent distillation contribution, curriculum-gating contribution, and claims of up to 16.9-point gains and competitiveness with larger models. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions attribute faster text decoding to reduced KV-cache burden, interpret SFT scaling behavior as overfitting, and explain weak low-data LaViT performance through limited generalization. They also relate filtering acceptance differences to alignment difficulty. Figure 2's caption modestly softens its necessity interpretation, although stronger causal language remains elsewhere.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information: the GPT-4o snapshot, VLMEvalKit, timing hardware and software, MiMo-V2-Flash correctness judge and prompt, Gemini-2.5-Flash difficulty filter, and stepwise bounding-box filtering pseudocode. It replaces the earlier GitHub access pointer with an anonymous repository and explicitly reports code, model, and dataset releases. These are newly documented details and access information, not evidence that the original experiments changed.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix B.2 adds Jigsaw evaluation to the previously tested perception and spatial-reasoning tasks. The original benchmarks and the 14,567-example training corpus with ten source datasets remain; the new training-subset sizes do not introduce additional domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator roster. The added timing and scaling analyses reuse existing methods, including the base model, SFT, LVR, and DMLR. Implementing LVR at 3B for timing is a model-configuration difference, not a new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: The original main training settings remain. New supplementary protocols vary training data from 3K to 15K while fixing total iterations, and measure batch-one latency on all 300 MMVP samples with 3B LVR and DMLR implementations. Figure 2 also extends the reported focusing-threshold sweep from 20% to 30%.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands supporting analyses through controlled data-scaling experiments, a breakdown of inference costs, and analysis of source-dependent filtering acceptance. These examine data dependence, computational overhead, and selection effects absent from v1. Existing component and latent-token/checkpoint ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 adds box-and-whisker summaries of focusing scores for correct and incorrect samples, replacing the earlier count/mean display and adding descriptive spread information. Figure 3 retains error-bar reporting and Table 2 retains standard deviations and coefficients of variation. No repeated-run protocol or defined confidence intervals are added.

E6.justification: V2 adds data-scaling curves, latency measurements, and filtering outcomes. Table 5 reports total latency of 0.143 seconds for LaViT, 0.215 for LVR, and 1.177 for DMLR; Table 9 reports 30,500 candidates and 47.8% acceptance. Section 3.1 corrects its prose means from 15.89%/11.84% to 18.78%/9.18%, matching values already plotted in v1 Figure 2, while the revised figure adds higher-threshold results. Main Tables 1–3 and the existing token-count ablation values are unchanged.

M1.justification: The latent-token procedure, semantic and trajectory losses, curriculum gating, and joint objective are retained. Top-K sparsification becomes Top-N with the same value of eight. Final-token-only supervision, newly emphasized in the main text, was already documented in v1 Appendix C.2; expanded filtering details do not establish a changed procedure.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained. Local revisions clarify the SFT control and attention extraction, distinguish Top-N sparsification from K latent tokens, and move ablation definitions from a caption into prose. Appendix headings expand and references move after the appendices.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figures 2 and 3 are redrawn, Tables 2 and 3 become adjacent, and new displays include the latency table, scaling figure, filtering algorithm, and filtering-statistics table. V1 Tables A1–A4 are retained as v2 Tables 4 and 6–8, rather than newly added evidence.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including ClueAegis, REVEAL, Driver-WM, MonoSR, VLMEvalKit, and MiMo-V2-Flash. These are limited additions to contextual and implementation references; the central positioning around dynamic attention-guided latent reasoning remains unchanged.

Equation 2 expands notation and explanation; the new filtering pseudocode documents an existing operation. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility and assessability through fuller filtering/evaluation documentation, useful data-scaling and latency checks, and correction of the Section 3.1 text/figure inconsistency. Main benchmark and component-ablation results remain unchanged. P1.justification: Beyond renaming INSIGHT to CFM, v2 substantially rewrites the introduction, contribution list, method exposition, and experimental narrative. Separate backbone and SAE subsections become a unified discussion of spatially localized representations, and downstream experiments are grouped under Foundation Model Applications. The appendices are reorganized and expanded with dedicated evaluation and analysis sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting and substantially reorganizes displays. V1's concept-quality table and human-study plot are combined in v2 Fig. 3; classification results and explanations are combined in Fig. 6. V2 adds naming comparisons, ablation tables, a C2-Score distribution plot, and pixel-level examples, and redraws captioning and concept-vector illustrations. Many existing appendix examples are retained with new placement.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations supporting VLM sparse autoencoders, LLaVA/Gemma-2, DreamLIP, AnyUp, polysemanticity evaluation, and captioning metrics. It removes v1's explicit attribution to Ye et al. as inspiration for feature-family discovery and emphasizes foundation-model positioning. The main related-work categories and most comparisons with prior approaches remain similar.

T1.justification: The written hierarchy-confidence definition changes substantively: after matching parent/child indices, v1 Eq. (5) weights co-occurrence by the conditioned child's activation, whereas v2 Eq. (2) uses parent activation in the numerator and child activation in the denominator. This is not equivalent notation and does not guarantee the asserted [0,1] range. V2 also describes the graph as typically a DAG. No new theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: The new dictionary/sparsity ablations and independent concept-quality checks address validation gaps in v1, while the judge prompt and detailed caption-training recipe improve reproducibility. These support a modest net quality gain. Benefits are tempered by claims covering all downstream tasks despite limited demonstrated coverage, and by the revised hierarchy-confidence formula, which no longer guarantees its stated probability range. The changed captioning and segmentation results also do not establish improvements under unchanged conditions.

A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from INSIGHT to CFM. Their core architecture, experiments, and appendix examples can be matched despite substantial rewriting and reformatting. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of both complete documents.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds automated naming evaluation, dictionary and sparsity ablations, polysemanticity measurements, and revised downstream experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original concept-quality measurements, human-study outcomes, classification and segmentation experiments, and captioning results in Sections 4 and Appendices A–C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: spatially grounded hierarchical concepts, improved naming, and interpretable foundation-model applications beyond classification with competitive downstream performance. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The added analyses explain guided pooling's importance, sparsity/locality/consistency tradeoffs, and applicability to a larger backbone. Figure C7 adds specific naming-failure interpretations, including lexical gaps and spurious correlations. Section C.8 qualifies steering effectiveness through category-dependent failures. The main conclusion and existing limitations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the relationship judge's full prompt, composite-image construction and filtering details, identifies the SigLIP-2 variant, and explicitly documents ImageNet-only SAE training for Appendix B.8. It also adds an interactive-visualization address. Existing core training hyperparameters and captioning hardware/time disclosures are retained.

E1.justification: The datasets, domains, and underlying classification, segmentation, concept-assessment, and caption-steering tasks are retained. SigLIP-2 changes the model configuration; the systematic COCO steering and hierarchy-direction evaluations add protocols and analyses within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure C15 introduces a CLIP target-word steering baseline against CFM's concept steering; v2 supplied qualitative steering examples without this comparison. The comparator sets in the retained main classification, concept-quality, captioning, and segmentation experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include judging 1,000 hierarchy pairs using top-five examples and consistency/directionality filtering, and testing caption deletion with 80 samples per COCO category using text matching and an LLM judge. Appendix B.8 adds a 400M-parameter SigLIP-2 configuration and controlled ImageNet-trained architecture variants. These are added experimental settings, not demonstrated reruns of the retained headline experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's dictionary-size and reconstruction/sparsity analyses, v3 tests guided-pooling removal, alternative SAE objectives, sparsity effects on downstream performance and interpretability, and backbone scaling. It also adds hierarchy-direction validation and quantitative category-wise steering analysis. Table 2 extends the existing dictionary-size analysis with C2 scores.

E5.justification: The new relationship-judge prompt requests a confidence rating from 1 to 5, and Figure A6 displays an example rating. This adds limited per-judgment confidence reporting, rather than statistical uncertainty for aggregate accuracy. The existing Wilcoxon test is retained; no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Figure 3 changes CFM's C2 score from 0.405 to 0.465, and Figure C9 changes the plotted distributions. New results include 86.2% ImageNet accuracy for CFM with SigLIP-2, hierarchy-direction accuracy of 300/376 filtered pairs, and steering deletion rates of 25.9% versus 21.3% by LLM judging and 28.2% versus 23.2% by text matching. The per-dataset 4k/16k segmentation results from v2 Table B1 are omitted when condensed into v3 Table 2.

M1.justification: The core CFM pipeline is retained, but the stated naming procedure changes in Eq. (B.8): alpha now scales the combined child and parent vectors, whereas v2 applied it only to the child vector. The accompanying explanation changes accordingly. This establishes a limited procedural revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 4.3 and Appendix A.3, expands B.8 and C.8, and makes localized grammar, terminology, caption, and cross-reference corrections. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation expands substantially: v2 Tables B1/B2 are condensed into main-text Table 2, new backbone and architecture tables are added, and new figures present the relationship-judge prompt/example and quantitative steering. Figure C9 is enlarged and redrawn with mean markers. Existing qualitative examples are retained, including the steering figure renumbered C16.

R1.justification: The same 86 reference entries and substantive research positioning are retained. Corrections to existing CLIP-DINOiser and COCO-Object citations do not introduce new cited works or redefine the relationship to prior research.

T1.justification: Equation (2) changes the numerator's activation weight from A_ip to A_jp, making it consistent with the stated conditional-probability definition. Equations (3) and (4) replace argmin with argmax, matching the maximum-similarity rule; Eq. (3) also removes the bias from the prior-method expression. These are substantive mathematical corrections, without new theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: v3 materially strengthens validation of the central design and steering claims. Controlled architecture ablations address questions left open by v2's narrower analyses, and quantitative steering supplies a baseline comparison beyond selected examples. Mathematical corrections also improve internal consistency. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed dictionary-size segmentation scores and the new steering text's reversal of the solid/hatched legend mapping. The hierarchy-direction result remains conditional on 376 of 1,000 sampled pairs, limiting its generality.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CFM research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

after.justification: v3 reports original human-study and downstream-task results, together with architecture ablations, backbone-scaling experiments, hierarchy-direction evaluation, and quantitative caption steering.

before.justification: v2 reports original concept-quality measurements, a human study, classification, captioning, segmentation, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: motion-centric reconstruction supervision, self-regularization and alignment, REG-based error mitigation, and state-of-the-art motion generation. The headline HumanML3D claim remains FID 0.032 and R-Precision@1 56.1% with 20 inference steps.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new diagnostics as evidence of motion-structure preservation, component complementarity, and error-adaptive REG correction. Its conclusion replaces v1’s high-quality-capture-data caveat and proposed noisy-data evaluation with a single-token conditioning limitation and plans for finer-grained, long-horizon generation.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a project URL for the promised code release, without establishing that code is available. v1’s Data Availability section and direct dataset links are removed. Appendix D expands the description of existing comparison controls; it does not establish changed training settings.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-motion generation on HumanML3D and KIT-ML and retain the same user-study coverage. The added diagnostics reuse existing coverage. No noisy-data or targeted long-horizon evaluation is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds MotionDiffuse, MotionLCM v2, and COME to the HumanML3D comparison. The original MotionLCM remains separately listed, so its v2 counterpart is an addition rather than a rename. KIT-ML, user-study, and existing latent-strategy comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce joint t-SNE and paired-cosine measurements, leave-one-out controls, per-step timing at batch size 32, and a REG correction probe with B=128 and a step-5 scatter plot. Existing training budgets, sampling schedules, benchmark metrics, batch-1 AITS measurement, and user-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D–F substantially extend mechanism analysis: Figure 5 examines text/motion latent geometry, Table 10 tests component complementarity by removing components from full RAM, and Figure 6 examines sample-dependent REG corrections and correction magnitudes across steps. Appendix B also adds per-step overhead analysis. Earlier ablations and sensitivity studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly reports a median Pearson correlation, and Figure 6(b) introduces shaded bands. The median’s aggregation and the bands’ statistical meaning are unspecified. Existing tables retain their ± reporting; neither version supplies explicit repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the original nine tables are retained. Added results include three baselines’ scores, paired cosine similarities of 0.157/0.493/0.579, leave-one-out FIDs of 0.424/0.064/0.132, REG correlation approximately 0.62, and baseline/CFG/REG/combined timing ratios of 1:1.95:2.18:3.13. These extend supporting results without changing RAM’s reported benchmark performance.

M1.justification: The two-stream architecture, encoders, diffusion decoder, four training objectives, gradient control, and combined REG/CFG inference procedure remain unchanged. Reformatted equations and expanded explanations do not introduce a new method component.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: the user study, inference-efficiency discussion, hyperparameter analysis, and latent-strategy implementation details move into Appendices A–D. The main text gains shorter summaries and cross-references. Related work and the conclusion are edited, Data Availability is removed, and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: v2 changes page format, typography, running headers, and table-caption placement throughout. Existing displays are relocated and renumbered, Table 1 gains comparator rows, and Figures 5–6 and Table 10 are added. The qualitative motion examples and user-study chart are retained rather than replaced.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to MotionLCM v2, COME, EasyTune, FrankenMotion, and ReAlign. It removes the structured-control discussion with four associated works and four video-reconstruction/data references tied to the old conclusion. The central positioning against two-stream, VQ-VAE, and diffusion-guidance approaches remains unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and guidance equations are equivalent across versions; some equation lines are combined and renumbered. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the new empirical diagnostics introduce no substantive mathematical derivation.

improvement.justification: The stronger comparator coverage in Table 1 and new latent-space, component, REG, and timing analyses provide additional support and cost transparency for the unchanged method. The gain is limited: the REG analysis uses an error proxy, its statistical reporting is incompletely specified, and v2 removes direct dataset links and the earlier noisy-data qualification. Overall, the added evidence modestly strengthens an already extensively evaluated paper.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAM research. All 23 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including Appendices A–F, support comparison. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds latent-space diagnostics, leave-one-out ablations, and measurements of REG’s behavior and computational cost.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAM results on HumanML3D and KIT-ML, component and hyperparameter experiments, inference timings, and a 15-participant user study.

C1.justification: The abstract newly highlights efficiency and a 24% RE10K LPIPS improvement, supported by the PRoPE comparison in v2 Table 1. The core positional-encoding contributions remain unchanged. RGB-D applicability leaves the abstract but remains claimed in the introduction and demonstrated later.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that depth prediction preserves robustness under domain and reference-count shifts. It removes v1's explanation that infinite depth adequately approximates RE10K scenes, instead emphasizing the usefulness of all retained components. Section 6's limitations concerning camera uncertainty and unposed images remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 specifies an Objaverse field-of-view sampling range of 20–80 degrees; v2 retains only general descriptions of random or diverse intrinsics. Basic EscherNet integration details are added. Existing large-LVSM architecture, batch settings, and camera normalization are relocated rather than newly disclosed; access references remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds DL3DV for EscherNet novel-view synthesis and unseen ScanNet for stereo-depth evaluation. It also evaluates CO3D-trained LVSM on Objaverse and RE10K as new cross-domain scenarios. The original datasets and held-out CO3D categories remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 newly compares against original EscherNet using CaPE and an EscherNet+PRoPE variant. CaPE was discussed but not experimentally compared in v1. Comparator membership in the retained LVSM and UniMatch comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate approximately 800M-parameter EscherNet with 3, 6, or 9 reference views and three target views, and test two-reference-trained LVSM with 2, 4, 8, or 16 references. Stereo reporting drops Sq Rel and RMSE log, retaining Abs Rel and RMSE. The 150M-parameter LVSM configuration already existed in v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds zero-shot reference-count and cross-domain robustness analyses, unseen-ScanNet evaluation, and additional layerwise depth visualizations. It removes the single-ray ablation and v1 Figure 6's qualitative ablation comparisons. The runtime, attention-similarity, and radial-versus-compound-pose analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 specifies three-seed averages for standard LVSM experiments and one seed for larger LVSM experiments. Both disclosures disappear in v2 without replacement run-count or averaging information. This establishes reduced statistical reporting, not a change in the number of runs actually performed.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises small-LVSM RayRoPE's RE10K PSNR/LPIPS from 24.42/0.113 to 26.07/0.085. Large-LVSM RE10K PSNR changes from 27.51 to 28.31, reversing its ordering against PRoPE's unchanged 27.77. Ablation scores also change, and new EscherNet, ScanNet, and generalization results appear. Single-ray and two stereo-metric result sets disappear. The PDFs do not explain the causes of the revised RE10K scores.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same ray representation, depth and uncertainty prediction, query-frame projection, expected RoPE, and known-depth substitution. EscherNet is an additional application; no changed RayRoPE procedure is documented.

P1.justification: The abstract and experimental explanations are rewritten and condensed. Known-depth evaluation becomes Section 5.4, while large-LVSM material moves from Appendix E into Section 5.1 and Appendix B. The overall narrative and most introductory, related-work, and method prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the experimental displays: large-LVSM results merge into Table 1, new EscherNet and generalization displays appear, and the known-depth table and emergent-depth figure move. It removes the qualitative ablation figure, adds EscherNet and depth examples, refreshes NVS examples, and explicitly depicts uncertainty inputs in Figure 3.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for ScanNet and DL3DV. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to CaPE, GTA, PRoPE, and concurrent depth-based positional encoding remain substantively unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–11, independence assumption, expected-encoding derivation, and relative-position proof in Appendix A remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new EscherNet/DL3DV, ScanNet, and zero-shot generalization evaluations strengthen evidence for applicability beyond v1's experiments. The benefit is limited by removed seed/averaging disclosures, reduced ablation and metric coverage, and unexplained RE10K revisions. v2 also leaves differing two-reference RE10K results in Table 1 and Figure 10 without clarifying their comparability. Broader validation provides a net improvement, but reporting weaknesses prevent a clear substantial quality gain.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RayRoPE work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds EscherNet, ScanNet, cross-domain, and varying-reference-view evaluations.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis, stereo-depth, ablation, runtime, and generalization results in Section 5 and the appendices.
